_meta.purpose: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A in CatalogFile shape, so applyCatalogFile creates the framework, its 93 requirements, the 93 control templates, their requirement links and the pack together.
_meta.why: The templates were generated inline inside prisma/seed.ts, which is not run on production deploys — so a fresh database or a restore gets none of them. Production has them only because a one-off backfill put them there. This is also the precondition for authoring: the generated templates carried GENERIC_TEMPLATE_TASKS and there was nowhere for authored content to live.
_meta.grounding: Requirement keys, titles, summaries and themes carried over verbatim from prisma/fixtures/iso27001_2022_annexA.json. Task content is authored from each control's own title and its 25-60 character intent paraphrase — the only grounding Annex A carries here. No ISO text is quoted or reproduced. Authored against docs/control-task-authoring.md, whose own worked example is A.8.24, an Annex A control with the same thin grounding. Each task's steps decompose that task's own description into the acts a practitioner ticks off, with no obligation, tool, frequency or figure the description does not carry; like the tasks, they quote and reconstruct no ISO text.
_meta.join: Template A-<key> links to requirement <key>; 93 of 93 resolve by construction.
_meta.packKey: ISO27001_2022_BASE — the key production already has, carrying all 93 templates. seed.ts spells it the same way, so this framework adds no pack-key divergence.

metadata.copyright: Structural outline of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A (control numbers with paraphrased titles), NOT a reproduction of the standard. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 is copyright ISO/IEC; the standard itself must be obtained from ISO or a national member body.

templates.title: Policies for information security
templates.description: Establish and maintain information security policy framework
templates.objective: To ensure that management's direction for information security is set out in an approved body of policy that reaches everyone it binds and is revisited when its assumptions change.
templates.successCriteria:
Every topic on the coverage list is addressed by a named policy, with partial coverage or a gap recorded rather than left unnoticed.
The top-level information security policy carries a management approval identifying its approver and date.
The register names an owner, approver, audience and review trigger for every policy in the set.
Each issued version reached the audience the register names, and every fired review trigger has a recorded outcome and approver.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the topic list showing which policy covers each security topic and what is recorded against the uncovered ones.
Obtain the approved top-level information security policy together with its approval record.
Export the policy register showing owner, version, audience and review trigger per policy.
Collect the issue record for each policy version released during the period.
Gather the review records for the policies whose review trigger fired in the period.

Analysis:
Trace each topic to the policy said to cover it and confirm the claim is borne out by that policy's text.
Confirm the approver of the top-level policy holds authority to approve it and that the approval precedes the issued version.
Search the register for rows missing an owner, an audience or a review trigger.
Compare the audience each issue record actually reached against the audience the register names.
Determine whether every trigger that fired produced an outcome, and whether the resulting changes reached the register.

Output:
A coverage statement naming the topics with no current policy statement behind them.
A register exception list of policies missing ownership, audience or review-trigger data.
A findings note on versions issued to an audience narrower than the register requires.
A list of overdue reviews with the time elapsed since each trigger fired.

title.en: List the security topics that require a policy statement, and which policy covers each

description.en: Work from the organisation's activities, its legal and contractual obligations and the risks it has accepted to derive the topics on which a written position has to exist. Mark each topic as covered by an existing policy, covered only in part, or not covered at all. Attach the topic list showing the covering policy or the gap against every entry.

text.en: List the organisation's activities, its legal and contractual obligations and the risks it has accepted
Derive from that list the security topics on which a written policy position has to exist
Mark each topic as covered by an existing policy, covered only in part, or not covered at all, naming the covering policy
Attach the topic list showing the covering policy, partial coverage or gap against every entry

evidenceHint.en: Topic list with the covering policy, partial coverage or gap recorded against each topic

title.en: Have management approve the top-level information security policy

description.en: Produce a single statement giving the purpose and scope of information security in the organisation, the principles it works to, and the topic policies it governs, and put it to the person or body holding the authority to approve it. Attach the approved document showing who approved it and on what date.

text.en: Draft one statement giving the purpose and scope of information security in the organisation
Add the principles the organisation works to and the topic policies the statement governs
Confirm who holds the authority to approve the top-level policy and submit the statement to them

hint.en: Approval by someone without that authority leaves the policy unapproved

text.en: Attach the approved top-level policy showing who approved it and on what date

evidenceHint.en: The approved top-level policy showing its approver and approval date

title.en: Record the owner, approver, audience and review trigger for every policy in the set

description.en: For each policy on the topic list capture in one register the owner, the approving authority, the current version and its approval date, the audience the policy binds, and what causes it to be reviewed — an elapsed interval, a change of obligation, an incident, or a combination. Attach the register with one row per policy.

text.en: Open one policy register with a row for every policy on the topic list
Record in each row the owner, the approving authority, the current version and its approval date
Name in each row the audience the policy binds
Set each policy's review trigger: an elapsed interval, a change of obligation, an incident, or a combination
Attach the policy register with one row per policy

evidenceHint.en: Policy register, one row per policy, carrying owner, version, audience and review trigger

title.en: Issue each new and revised policy version to the audience the register names

description.en: When a policy is first approved or reissued, put the current version where the audience recorded against it can obtain it and tell that audience it has changed, including contractors and third-party personnel where the policy binds them. Attach the issue record for every version released in the period, naming the audience told, the date, and where the current version can be obtained.

text.en: Identify each policy first approved or reissued in the period and the audience its register row names
Publish the current version where that audience can obtain it
Tell the audience the policy has changed, including contractors and third-party personnel it binds
Record for each version the audience told, the date and where the current version can be obtained
Attach the issue record for every policy version released in the period

evidenceHint.en: Issue record per policy version: audience told, date, and where the current version is available

title.en: Review each policy whose review trigger has fired and record the outcome

description.en: Take every policy the register shows as due, check whether it still matches current practice, obligations and risk, and record for each whether it was reissued unchanged, amended, merged into another policy or withdrawn, together with who approved that outcome. Attach the review record and the register rows updated as a result.

text.en: List every policy the register shows as due because its review trigger has fired
Check each due policy against current practice, current obligations and current risk
Decide for each whether it is reissued unchanged, amended, merged into another policy or withdrawn
Record who approved each review outcome and update the affected register rows
Attach the per-policy review record and the register rows updated as a result

evidenceHint.en: Per-policy review record with the outcome and its approver, plus the updated register rows

templates.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
templates.description: Define and assign information security roles
templates.objective: To ensure that every part of the organisation's security work is held by a named person whose role definition carries it, so nothing rests on an assumption about who acts.
templates.successCriteria:
Each responsibility on the list states in one line what its holder is expected to do.
Every responsibility has a named holder and an effective date, with cover or escalation recorded where such an arrangement exists.
The role definitions of the people holding security responsibilities name those responsibilities.
A responsibility left unheld after a change of holder is visible on the record rather than silently vacant.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the responsibility list with the one-line statement held against each entry.
Export the assignment record showing holder, effective date and any cover or escalation arrangement.
Collect the role definitions of the people named as holders.
Obtain the assignment rows amended during the period and the list of responsibilities recorded as unheld.
Obtain the most recent reconciliation of the assignment record against current personnel.

Analysis:
Read each responsibility statement and judge whether a holder could tell from it what is expected of them.
Identify rows with no named holder, no effective date, or a holder who has left the organisation.
Compare each holder's role definition against the responsibilities the assignment record gives them.
Test whether responsibilities that changed hands in the period show the new holder and the date of the change.
Check that every orphaned, vacant or misassigned responsibility found at reconciliation carries a resolution.

Output:
A list of responsibilities whose statement is too vague to be assigned to anyone.
An exception register of unassigned, stale or duplicated assignments.
A gap list of role definitions that omit the security responsibilities their holder carries.
A note on orphaned or vacant responsibilities still unresolved at the date of test.

title.en: Break the organisation's security work into responsibilities somebody must hold

description.en: Go through the security work the organisation depends on — protecting information, deciding and accepting risk, maintaining the policies and procedures, handling security events, overseeing the parties acting for the organisation — and write each discrete responsibility as one line saying what its holder actually does. Attach the responsibility list.

text.en: List the areas of security work the organisation depends on, from protecting information to overseeing parties acting for it
Split each area into discrete responsibilities, such as deciding and accepting risk or handling security events
Write each responsibility as one line saying what its holder actually does

hint.en: Describe the act the holder performs, not a job title

text.en: Attach the responsibility list with its one-line statement per entry

evidenceHint.en: Responsibility list, each entry with a one-line statement of what its holder does

title.en: Assign every responsibility to a named holder, with the date the assignment took effect

description.en: Against each entry on the list record the person or named role that holds it and the date the assignment took effect. No entry may be left without a holder — that is the whole point of the record. Where the organisation has arranged cover for the holder's absence, or a point at which the holder refers a decision upward rather than taking it alone, record that against the entry as well; where the size or shape of the organisation means there is neither, record that fact against the entry rather than leaving the row incomplete. Attach the completed assignment record.

text.en: Record against each responsibility the person or named role that holds it and the date the assignment took effect
Check the record for entries without a holder and have one assigned before the record is closed
Note the cover arranged for the holder's absence and the point at which a decision is referred upward, where either exists
Note against the entry where the organisation's size or shape means there is no cover or escalation, rather than leaving it blank
Attach the completed assignment record with a holder and effective date on every row

evidenceHint.en: Assignment record with a named holder and effective date on every row, and the cover or escalation arrangement recorded where one exists

title.en: Write the assigned responsibilities into the definition of each role that carries them

description.en: For every role named in the assignment record, add the security responsibilities it now holds to that role's own definition, so the obligation attaches to the post rather than to whoever currently occupies it. Attach the amended role definitions.

text.en: List every role named in the security assignment record
Retrieve the current definition of each of those roles
Add the security responsibilities each role now holds to that role's own definition

hint.en: Attach the obligation to the post, not to whoever occupies it today

text.en: Attach the amended role definitions naming the security responsibilities each carries

evidenceHint.en: Amended role definitions naming the security responsibilities each role carries

title.en: Update the assignment record for each responsibility that changed holder this period

description.en: For every responsibility whose holder or deputy changed during the period — whoever the employment event belonged to — amend the assignment record to name the incoming holder and the date the responsibility moved, and list any responsibility the change left with no holder at all. Attach the amended rows together with the list of unheld responsibilities, empty if there are none.

text.en: Identify each responsibility whose holder or deputy changed during the period, whichever team the employment event belonged to
Amend the assignment record to name the incoming holder and the date the responsibility moved
List any security responsibility the change left with no holder at all
Attach the amended rows with the list of unheld responsibilities, recorded as empty if there are none

evidenceHint.en: The assignment rows amended this period, plus the list of responsibilities left unheld

title.en: Reconcile the assignment record against who actually works here now

description.en: Compare every named holder and deputy against current personnel records and current role definitions, and list the responsibilities now held by someone who has left or moved, held by a role that no longer exists, or held by nobody at all. Attach the reconciliation with the resolution recorded against each discrepancy.

text.en: Compare every named holder and deputy in the assignment record against current personnel records
Compare the roles named in the record against the current role definitions
List responsibilities held by someone who has left or moved, by a role that no longer exists, or by nobody
Resolve each discrepancy and record the resolution against it
Attach the reconciliation of security role holders against personnel and role records

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing orphaned, vacant or misassigned responsibilities and how each was resolved

templates.title: Segregation of duties
templates.objective: To ensure that no single person can both perform and conceal an action against the organisation's information, and that any conflict left standing has been knowingly accepted.
templates.successCriteria:
The conflicting-duties list names each duty pair and the process in which the conflict arises.
Each duty pair is traced to the specific system roles and permissions that confer it.
No account holds both sides of a pair except where an exception records a compensating check and a named risk acceptor.
Entitlement testing runs against current entitlements and every violation it returns has a recorded resolution.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the conflicting-duties list with the process recorded against each pair.
Obtain the mapping of each duty pair to the roles and permissions that grant it, per system.
Collect the before and after entitlement exports for the accounts separated during the period.
Obtain the exception record with its compensating check and risk acceptor per entry.
Obtain the latest entitlement test output listing accounts holding both sides of a pair.

Analysis:
Judge whether the duty pairs cover the processes in which one actor could initiate and approve the same transaction.
Re-perform the mapping for a sample of pairs by inspecting role definitions in the live system.
Confirm each separated account no longer holds the conflicting entitlement in its post-change export.
Assess whether each compensating check would actually detect misuse of the conflict it stands against.
Reconcile the entitlement test output against the resolutions recorded for the accounts it named.

Output:
An assessment of how completely the duty-pair list covers the in-scope processes.
A list of pairs with no system mapping, or a mapping the live configuration contradicts.
A schedule of accounts in violation, each marked separated, excepted or unresolved.
A view on the adequacy of each compensating check and the currency of its risk acceptance.

title.en: Identify the duty pairs that must not be held by one person

description.en: Walk the processes that move money, grant access, change production systems and handle sensitive data, and record each pair of duties that would let one person act and conceal it — requesting versus approving access, developing versus deploying, raising versus approving payment. Attach the conflicting-duties list with the process each pair sits in.

text.en: Walk the processes that move money, grant access, change production systems and handle sensitive data
Record each pair of duties that would let one person act and conceal it, such as developing versus deploying
Note the process each conflicting duty pair sits in
Attach the conflicting-duties list, one row per pair with its process

evidenceHint.en: The conflicting-duties list, one row per pair with its process

title.en: Map each conflicting duty pair to the system roles and permissions that grant it

description.en: For every pair on the list, identify in each in-scope system the concrete roles, groups or permissions that confer each side, so the conflict becomes testable against an entitlement export. Attach the mapping from duty pair to role or permission per system.

text.en: Identify the in-scope systems in which each conflicting duty pair is exercised
Find in each system the roles, groups or permissions that confer each side of the pair
Write up the mapping so each conflict can be tested against an entitlement export
Attach the duty-pair to role or permission mapping for each system

evidenceHint.en: The duty-pair to role/permission mapping, per system

title.en: Separate the accounts that currently hold both sides of a conflicting pair

description.en: Run the mapping against current entitlements, identify accounts holding both sides, and remove or move one side for each so no single account retains the conflict. Attach the before and after entitlement export for the accounts changed.

text.en: Obtain a current entitlement export from each in-scope system
Run the duty-pair mapping against the export and list the accounts holding both sides of a pair
Remove or move one side of the conflict for each account found
Take a second export to confirm no changed account still holds both sides
Attach the before and after entitlement export for every account changed

evidenceHint.en: Before/after entitlement export for every account changed

title.en: Record a compensating check for each conflict that cannot be separated

description.en: Where headcount or system design makes separation impossible, record the conflict, why it persists, the detective check that compensates (independent review of a log, second-person confirmation of the output), who performs it, and who accepted the residual risk. Attach the exception record.

text.en: Identify the conflicting duty pairs that headcount or system design makes impossible to separate
Record for each why the conflict persists and the detective check that compensates, such as independent log review
Name who performs each compensating check and who accepted the residual risk
Attach the segregation exception record with the check and risk acceptor for each entry

evidenceHint.en: The exception record, each entry naming its compensating check and risk acceptor

title.en: Test current entitlements for accounts holding both sides of a conflicting pair

description.en: Re-run the duty-pair mapping over a fresh entitlement export from each in-scope system, list the violations found, and record the remediation or the exception each was closed under. Attach the check output and the remediation record.

text.en: Pull a fresh entitlement export from every in-scope system for this check
Re-run the duty-pair mapping over the export and list the violating accounts
Close each violation by remediation or under a recorded exception, noting which applied
Attach the check output and the remediation record for the violations found

evidenceHint.en: The check output listing violating accounts, with the resolution of each

templates.title: Management responsibilities
templates.objective: To ensure that the people acting for the organisation are held to its security rules by a manager answerable for them, and that anyone unable to comply receives a decision.
templates.successCriteria:
Every population acting for the organisation, contractors and third-party personnel included, has a named answerable manager.
Managers hold the brief stating what they must do about security, and its issue is recorded against each of them.
New and transferring people were told which rules bind their work before their access was granted, with late cases flagged.
Matters raised as impossible to comply with carry a decision, a decider and a date answered, or the period shows a nil return.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the population list with the answerable manager named against each group.
Obtain the approved manager brief and the record of its issue to each manager.
Collect the per-person briefing confirmations for the period with briefing and access-grant dates.
Obtain the log of matters raised as impossible to comply with, or the nil return for the period.
Obtain the sample review of teams against what the brief requires of their manager.

Analysis:
Compare the population list against payroll, contractor and third-party sources for groups with no manager named.
Read the brief for duties a manager can actually discharge rather than aspirations they cannot act on.
For a sample of joiners and transfers, test whether the briefing date precedes the access-grant date.
Follow each raised matter through to the decision given back and judge how long the answer took.
Assess whether the omissions found in the sampled teams were acted on or merely recorded.

Output:
A list of populations with no answerable manager, or one who has left that role.
A distribution exception list of managers with no recorded receipt of the brief.
A schedule of people granted access before being briefed, with the interval in each case.
A summary of raised matters left undecided and of sampled omissions without action.

title.en: List the groups of people who act for the organisation and the manager answerable for each

description.en: Enumerate the populations doing work for or on behalf of the organisation — employees by function, fixed-term and temporary staff, contractors, and third-party personnel given accounts or premises access — and name for each the manager who answers for that group's conduct toward information security. Attach the list with an answerable manager against every group.

text.en: List the employee groups by function, plus fixed-term and temporary staff, who act for the organisation
Add contractors and third-party personnel who have been given accounts or premises access
Name for each group the manager who answers for its conduct toward information security
Attach the group list with an answerable manager against every group

evidenceHint.en: Group list with a named answerable manager for every population, contractors and third-party personnel included

title.en: Write and issue the brief setting out what a manager must do about security

description.en: Set down what management requires of every manager: tell each person joining or transferring into their team which policies and procedures bind their work before access is granted, make the time and means available for the security work their people are required to do, answer what those people cannot resolve themselves, and pass unresolved refusal to comply to the route the organisation has defined for it. Approve the brief and issue it to every manager on the group list. Attach the approved brief and the record of who has been issued with it.

text.en: Set down the manager's duty to tell each joiner or transferee which policies and procedures bind their work before access is granted
Add the duties to make time and means available for required security work and to answer what people cannot resolve
State the route to which a manager passes an unresolved refusal to comply
Approve the brief and issue it to every manager on the group list
Attach the approved manager brief and the issue record naming each manager and the date

evidenceHint.en: The approved manager brief plus the issue record naming each manager and the date

title.en: Record that each new or transferring person was told which rules bind their work before they got access

description.en: For every person starting in or moving into a team during the period, capture the manager's confirmation of what they were told applies to their work and the date it was given, then set that date against the date their access was granted. Attach the confirmations for the period with any that came after the access grant flagged.

text.en: List every person who started in or moved into a team during the period
Obtain each manager's confirmation of what the person was told applies to their work and when
Compare each briefing date with the date the person's access was granted
Attach the confirmations for the period with those dated after the access grant flagged

evidenceHint.en: Per-person confirmations for the period showing briefing date and access-grant date, with late ones flagged

title.en: Log what people raised as unable to comply with, and the decision management gave back

description.en: Keep the record of every case where a person told their manager they could not do what the rules require — the work would stop, the equipment does not permit it, a customer forbids it — with what was asked, who decided, what was decided, and when the answer was given back. A nil return is a valid entry where nothing was raised. Attach the log.

text.en: Record each case where a person told their manager they could not do what the security rules require
Note what was asked, who decided, what was decided and when the answer was given back
Enter a nil return for the period where nothing was raised
Attach the log of matters raised in the period, or the nil return

evidenceHint.en: Log of matters raised in the period, or a nil return, each with the decision, the decider and the date answered

title.en: Sample teams and check the manager did what the brief requires of them

description.en: Take a sample of the groups on the list and for each look for the briefing confirmations covering its recent starters and movers and the answers given back on anything its people raised. Record where the manager's acts were missing, late or undocumented, and what was done about it. Attach the sample review.

text.en: Select a sample of groups from the group list
Look in each sampled group for briefing confirmations covering its recent starters and movers
Check the answers given back on anything the group's people raised
Record where the manager's acts were missing, late or undocumented, and the action taken on each
Attach the sample review naming the teams examined, the omissions found and the action taken

evidenceHint.en: Sample review naming the teams examined, the omissions found and the action taken on each

templates.title: Contact with authorities
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation can reach the right authority quickly when an event demands it, rather than searching for a channel while the incident is running.
templates.successCriteria:
Each authority on the list carries the circumstance that obliges or prompts contact with it.
The contact register holds a current reporting channel, and any reference number, for every authority listed.
An approved procedure states who contacts an authority during an incident and what is passed to them.
Every contact made with an authority appears in the log with its subject and its outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the authority list with the triggering circumstance recorded per entry.
Export the authority contact register with the channel and reference number held on each row.
Obtain the approved procedure for contacting an authority during a security incident.
Obtain the contact log for the period with subject and outcome per entry.
Obtain the verification record showing when each register entry was last checked against the published channel.

Analysis:
Test the authority list against the jurisdictions, sectors and regulations that apply to the organisation.
Check a sample of register rows against the channel the authority currently publishes.
Judge whether the procedure gives a responder enough to act without further research mid-incident.
Reconcile the contact log against the incident record for events whose trigger should have produced a contact.
Assess whether any statutory reporting deadline implied by a trigger is reflected in the procedure.

Output:
A gap list of authorities the organisation is obliged to reach but has not registered.
A list of register rows whose channel or reference no longer matches the published source.
A reconciliation of triggering incidents against the contacts actually logged.
A note on procedural steps that would stall a notification under time pressure.

title.en: Identify the authorities the organisation must be able to reach

description.en: Name the regulators, data protection authority, law enforcement, national CERT and sector bodies relevant to where the organisation operates and what it processes, and record for each what circumstance would require contacting it. Attach the authority list with the trigger per entry.

text.en: List the regulators, data protection authority, law enforcement, national CERT and sector bodies that apply
Check the list against where the organisation operates and what information it processes
Record for each authority the circumstance that would require contacting it
Attach the authority list with the trigger for contact against each entry

evidenceHint.en: The authority list, each entry with the circumstance that triggers contact

title.en: Record the current reporting channel and any reference numbers for each authority

description.en: For every authority on the list capture the channel actually used (portal, hotline, secure email), any registration or case reference the organisation already holds, and the internal person authorised to make contact. Attach the contact register.

text.en: Record for each authority the channel actually used, such as a portal, hotline or secure email
Add any registration or case reference the organisation already holds with that authority
Name the internal person authorised to make contact with each authority
Attach the authority contact register, one row per authority

evidenceHint.en: The authority contact register, one row per authority

title.en: Write the procedure for contacting an authority during a security incident

description.en: State who decides that contact is required, who makes it, what information is provided, how legal review fits in, and how the contact is recorded. Cross-reference the incident procedure so the two do not diverge. Attach the approved procedure.

text.en: State who decides that contact with an authority is required and who makes it
Set out what information is provided to the authority and how legal review fits in
Define how each contact with an authority is recorded
Cross-reference the incident procedure and align the two so they do not diverge
Obtain approval of the authority-contact procedure and attach the approved version

evidenceHint.en: The approved authority-contact procedure

title.en: Log every contact made with an authority and what was reported

description.en: Record each outbound and inbound contact: date, authority, who made it, the subject, what information was disclosed, and the response or reference number received. Attach the contact log for the period.

text.en: Log each outbound and inbound contact with an authority with its date and the authority concerned
Record who made the contact, the subject and what information was disclosed
Note the response or reference number the authority gave
Attach the authority contact log for the period

evidenceHint.en: The authority contact log, one entry per contact with subject and outcome

title.en: Verify each register entry against the authority's currently published channel

description.en: Check every entry still resolves — portal reachable, address and telephone current, named internal contact still in post — and correct the entries that have moved. Attach the verification record showing the date each entry was confirmed and what changed.

text.en: Compare each register entry with the channel the authority currently publishes, checking portal, address and telephone
Confirm that the named internal contact for each authority is still in post
Correct the register entries whose channel or contact has moved
Attach the verification record showing the date each entry was confirmed and what changed

evidenceHint.en: The verification record, confirmation date and correction per entry

templates.title: Contact with special interest groups
templates.description: Maintain contacts with security forums and groups
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation draws specialist security knowledge from outside its own walls and passes what it learns to the teams able to act on it.
templates.successCriteria:
Each group selected is held together with the benefit the organisation expects to draw from it.
The membership register names a representative and an alternate, with a joining date, for every group joined.
Approved rules state what may and may not be disclosed in these forums.
Advisories received have reached the teams they concern, with the recipient and the date recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the candidate group list with the expected benefit noted against each group.
Export the membership register showing group, representative, alternate and joining date.
Obtain the approved rules governing what may be shared with special interest groups.
Obtain the distribution record for the advisories received during the period.
Obtain the most recent membership review with its retain, drop or replace decision per group.

Analysis:
Judge whether the groups joined match the technologies and threats the organisation actually faces.
Check the register for groups whose named representative has left or whose membership has lapsed.
Read the sharing rules against what representatives actually posted or discussed in the period.
Trace a sample of received advisories to the team recorded as recipient and ask what action followed.
Assess whether the retain or drop decisions are supported by what each membership returned.

Output:
A coverage view of the organisation's threat landscape against the groups it belongs to.
A membership exception list of lapsed groups and vacant representative roles.
A sample result on advisories that reached no recipient, or reached one too late to act.
A summary of memberships carried without demonstrated benefit.

title.en: Identify the security forums and professional groups relevant to the organisation

description.en: List the sector information-sharing groups, vendor security communities, national CERT distribution lists and professional associations that match the technologies the organisation runs and the sector it operates in, and record what each is expected to provide. Attach the list with the expected benefit per entry.

text.en: List the sector information-sharing groups, vendor security communities, national CERT lists and professional associations
Match each candidate group to the technologies the organisation runs and the sector it operates in
Record what each matching group is expected to provide
Attach the candidate group list with the expected benefit per entry

evidenceHint.en: The candidate group list, each with the benefit expected from it

title.en: Enrol in the selected groups and name the person who represents the organisation

description.en: Complete membership or subscription for each group chosen from the list, and record the named representative, an alternate, and the joining date. Attach the membership register and the confirmations of membership.

text.en: Select the groups to join from the candidate list
Complete membership or subscription for each selected group
Record the named representative, an alternate and the joining date for each group
Attach the membership register and the confirmations of membership

evidenceHint.en: The membership register showing group, representative, alternate and joining date

title.en: Set the rules for what may be shared with these groups

description.en: Record what information about incidents, vulnerabilities, architecture and customers may leave the organisation through these channels, at what classification, in what form (anonymised or attributed), and who approves an exception. Attach the approved sharing rules.

text.en: Set out what information about incidents, vulnerabilities, architecture and customers may be shared through these groups
State the classification at which each kind may be shared and whether it goes anonymised or attributed
Name who approves an exception to the group sharing rules
Obtain approval of the sharing rules and attach the approved version

evidenceHint.en: The approved sharing rules for special interest group participation

title.en: Circulate advisories received from these groups to the teams that must act

description.en: For each advisory, bulletin or alert received through a membership, route it to the owning team and record what was sent, to whom and on what date. Attach the distribution record for the period.

text.en: Log each advisory, bulletin or alert received through a membership with its source group and date
Route each item to the team that owns the affected technology or service
Record what was sent, to which team and on what date
Attach the advisory distribution record for the period

evidenceHint.en: The distribution record, item received with date and recipient team

title.en: Assess each membership for what it returned and decide whether to keep it

description.en: For every group in the register, record what was received during the period, what action it triggered, and whether participation met the benefit recorded when it was selected; recommend retain, drop or replace. Attach the review with a decision per group.

text.en: Record for each group in the membership register what was received during the period
Note the action each group's material triggered, if any
Compare what participation returned with the benefit recorded when the group was selected
Decide to retain, drop or replace each membership
Attach the membership review with a retain, drop or replace decision per group

evidenceHint.en: The membership review, with a retain/drop/replace decision per group

templates.title: Threat intelligence
templates.objective: To ensure that knowledge of how attackers behave is turned into decisions the organisation acts on, instead of accumulating unread in a feed.
templates.successCriteria:
The source list records each source's coverage level and the route by which the organisation obtains it.
Incoming intelligence is filtered against a recorded profile of the technologies and services actually in use.
Each relevant item carries a rating, a named owner and the action taken, on one log.
The threat summary for the period was issued to the audiences recorded as acting on it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the intelligence source list with coverage level and access route per source.
Obtain the relevance profile listing the technologies and services intelligence is matched against.
Obtain the approved triage and routing procedure, including its rating scale.
Export the threat intelligence log for the period with rating, owner and action per item.
Obtain the issued threat summary with its distribution list, and the latest coverage assessment.

Analysis:
Compare the relevance profile against the technology estate for material omissions.
Re-rate a sample of logged items against the published scale and test whether routing followed the rating.
Follow the highest-rated items to the action they produced and the date it completed.
Compare the intelligence received against the incidents and vulnerabilities the organisation actually experienced.
Judge whether the source-list changes flowing from that comparison were in fact made.

Output:
A statement of the gaps between the relevance profile and the live technology estate.
A sample result on rating consistency and adherence to the routing procedure.
An ageing list of intelligence items with no action recorded against them.
A conclusion on whether the sources in use would have warned of the incidents seen.

title.en: List the threat intelligence sources the organisation will draw on

description.en: Record each feed, vendor bulletin, CERT advisory, commercial service and community source to be used, what level it covers (strategic, tactical or operational), how it is accessed, and its cost. Attach the source list with coverage per source.

text.en: List each feed, vendor bulletin, CERT advisory, commercial service and community source to be used
Classify each source by the level it covers: strategic, tactical or operational
Note how each source is accessed and what it costs
Attach the intelligence source list with coverage level and access route per source

evidenceHint.en: The intelligence source list, each with coverage level and access route

title.en: Record the technologies and services incoming intelligence is filtered against

description.en: Derive from the asset inventory the products, platforms, cloud services and business services the organisation actually runs, so an incoming item can be judged relevant or not. Attach the relevance profile and note the asset inventory version it came from.

text.en: Obtain the current version of the asset inventory
Extract the products, platforms, cloud services and business services the organisation actually runs
Compile them into a relevance profile against which incoming intelligence is judged
Attach the relevance profile noting the asset inventory version it came from

evidenceHint.en: The relevance profile, listing the technologies intelligence is matched against

title.en: Define how an intelligence item is triaged, rated and routed to an owner

description.en: Write the procedure: how relevance is decided against the profile, the rating scale applied, which team receives which category of item, and how an item that warrants immediate action is escalated. Attach the approved triage procedure.

text.en: Define how the relevance of an intelligence item is decided against the relevance profile
Set the rating scale applied to relevant items
Assign the team that receives each category of intelligence item
Define how an item that warrants immediate action is escalated
Obtain approval of the triage and routing procedure and attach it

evidenceHint.en: The approved triage and routing procedure, including the rating scale

title.en: Record every relevant intelligence item, its assessment and the action taken

description.en: For each item that passes triage, log the source, date, what it concerns, the relevance decision and rating, the owner it was routed to, and the action taken or the reason none was needed. Attach the log for the period.

text.en: Log each intelligence item that passes triage with its source, date and what it concerns
Record the relevance decision and the rating given to each item
Name the owner each item was routed to and the action taken, or why none was needed
Attach the threat intelligence log for the period

evidenceHint.en: The threat intelligence log, one row per item with rating, owner and action

title.en: Issue the threat summary to the audiences that act on it

description.en: Produce the consolidated summary for the period covering what was seen, what changed in the threat picture for the organisation's technologies, and what is recommended, and distribute it to the technical and management audiences named in the triage procedure. Attach the issued summary and its distribution list.

text.en: Consolidate what was seen in the period and what changed in the threat picture for the organisation's technologies
Write the recommendations arising from the period's intelligence
Distribute the summary to the technical and management audiences named in the triage procedure
Attach the issued threat summary with its distribution list

evidenceHint.en: The issued threat summary for the period, with its distribution list

title.en: Compare the intelligence received against the incidents and vulnerabilities actually seen

description.en: For the period, check whether the sources warned of what actually occurred, whether items dismissed as irrelevant later mattered, and where a source produced nothing usable; record the coverage gaps and the resulting changes to the source list. Attach the coverage assessment.

text.en: List the incidents and vulnerabilities actually seen in the period
Check whether any intelligence source warned of each before it occurred
Identify items dismissed as irrelevant that later mattered
Record the coverage gaps, including sources that produced nothing usable
Change the source list in response and attach the coverage assessment recording the changes

evidenceHint.en: The coverage assessment, with source gaps and the changes made to the source list

templates.title: Information security in project management
templates.objective: To ensure a project cannot reach delivery without its security work having been done and its residual risk knowingly taken on by a named permanent owner.
templates.successCriteria:
The in-scope test is applied at a named step of the project method rather than left to each project's own judgement.
Each item of required security work has a point in the project's life at which it falls due and a role that decides it is done.
Projects in scope hold completed initiation answers and a risk record naming an acceptor for every accepted risk.
A closing project records what passes to the permanent owner, including the residual risk that owner takes on.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the in-scope criteria and the project-method step at which they are applied.
Obtain the schedule of required security work with its due point and deciding role per item.
Obtain the initiation question set and the answers completed by projects entering scope.
Export the per-project risk records with owner, treatment decision and named acceptor.
Obtain the stage and close decision records and the sample review of closed projects.

Analysis:
Take the full project population for the period and test the in-scope determination independently.
For a sample of in-scope projects, check each due item of security work against evidence that it was decided done.
Read the risk records for accepted risks with no acceptor, or an acceptor without authority at that level.
Test stage decisions for the conditions imposed and whether those conditions were later met.
Check closed projects for a named owner of the residual risk and for security work never completed.

Output:
A list of projects that met the criteria but were never brought into scope.
A per-project schedule of security items overdue, waived or still undecided.
An exception list of accepted risks lacking a competent acceptor.
A summary of closures made with outstanding security work or no residual-risk owner.

title.en: State which projects must involve information security and where the test is applied

description.en: Write the criteria that bring a project into scope — it introduces or changes a system, handles a kind of information the organisation has not handled before, opens a new external exposure, brings in a new third party, or changes an existing control — and name the point in the organisation's project method at which every project is tested against them. Attach the criteria and the step in the method that references them.

text.en: Write the criteria that bring a project into scope for information security involvement
Cover new or changed systems, new kinds of information, new external exposure, new third parties and changed controls
Name the step in the organisation's project method at which every project is tested against the criteria
Reference the criteria from that step of the method
Attach the criteria and the step in the method that references them

evidenceHint.en: In-scope criteria plus the named step in the project method where they are applied

title.en: Name the security work an in-scope project must do, when in its life each item falls due, and who decides it is done

description.en: List the security work an in-scope project has to carry out — the assessment done at the outset, the work its results call for, what must be settled before the project's output is put to real use, and what must be settled before the project is closed. Against each item record the point in the project's life at which it falls due, expressed in whatever terms the organisation actually uses to run work — a stage the method names, a checkpoint, a decision to proceed, or the state the work has reached — and the role that decides the item has been done. Where projects are delivered inside a method the organisation does not control, record how each item is placed within that method and who takes the decision there. Attach the schedule of security work with its due point and its deciding role against every item.

text.en: List the security work an in-scope project must do, from the initial assessment to what is settled before close
Record against each item the point in the project's life when it falls due, in the terms the organisation runs work by

hint.en: A named stage, a checkpoint, a decision to proceed or a state of the work

text.en: Name the role that decides each item of security work has been done
Set out how each item is placed, and who decides, for projects delivered inside a method the organisation does not control
Attach the schedule of security work with its due point and deciding role against every item

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of the security work required of an in-scope project, each item with the point in the project's life at which it falls due and the role that decides it is done

title.en: Produce the security questions a project answers when it comes into scope

description.en: Build the set of questions each in-scope project must answer at initiation: what information it will handle and how sensitive that is, who will need access to it, what it has to stay available for, which third parties are involved, and which obligations apply. Attach the question set as it will be given to projects.

text.en: Draft questions on what information the project will handle and how sensitive it is
Add questions on who will need access, what it must stay available for and which third parties are involved
Add a question on which obligations apply to the project
Assemble the questions into the form projects complete on entering scope and attach it

evidenceHint.en: The initiation question set that projects complete on entering scope

title.en: Record the security risks each in-scope project raised, their owners and what was decided

description.en: For every project in scope during the period, produce the record of the risks surfaced by its initiation answers and by its later stages: what the risk is, who owns it, what treatment was decided, and for anything accepted rather than treated, who accepted it. Attach the record for each project.

text.en: List every project that was in scope for information security during the period
Record the risks surfaced by each project's initiation answers and by its later stages
Record the owner and the treatment decided for each project risk
Name who accepted each risk that was accepted rather than treated
Attach the risk record for each in-scope project

evidenceHint.en: Per-project risk record with owner, treatment decision, and the named acceptor of every accepted risk

title.en: Record each stage decision and, at close, what passes to the permanent owner

description.en: Capture at every stage the decision taken (proceed, proceed with conditions, hold), the conditions attached to it and who took it; at close, record what transfers to the person who will own the delivered thing — residual risks, conditions still open — and that owner's acceptance of them. Attach the decision record for each in-scope project.

text.en: Capture at every stage the decision taken: proceed, proceed with conditions, or hold
Note the conditions attached to each stage decision and who took it
List at close the residual risks and open conditions passing to the permanent owner of what was delivered
Obtain that owner's acceptance of what transfers to them
Attach the decision record for each in-scope project

evidenceHint.en: Decision record per project: stage decisions with conditions and approver, and a close entry naming who took on the residual risk

title.en: Sample closed projects and check the security work each stage required was actually done

description.en: Take the projects closed during the period and for each look for the initiation answers, the risk record, a decision at every stage the method names, and a close entry with a named owner for what remained open. Record every miss and how it was put right. Attach the sample review.

text.en: Select a sample from the projects closed during the period
Look in each sampled project for the initiation answers and the risk record
Confirm a decision is recorded at every stage the project method names
Confirm a close entry names the owner of what remained open
Record every miss and how it was put right, and attach the sample review

evidenceHint.en: Sample review of closed projects listing the missing items per project and their remediation

templates.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation knows what information it holds, where it sits and who answers for it, so that every later protection decision has something to attach to.
templates.successCriteria:
Every business process has been walked, and the information it creates, holds and transmits appears on the inventory.
No inventory entry stands without a named accountable owner, and disputed assets carry a recorded decision.
A record specification states the mandatory fields, their permitted values and who may create or amend an entry.
Assets arriving, moving or going out of use are reflected in the change history with a date and the person who made the change.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the consolidated inventory with type, holding location and serving process per row.
Obtain the inventory export showing the owner field on every entry and the decisions on disputed assets.
Obtain the inventory record specification with its mandatory fields and permitted values.
Obtain the inventory change history for the period covering additions, amendments and retirements.
Obtain the reconciliation against an independent source, with both discrepancy lists.

Analysis:
Select business processes not represented on the inventory and test whether they genuinely hold no information.
Check owner fields for placeholders, team names where a person is required, and holders who have left.
Test a sample of entries against the record specification for missing or out-of-value fields.
Trace assets known to have been acquired or decommissioned through to their change-history entry.
Assess whether the source used for reconciliation is genuinely independent of the inventory itself.

Output:
A list of processes and information flows absent from the inventory.
An exception report of entries with no valid owner or with non-conforming field values.
A lag measure between an asset's real-world change and its inventory update.
A list of discrepancies from the independent-source comparison that remain open.

title.en: Walk each business process and record the information it creates, holds and transmits

description.en: Take each business process or service in turn with the person who runs it and capture the information it handles together with everything that holds that information — systems, databases, shared drives, physical files, and services others run on your behalf. Consolidate what you collect into one inventory. Attach it, with one row per information asset naming its type, where it is held and the process it serves.

text.en: Go through each business process or service in turn with the person who runs it
Capture the information each process creates, holds and transmits
Record everything that holds that information: systems, databases, shared drives, physical files and services others run
Consolidate what was collected into one inventory with one row per information asset
Attach the inventory naming each asset's type, where it is held and the process it serves

evidenceHint.en: Consolidated inventory, one row per asset with its type, where it is held and the process it serves

title.en: Record a named accountable owner against every inventory entry

description.en: For each row identify the individual accountable for that asset being protected and record their name and role. Where a row has no natural owner, put it to management for a decision and record the outcome rather than leaving the field empty. Attach an inventory export showing the owner column with no blanks, plus the decision record for any asset whose ownership was disputed.

text.en: Identify for each inventory row the individual accountable for that asset being protected

hint.en: Name an individual, not a team or department

text.en: Record that person's name and role in the owner field
Put each asset with no natural owner to management and record the decision
Attach an inventory export with no blank owner fields and the decision record for disputed assets

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export with every owner field populated, plus the decision record for disputed assets

title.en: Write down what every inventory entry must carry before it is accepted

description.en: State the mandatory fields for a record — identifier, asset type, owner, where it is held, the process or service it supports — the permitted values for each, and who may create or amend an entry. This is what stops the inventory decaying into free text as entries accumulate. Attach the record specification.

text.en: List the mandatory fields: identifier, asset type, owner, where it is held, and the process or service supported
Set the permitted values for each mandatory inventory field
Name who may create or amend an inventory entry
Attach the record specification with each mandatory field, its permitted values and who may amend

evidenceHint.en: Inventory record specification listing every mandatory field, its permitted values, and who may create or amend a record

title.en: Add, amend and retire entries as assets arrive, move and go out of use

description.en: Run the inventory as a live register: enter new assets when a system goes live or a data set is acquired, amend entries when the owner or the holding location changes, and mark retired assets with the date they went out of use rather than deleting the row. Attach the change history for the period showing every addition, amendment and retirement with its date and the person who made it.

text.en: Enter a new asset when a system goes live or a data set is acquired
Amend the entry when an asset's owner or holding location changes
Mark retired assets with the date they went out of use instead of deleting the row
Attach the period's change history with the date and author of every addition, amendment and retirement

evidenceHint.en: Inventory change history for the period: each addition, amendment and retirement with its date and the person who made it

title.en: Reconcile the information asset inventory against an independent source of what exists

description.en: Choose a source built independently of the inventory — the records the teams running the systems keep for themselves, the services actually being paid for, the contracts held with third parties — and compare it against the inventory line by line. List what exists but is not recorded, and what is recorded but no longer exists, and drive each item to a resolution. Attach the reconciliation naming the source used, both discrepancy lists, and the action taken on every item.

text.en: Choose a source built independently of the inventory, such as teams' own system records, paid services or third-party contracts
Compare the chosen source with the inventory line by line
List what exists but is not recorded, and what is recorded but no longer exists
Drive each discrepancy to a resolution and record the action taken
Attach the reconciliation naming the source used, both discrepancy lists and the action on each item

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation naming the independent source, both discrepancy lists, and the resolution of each item

templates.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
templates.description: Define acceptable use rules for assets
templates.objective: To ensure people handling the organisation's assets know what use is permitted before they make it, and that permission for the conditional cases can actually be obtained.
templates.successCriteria:
Every asset class on the list has a user population recorded against it and a rules section addressing it.
For each class the rules separate what is permitted, what is forbidden and what requires prior permission.
Each conditional use names its grantor, the basis on which permission is given and how long it lasts.
People hold an acknowledgement of the rules version in force, and outstanding responses to a revision are tracked.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the asset-class list with the user population recorded against each class.
Obtain the acceptable use rules with their per-class permitted, forbidden and conditional statements.
Obtain the authorisation table naming grantor, basis and duration for each conditional use.
Obtain the acknowledgement record with person, rules version and date, plus the outstanding-response list.
Obtain the period's record of reported misuse with the classification applied to each case.

Analysis:
Test the asset-class list against the asset inventory for classes in use but not covered by the rules.
Read the rules for uses that are neither permitted, nor forbidden, nor made conditional.
Sample granted permissions and check each against the grantor and basis the table specifies.
Compare acknowledgements against the current rules version and against the population actually holding assets.
Judge whether cases classified as a rule being unclear led to an amendment or a reasoned no-change decision.

Output:
A gap view of the asset classes in use against the classes the rules address.
A list of conditional uses with no identified grantor or no stated duration.
An acknowledgement gap list broken down by population and rules version.
A summary of misuse cases by classification and the amendments they produced.

title.en: List the asset classes the acceptable-use rules must cover, and who handles each

description.en: Take the information asset inventory and derive from it the distinct classes of thing a person handles unaided — computers and mobile devices, removable media, email and messaging, collaboration and file-sharing services, printed output, network access — and record against each the population that handles it. This list is the table of contents for the rules. Attach it.

text.en: Work through the information asset inventory for the things a person handles unaided
Group them into classes such as devices, removable media, email and messaging, file sharing, printed output and network access
Record against each class the population that handles it
Attach the asset-class list with the user population for each class

evidenceHint.en: Asset-class list with the user population recorded against each class

title.en: State what a user may do, may not do, and may do only with permission, for each class

description.en: For every class on the list write, in language a user can act on, what is permitted, what is forbidden, and what is allowed only with permission obtained first — covering personal use, moving organisational information onto personal accounts or personal devices, and use of services the organisation has not approved. Attach the rules with a named section per asset class.

text.en: Write for each class, in language a user can act on, what is permitted and what is forbidden
Add for each class what is allowed only with permission obtained first
Cover personal use, moving organisational information onto personal accounts or devices, and unapproved services
Attach the acceptable use rules with a named section per asset class

evidenceHint.en: Acceptable use rules with a section per asset class stating permitted, forbidden and conditional uses

title.en: Name who grants the permissions the rules make conditional, and how a user asks

description.en: For each conditional use in the rules record who is entitled to grant it, what they need to establish before granting it, how long a grant lasts, and the route by which a user asks for one. Attach the authorisation table alongside the rules.

text.en: List every conditional use in the acceptable use rules
Record who may grant each conditional use and what they must establish before granting it
Set how long each grant of a conditional use lasts
Describe the route by which a user asks for a permission
Attach the authorisation table alongside the rules

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation table naming the grantor, the basis for granting and the duration for every conditional use

title.en: Record each person's acknowledgement when they are first given assets, and issue the current rules whenever they change

description.en: When a person is first given any asset on the list, put the current rules in front of them and record their acknowledgement, covering contractors and third-party account holders as well as employees, and chase the people who have not responded rather than closing the round with gaps. When the rules are revised, issue the new version to everyone they bind and record that it went out and to whom. Decide for each revision, and write down the reason, whether the change is substantial enough to warrant collecting acknowledgements again — a fresh round is a judgement about that change, not something every amendment owes. Attach the acknowledgement record for people newly given assets, the issue record for each revision, and the list of responses still outstanding.

text.en: Put the current rules in front of each person first given an asset, contractors and third-party account holders included
Record each person's acknowledgement with the rules version and the date
Chase the people who have not responded rather than closing the round with gaps
Issue each revised version to everyone it binds and record when it went out and to whom
Decide for each revision whether it warrants a fresh round of acknowledgements and write down the reason

hint.en: A fresh round is a judgement about that change, not owed by every amendment

text.en: Attach the acknowledgement records, the issue record per revision and the outstanding-response list

evidenceHint.en: Acknowledgement record naming person, rules version and date, the issue record for each revision, and the outstanding-response list

title.en: Classify the misuse reported in the period as a rule broken or a rule unclear, and amend accordingly

description.en: Collect what was reported during the period as misuse of an asset and decide for each case whether the rule was clear and was broken, or whether it did not say plainly enough what to do. Amend the wording where the second applies; repeated cases against one clause are a defect in the rules, not only in the person. Attach the record with each case classified and the resulting amendment or the explicit decision to leave the wording alone.

text.en: Collect the cases reported during the period as misuse of an asset
Classify each case as a clear rule that was broken or a rule that did not say plainly enough what to do
Look for repeated cases against one clause and treat them as a defect in the rules
Amend the wording where the rule was unclear, or record the decision to leave it alone
Attach the misuse record with each case classified and its amendment or no-change decision

evidenceHint.en: Record of reported misuse for the period, each case classified, with the resulting amendment or no-change decision

templates.title: Return of assets
templates.description: Ensure return of assets upon termination
templates.objective: To ensure that what the organisation issued to a person comes back, or has its information removed, at the point that person's need for it ends.
templates.successCriteria:
The issued-asset register is keyed to the holder and carries the issue date and issuing function for every item.
The leaver and role-change checklists contain an asset-return step with a sign-off.
Each departure has an itemised return record showing a return date or an outstanding status against every item.
Where an asset cannot be handed back, removal of the organisation's information from it is confirmed and dated.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the issued-asset register keyed to holder, with issue date and issuing function per item.
Obtain the leaver and role-change checklists showing the asset-return step and its sign-off.
Collect the completed asset-return records for the departures in the period.
Obtain the wipe or removal confirmations for assets that could not be physically returned.
Obtain the reconciliation of departures against the register rows left open.

Analysis:
Compare the register against procurement, provisioning and facilities records for issues never recorded.
Take the period's leaver population and test whether each has a completed return record.
Check that itemised returns match what the register says the person held, not only what was handed back.
Verify that removal confirmations name the device or account and the information it held.
Measure how long items remain outstanding before recovery, write-off or a further decision.

Output:
A list of issued items absent from the register, or held by someone no longer employed.
A leaver population result showing returns completed, partial and missing.
A schedule of assets that could not be returned, with the state of information removal on each.
An ageing of outstanding items and the write-off decisions taken on them.

title.en: Build a register of the assets issued to each person, keyed to the holder

description.en: Pull issued laptops, phones, tokens, keys, access cards, removable media, licensed software and physical documents from asset management, procurement and facilities records, and key every item to the individual holding it. Assets nobody can be shown to hold are the ones that never come back. Evidence: the issued-asset register with one row per item, naming the holder, the issue date and the issuing function.

text.en: Pull issued laptops, phones, tokens, keys, cards, media, software and documents from asset, procurement and facilities records
Key each item to the individual holding it, recording the issue date and issuing function
Identify items no holder can be shown for and establish who holds them
Attach the issued-asset register, one row per item naming holder, issue date and issuing function

evidenceHint.en: Issued-asset register keyed to holder, with issue date and issuing function per item

title.en: Add an asset-return step to the leaver and role-change checklists

description.en: Amend the offboarding and internal-transfer checklists so that the issued-asset register is queried for the individual and each item is explicitly cleared, with the step held open until every line is closed. Name the function responsible for clearing each asset type. Evidence: the amended checklists showing the return step, the register query it depends on and the sign-off it requires.

text.en: Amend the offboarding checklist to query the issued-asset register for the person leaving
Amend the internal-transfer checklist with the same register query
Require each item to be cleared explicitly, with the step held open until every line is closed
Name the function responsible for clearing each asset type
Attach the amended checklists showing the return step, the register query and the sign-off required

evidenceHint.en: The amended leaver and role-change checklists showing the asset-return step and its sign-off

title.en: Sign off each departure's asset return against the issued-asset register

description.en: At each departure or role change, work the individual's register rows and record for each item whether it was returned, its condition and the date, closing the row on return. Where an item is not returned, record it as outstanding rather than closing the checklist. Evidence: the completed return records per departure, naming the holder, each item and its return or outstanding status.

text.en: Pull the departing or moving person's rows from the issued-asset register
Record for each item whether it was returned, its condition and the date
Close each row on return and record unreturned items as outstanding
Leave the checklist open while any item remains outstanding
Attach the completed asset-return records for each departure

evidenceHint.en: Completed asset-return records per departure, itemised with return date or outstanding status

title.en: Record the removal of organisational information from assets that cannot be physically returned

description.en: Where a leaver used a personally owned device, a personal cloud account or remote infrastructure the organisation cannot repossess, run the removal or remote wipe and capture the confirmation. Note the information that was held and the method used. Evidence: the wipe or removal confirmations per departure, naming the device or account, the information affected and the date of removal.

text.en: Identify leavers who used a personal device, a personal cloud account or remote infrastructure that cannot be repossessed
Run the removal or remote wipe on each and capture the confirmation it produces
Note the organisational information that was held and the method used
Attach the confirmations naming the device or account, the information affected and the removal date

evidenceHint.en: Remote wipe or removal confirmations naming the device or account, the information held and the removal date

title.en: Reconcile outstanding register rows against the departures recorded in the period

description.en: List every departure and role change in the period, pull the register rows still open against those individuals, and drive each to recovery, replacement or a written write-off. Report items still outstanding at the end rather than closing the reconciliation. Evidence: the reconciliation showing every departure, its open items and the recovery, write-off or still-outstanding status of each.

text.en: List every departure and role change in the period
Pull the issued-asset register rows still open against those individuals
Drive each open item to recovery, replacement or a written write-off
Report items still outstanding at the end rather than closing the reconciliation
Attach the reconciliation showing every departure, its open items and the status of each

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of departures against open register rows, with recovery, write-off or outstanding status per item

templates.title: Classification of information
templates.objective: To ensure information receives protection proportionate to the harm its loss would cause, by placing every asset at a level the organisation has defined in advance.
templates.successCriteria:
The scheme sets out each level with criteria and worked examples that distinguish it from the levels either side of it.
Legal, contractual and regulatory obligations are mapped to the information they cover and the minimum level each demands.
Every asset in the inventory carries a classification level, with contested assignments noted.
Information created or acquired in the period was classified as it entered, with the assigner and the date recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the classification scheme with the criteria and worked examples for each level.
Obtain the obligations table mapping each legal or contractual source to a minimum level.
Obtain the inventory export showing the classification level on every entry.
Obtain the period's inventory additions with the level assigned, the assigner and the date.
Obtain the reclassification record with previous level, new level and the triggering change.

Analysis:
Apply the criteria independently to a sample of assets and compare the result with the level assigned.
Check that assets covered by an obligation are classified at or above the minimum that obligation demands.
Look for levels used so rarely, or so widely, that the scheme is not discriminating in practice.
Test whether additions were classified on entry rather than retrospectively in a single batch.
Follow assets whose sensitivity or value changed to the reclassification that change should have triggered.

Output:
A comparison of assessor-assigned against organisation-assigned levels, with the disagreement rate.
