A list of assets classified below the minimum an obligation requires.
A distribution of assets by level, with unclassified entries called out.
A list of sensitivity changes with no corresponding reclassification.

title.en: Define the classification levels and the criteria that place information in each

description.en: Agree a small set of levels and write, for each, the test a person applies to decide whether information belongs there — the harm from disclosure, from corruption and from unavailability. Include worked examples of real organisational information at each level so the test can be applied without interpretation. Evidence: the classification scheme, one section per level with its criteria and at least one worked example.

text.en: Agree a small set of classification levels
Write for each level the test that places information there, based on the harm from disclosure, corruption and unavailability
Add worked examples of real organisational information at each level

hint.en: Real examples let the test be applied without interpretation

text.en: Attach the classification scheme with one section per level, its criteria and a worked example

evidenceHint.en: The classification scheme with criteria and worked examples for each level

title.en: Record the minimum classification each legal, contractual or regulatory obligation demands

description.en: Work through data protection obligations, customer contract clauses, sector regulation and confidentiality undertakings, and record for each the categories of information it covers and the minimum level that information must therefore carry. This is what makes classification follow business need rather than preference. Evidence: the obligations table mapping each source obligation to the information categories it covers and the minimum level it forces.

text.en: List the data protection obligations, customer contract clauses, sector regulation and confidentiality undertakings that apply
Record for each obligation the categories of information it covers
Set against each obligation the minimum classification level that information must carry
Attach the obligations table mapping each source to the information covered and the minimum level

evidenceHint.en: Obligations table mapping each legal or contractual source to the information covered and the minimum level required

title.en: Assign a classification level to every information asset already in the inventory

description.en: Work the asset inventory row by row with each asset's owner, apply the criteria and the obligations table, and record the resulting level against the entry. Record the reasoning for any asset where the owner and the criteria disagreed. Evidence: the inventory export showing a populated classification for every entry, plus the notes on contested assignments.

text.en: Work through the asset inventory row by row with each asset's owner
Apply the classification criteria and the obligations table to each asset

hint.en: The obligations table sets a minimum; the criteria can place an asset higher

text.en: Record the resulting classification level against the inventory entry
Note the reasoning wherever the owner and the criteria disagreed
Attach the inventory export with a level on every entry and the notes on contested assignments

evidenceHint.en: Inventory export with a classification level on every entry, plus notes on contested assignments

title.en: Classify newly created and newly acquired information as it enters the inventory

description.en: Make classification part of accepting a new information asset: no entry is completed without a level, applied by the asset owner using the published criteria. Cover data sets acquired from customers and third parties as well as internally created information. Evidence: the inventory additions for the period, each showing the level assigned, by whom and on what date.

text.en: Set the inventory acceptance step so no new entry is completed without a classification level
Have the asset owner apply the published classification criteria to each new asset
Include data sets acquired from customers and third parties in the same acceptance step
Attach the period's inventory additions with the level assigned, the assigner and the date

evidenceHint.en: Inventory additions for the period, each with the level assigned, the assigner and the date

title.en: Re-check the classification of assets whose sensitivity or value has changed

description.en: Identify assets affected by a change in use, a new contractual obligation, aggregation with other data, or the passage of time that reduces sensitivity, and re-apply the criteria to each. Record both upward and downward reclassifications, since over-classification carries its own cost. Evidence: the reclassification record listing each asset, its previous and new level, and the change that triggered the re-check.

text.en: Identify assets whose use changed, that gained a new contractual obligation or were aggregated with other data
Identify assets whose sensitivity has fallen with the passage of time
Re-apply the classification criteria to each identified asset
Record every upward and downward reclassification with the previous and new level

hint.en: Over-classification carries its own cost, so record downward moves too

text.en: Attach the reclassification record with the triggering change against each asset

evidenceHint.en: Reclassification record with previous level, new level and triggering change per asset

templates.title: Labelling of information
templates.description: Implement labelling procedures for classified information
templates.objective: To ensure whoever handles a piece of information can see the level it was given, so that the handling rules for that level can be followed without anyone having to ask.
templates.successCriteria:
Each form classified information takes is listed with its producing function and the point at which marking can be applied.
A level-by-form table gives the exact marking wording and where on the item it is placed.
Every form has an accountable role for applying the marking, and forms that cannot carry one have a recorded substitute.
Information received from third parties bears its marking, or the recorded substitute, as internally produced information does.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the form list naming the producing function and the marking point for each form.
Obtain the labelling procedure with its level-by-form marking wording and placement.
Obtain the application map naming the accountable role per form and the substitutes recorded.
Collect the period's sample of produced and received items covering each form on the list.
Obtain the re-marking records for reclassified assets and the latest marking-mismatch sampling.

Analysis:
Check the form list against how information actually leaves and enters the organisation, for forms not listed.
Compare the marking on sampled items against the exact wording and placement the table prescribes.
Judge whether the substitute recorded for an unmarkable form conveys the level to the person handling it.
For reclassified assets, test whether items were re-marked, withdrawn, or recorded as unreachable.
Measure the mismatch rate from sampling and check the corrections were applied to the items found.

Output:
A list of forms in use with no marking defined and no substitute recorded.
A sample result comparing expected against actual marking, by form and by level.
A schedule of reclassified assets with items still bearing the former marking.
A mismatch rate, with the corrections applied and those still outstanding.

title.en: List the forms classified information takes and the point at which each can be marked

description.en: Work with the functions that produce and hold information and enumerate the concrete forms it exists in — documents and spreadsheets, messages, extracts drawn from structured data, removable media, printed output, information shown on screens, and physical files. For each form record the producing function and the point in its life at which a marking can be attached without altering the information itself. Attach the form list, one row per form with its producing function and its marking point.

text.en: Work with the functions that produce and hold information to enumerate the forms it exists in
Cover documents, messages, structured-data extracts, removable media, printed output, on-screen information and physical files
Name the producing function for each form
Identify for each form the point at which a marking can be attached without altering the information
Attach the form list, one row per form with its producing function and marking point

evidenceHint.en: Form list naming each form classified information takes, its producing function and the point at which it can be marked

title.en: Set out the marking that stands for each classification level in each form

description.en: For every level in the classification scheme and every form on the list, write down the exact wording of the marking, where on the item it appears, and what it must survive — copying, printing, extraction, and conversion into another form. Include what a person does when a form cannot carry a visible marking at all. Attach the labelling procedure containing a level-by-form table.

text.en: Draw up a table setting every classification level against every form on the list
Write in each cell the exact wording of the marking and where on the item it appears
State what each marking must survive: copying, printing, extraction and conversion into another form
Set out what a person does when a form cannot carry a visible marking
Attach the labelling procedure containing the level-by-form table

evidenceHint.en: Labelling procedure with a level-by-form table giving the exact marking wording and its placement

title.en: Record who applies the marking for each form and what stands in where none can be carried

description.en: Take each form on the list and record whether the marking is put on by the person producing the information, by the process that produces it, or by a controlling function at the point of issue, and name the accountable role in each case. Where a form genuinely cannot carry a marking, record the substitute that ties the item to its level — an accompanying note, a register entry, a marked container. Attach the application map covering every form on the list, with none left unassigned.

text.en: Record for each form whether the marking is applied by the producer, the producing process or a controlling function at issue
Name the accountable role for applying the marking to each form
Specify the substitute for each form that cannot carry a marking: an accompanying note, a register entry or a marked container
Check that no form on the list is left without an assigned role
Attach the application map covering every form on the list

evidenceHint.en: Application map naming the accountable role per form and the substitute recorded for forms that cannot carry a marking

title.en: Apply the marking, or the recorded substitute, as classified information is produced and as it is received

description.en: Apply the defined marking at the moment information is created, extracted or printed. Where the form cannot carry a marking at all, apply instead the substitute recorded against that form in the application map — the accompanying note, the register entry, the marked container. Information arriving from third parties is brought to the level it warrants under the local scheme rather than leaving another organisation's marking to be read as though it were local. Attach a sample of items from the period covering each form on the list, each item showing either the marking the procedure specifies for that form and level or the substitute recorded against that form, and including items received from third parties.

text.en: Apply the defined marking when information is created, extracted or printed
Apply the substitute recorded in the application map where a form cannot carry a marking
Re-mark information received from third parties at the level it warrants under the local scheme

hint.en: Do not read another organisation's marking as if it were a local level

text.en: Draw a sample of the period's items covering every form, including items received from third parties
Attach the sample showing on each item its specified marking or the recorded substitute

evidenceHint.en: Sample of items from the period covering each form on the list, each showing its specified marking or the recorded substitute, including items received from third parties

title.en: Change the marking on information whose classification level has moved

description.en: When an asset's classification changes, locate the copies and forms already in circulation, apply the new marking or withdraw the item, and record what was reached and what could not be. Downward changes matter as much as upward ones, since a marking left too high keeps information from people who are entitled to it. Attach the re-marking record naming the asset, its old and new level, and the items changed, withdrawn or found unreachable.

text.en: List the assets whose classification changed, downward moves as well as upward ones

hint.en: A marking left too high keeps information from people entitled to it

text.en: Locate the copies and forms of each such asset already in circulation
Apply the new marking to each item reached, or withdraw the item
Note against each asset the copies that could not be reached
Attach the re-marking record naming the asset, old and new level and the items changed, withdrawn or unreachable

evidenceHint.en: Re-marking record per reclassified asset naming old and new level and the items changed, withdrawn or unreachable

title.en: Sample held information and record where the marking does not match its classification

description.en: Draw a sample across the forms on the list, compare the marking on each item against the level its asset carries, and record every mismatch — unmarked, marked too low and marked too high alike. Correct the sampled items and note where repeated errors point at a form whose marking point does not work in practice. Attach the sampling record with expected marking, actual marking and the correction applied for each item.

text.en: Draw a sample of held items across every form on the list
Compare the marking on each sampled item with the level its asset carries
Record every mismatch, whether unmarked, marked too low or marked too high
Correct the sampled items and note forms where repeated errors show the marking point does not work
Attach the sampling record with expected marking, actual marking and correction per item

evidenceHint.en: Sampling record listing each item's expected and actual marking, the mismatches found and the corrections applied

templates.title: Information transfer
templates.description: Secure information transfer policies and procedures
templates.objective: To ensure information keeps the protection its classification demands while it moves between teams, organisations and external parties, by whatever route carries it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every route information takes out of a team or the organisation is listed with its direction, its typical content and a named owner.
Each classification level states the routes that may carry it, those that may not, and the protection and recipient confirmation required first.
Sender and receiver obligations are settled per route, including what is done when a transfer miscarries.
The period's most sensitive transfers are recorded, and per-route checks show each route delivering the protection its rule demands.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the transfer route list and confirm it states direction, the information typically carried and a named owner per route.
Collect the transfer rules table of permitted routes, prohibited routes, required protection and recipient confirmation per classification level.
Gather the statement of sender and receiver responsibilities, including what is done when a transfer goes astray.
Retrieve the transfer records kept for the period's most sensitive transfers and the per-route check records.

Analysis:
Compare the route list against the messaging, file sharing, courier and removable media channels actually available to staff, and name routes absent from it.
Test whether each recorded transfer used a route permitted for the classification of the content it carried.
Confirm the protection noted on each transfer record is the protection that classification's rule demands.
Follow a miscarried or misdirected transfer through the recorded response and against the stated responsibilities.
Judge whether the per-route checks tested the protection claimed rather than the route's availability.

Output:
A route-by-route statement of rule coverage, including unlisted routes discovered.
A table of sampled transfers showing classification carried, route used and protection applied.
Findings on routes whose checks did not demonstrate the required protection.

title.en: List the routes information travels on to leave a team or the organisation

description.en: Enumerate every route in use — messaging, file exchange, portals and interfaces run by the organisation or by the other party, physical carriage of media and paper, and spoken exchange in meetings and calls — and include routes that cross an internal boundary where the receiving part of the organisation is governed separately. Record the direction, the kinds of information typically carried, and a named owner for each route. Attach the route list.

text.en: Enumerate the messaging, file exchange, portals and interfaces in use, whether run by the organisation or the other party
Add physical carriage of media and paper and spoken exchange in meetings and calls
Include routes into parts of the organisation that are governed separately
Record the direction, the information typically carried and a named owner for each route
Attach the transfer route list with direction, content and owner per route

evidenceHint.en: Transfer route list with direction, the information typically carried and a named owner per route

title.en: State for each classification level which routes may carry it and what must be true before it is sent

description.en: Produce the rule table: for every level, the routes that may carry it, the routes that may not, the protection the information must have against interception, alteration and delivery to the wrong party, and how the sender confirms the recipient is the intended one and is entitled to receive. Say what a sender is to do when the permitted route is unavailable. Attach the table with one row per classification level.

text.en: List for each classification level the routes that may carry it and those that may not
State the protection required against interception, alteration and delivery to the wrong party
Set how the sender confirms the recipient is the intended one and is entitled to receive
Say what a sender is to do when the permitted route is unavailable
Attach the transfer rules table, one row per classification level

evidenceHint.en: Transfer rules table showing permitted routes, prohibited routes, required protection and recipient confirmation per level

title.en: Set out what sender and receiver are each responsible for on a transfer, and what is done when one goes astray

description.en: For the routes on the list, write down who is responsible for what when information travels. On the sending side: who may send information at each level by that route, what they must do to carry out the rule for that route and level, and how they establish that it arrived rather than assuming it did. On the receiving side: what the receiving party is expected to do for the transfer to be complete — acknowledge receipt, check the information arrived intact and readable, or say that it did not. Then record what is done when a transfer miscarries: sent to the wrong party, delivered to nobody, or found afterwards to have gone without the protection the rule required. Say what is attempted to retrieve, recall or render useless what was sent, who is told, and by which route it is raised as a security event, without restating the event process here. Attach the responsibilities statement covering every route on the list together with the miscarriage steps.

text.en: Record for each route who may send information at each level by it and what they must do to meet the rule
Set how the sender establishes that a transfer arrived rather than assuming it did
State what the receiver does to complete a transfer: acknowledge receipt, check it arrived intact and readable, or say it did not
Set out how to retrieve, recall or render useless information sent to the wrong party, to nobody, or without protection
Name who is told of a miscarried transfer and the route by which it is raised as a security event

hint.en: Point to the security event process rather than restating it

text.en: Attach the responsibilities statement covering every route, with the miscarriage steps

evidenceHint.en: Statement of sender and receiver responsibilities for every route on the list, plus the steps taken when a transfer miscarries

title.en: Record the transfers of the most sensitive information made in the period

description.en: For the levels the rules single out as most sensitive, keep a record of each transfer outside the organisation: what was sent, to whom, on which route, by whom, on what date, and which protection was applied — using whatever record the route itself produces and a written entry where it produces none. Attach the transfer record for the period.

text.en: Identify the classification levels the transfer rules single out as most sensitive
Record each external transfer at those levels: content, recipient, route, sender, date and protection applied
Use the record the route itself produces, and write an entry where it produces none
Attach the sensitive transfer record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Transfer record for the period naming content, recipient, route, sender, date and the protection applied

title.en: Check that each route delivers the protection its rule requires

description.en: Take the routes one at a time and establish by observation rather than assumption that the stated protection is actually in force — inspect a completed transfer end to end, have the route's owner demonstrate the protection, and where it is safe to do so attempt a transfer the rules prohibit and record whether it was prevented or noticed. Attach the check record naming, per route, what was done, what was observed and whether it met the rule.

text.en: Inspect a completed transfer on each route end to end
Have the route's owner demonstrate the stated protection in force
Attempt a prohibited transfer where it is safe to do so and record whether it was prevented or noticed
Record per route what was done, what was observed and whether it met the rule
Attach the per-route check record with its pass or fail against the rule

evidenceHint.en: Per-route check record stating what was tested, what was observed and the pass or fail against the rule

templates.title: Access control
templates.description: Establish access control policy and rules
templates.objective: To ensure the access each role may hold over each system is decided in advance from business need, rather than settled case by case as requests arrive.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope system and information store is listed with its owner, what it holds and its highest classification.
Each listed system has a rule naming the eligible roles, the access levels they may hold and the forbidden combinations.
A default stance is recorded per system, and access held outside the rules stands on a recorded authorisation.
Systems entering service had a rule before anyone was given access, and the review reached systems no rule previously covered.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope list of systems and information stores the access rules are to cover.
Collect the access control rules, one per in-scope system, with eligible roles, access levels and forbidden combinations.
Gather the recorded default stance per system and the standing list of access held outside the rules.
Retrieve the rule entries for systems brought into service during the period, with date of entry to service and date the rule was recorded.
Obtain the rule review record with its confirm, amend or newly written outcome per system.

Analysis:
Reconcile the scope list against the asset inventory and the stores holding regulated or classified information to find systems no rule reaches.
Test each rule for a stated position on what is denied as well as what is permitted.
Compare, for systems added in the period, the date the rule was recorded with the date the system entered service.
Check that each outside-the-rules entry carries an authorisation and a business reason rather than only a description.
Establish whether the review re-tested rules against current business need or reconfirmed them unchanged.

Output:
A coverage statement of in-scope systems against written access rules.
A list of systems where access preceded the rule, with the interval in each case.
An assessment of standing access outside the rules and the authorisation behind each.

title.en: List the systems and information stores the access rules must cover

description.en: Enumerate the applications, infrastructure, data stores, shared repositories, externally hosted services and administrative consoles that hold or reach organisational information, and record for each a named owner, the information it holds and the highest classification that information carries. Attach the scope list; a system absent from it is one no rule will ever be written for.

text.en: Enumerate the applications, infrastructure, data stores, shared repositories, hosted services and administrative consoles in use

hint.en: A system missing from this list is one no rule will be written for

text.en: Name the owner of each system or information store on the scope list
Record the information each system holds and the highest classification it carries
Attach the scope list naming each system, its owner, its information and its highest classification

evidenceHint.en: Scope list naming each in-scope system, its owner, the information it holds and its highest classification

title.en: Write the access rule for each system, naming the roles and the level of access each may hold

description.en: For every system on the scope list, state which job roles may hold read, contribute and administrative access, what business need must exist before each is given, and which combinations one person must not hold — carrying across the conflicting duty pairs already agreed rather than restating them. Set the strictness from the classification recorded against the system rather than from custom. Attach the access control rules, one rule per system on the list.

text.en: State for each system which job roles may hold read, contribute and administrative access
Record the business need that must exist before each level of access is given
Carry across the conflicting duty pairs already agreed as combinations one person must not hold
Set the strictness of each rule from the classification recorded against the system, not from custom
Attach the access control rules, one per system on the scope list

evidenceHint.en: Access control rules with one rule per in-scope system naming eligible roles, access levels and forbidden combinations

title.en: Record the default stance and the conditions for access no rule covers

description.en: Decide and write down, per system, whether access is refused unless a rule permits it or allowed unless a rule forbids it, and record who may authorise access that no rule covers, what must be true for that to happen, and how long such access may stand before it is revisited. Attach the recorded stance per system together with the standing list of access held outside the rules and the authorisation behind each entry.

text.en: Decide per system whether access is refused unless a rule permits it or allowed unless a rule forbids it
Record who may authorise access that no rule covers and what must be true for that to happen
Set how long access granted outside the rules may stand before it is revisited
Keep a standing list of access held outside the rules with the authorisation behind each entry
Attach the recorded stance per system with the standing list of out-of-rule access

evidenceHint.en: Recorded default stance per system plus the standing list of access held outside the rules with its authorisation

title.en: Write the access rule for each system brought into use before anyone is given access to it

description.en: As each new system, data store or externally hosted service enters service, add it to the scope list with its owner and classification and record the rule that governs access to it; where no existing rule fits, record the decision taken and who took it rather than leaving the system unruled. Attach the rule entries added in the period, each naming the system, the date it entered service and the date its rule was recorded.

text.en: Add each new system, data store or hosted service to the scope list with its owner and classification as it enters service
Write the rule governing access to it before anyone is given access
Record the decision taken and who took it where no existing rule fits
Attach the rule entries added in the period with each system's service entry date and rule date

evidenceHint.en: Rule entries added in the period naming the system, its date of entry to service and the date its rule was recorded

title.en: Re-test each rule against current business need and cover the systems no rule reaches

description.en: Walk the rules with each system owner and confirm that the roles named still exist, still need that access, and still match the classification of the information held, amending the rules that no longer fit and recording those confirmed unchanged. In the same pass, compare the systems actually in use against the scope list and write a rule for anything found uncovered. Attach the review record with a confirm, amend or newly written outcome for every system.

text.en: Walk each rule with its system owner and confirm the named roles still exist and still need that access
Check each rule still matches the classification of the information the system holds
Amend the rules that no longer fit and record those confirmed unchanged
Compare the systems actually in use with the scope list and write a rule for each one found uncovered
Attach the review record with a confirm, amend or newly written outcome for every system

evidenceHint.en: Rule review record with a confirm, amend or newly written outcome per system, including systems found uncovered

templates.title: Identity management
templates.description: Manage identity lifecycle for access control
templates.objective: To ensure every identity in use, human or machine, traces to a known holder and is created, changed and disabled on an authoritative trigger rather than on request.
templates.successCriteria:
Each identity type in use is registered against the directory holding it and the size of its population.
Create, change and disable events each map to an authoritative trigger, so no identity changes state on an unsourced request.
Every shared and service identity carries a justification, a named human owner and recorded custody of its credential.
Leaver disablements record the elapsed time from trigger to disablement, and no orphaned or dormant identity is left without a decision.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and its population size.
Collect the identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and the identity action taken.
Gather the shared and service identity register with justification, named owner and credential custody per entry.
Retrieve leaver identity records carrying both the trigger timestamp and the disablement timestamp.
Obtain the reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the decision on each.

Analysis:
Export the live account population from each named directory and compare its size with the figure registered.
Trace a sample of leavers from the authoritative people record to disablement and compute the elapsed time from the stated trigger.
Check that each shared or service identity has a current employee as owner and a justification that still describes a live need.
Test whether the reconciliation source is the authoritative people, contractor and service record, not the directory reconciled against itself.
Establish that dormant identities close with a disablement or a dated exception rather than an open status.

Output:
A per-directory count of live identities against the registered population.
The distribution of leaver disablement intervals with the outliers named.
A list of shared and service identities lacking a current owner or a live justification.

title.en: List the identity types in use and the directories that hold each

description.en: Enumerate the categories of identity the organisation issues — employee, contractor, temporary, third-party, customer, service and shared identities — and record which directory, application account store or cloud tenancy holds each category. Identities held outside the central directory are the ones that survive a leaver process. Evidence: the identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and the population size.

text.en: List the identity categories issued: employee, contractor, temporary, third-party, customer, service and shared
Record which directory, application account store or cloud tenancy holds each category

hint.en: Identities held outside the central directory are the ones that survive a leaver process

text.en: Count the population of each identity type
Attach the identity register naming each type, its holding directory and its population size

evidenceHint.en: Identity register naming each identity type, its holding directory and its population size

title.en: Define the lifecycle events that create, change and disable an identity, and the trigger for each

description.en: Write the procedure connecting a real-world event to an identity action: hire, contract start, internal transfer, extended absence, contract end and departure, and for each name the authoritative source that signals it and the identity action it forces. Cover contractor and third-party identities, which usually have a different signalling source from employees. Evidence: the identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and the resulting create, amend or disable action.

text.en: List the lifecycle events: hire, contract start, internal transfer, extended absence, contract end and departure
Name for each event the authoritative source that signals it
Name the create, amend or disable action each event forces
Record the signalling sources for contractor and third-party identities separately

hint.en: These usually differ from the source that signals employee events

text.en: Attach the identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its trigger and action

evidenceHint.en: Identity lifecycle procedure mapping each event to its authoritative trigger and identity action

title.en: Record the justification and named human owner for every shared and service identity

description.en: Work through the shared accounts, service accounts and machine identities found in the register; for each, record why an individual identity could not be used, the human accountable for it, the systems it reaches and how its credential is held. Where no justification survives contact, schedule the identity for replacement. Evidence: the shared and service identity register, one row per identity with its justification, its named owner and its credential custody arrangement.

text.en: Pull the shared accounts, service accounts and machine identities from the identity register
Record for each why an individual identity could not be used
Name the human accountable for each and the systems it reaches
Note how each shared or service identity's credential is held
Schedule for replacement any identity whose justification does not hold up
Attach the shared and service identity register with justification, owner and credential custody

evidenceHint.en: Shared and service identity register with justification, named owner and credential custody per identity

title.en: Disable identities on the leaver trigger and record the elapsed time from trigger to disablement

description.en: On each departure or contract end, disable the individual's identities across every directory in the register, and record both the moment the authoritative trigger fired and the moment each identity was disabled. Recording the interval is what makes the delay visible and improvable. Evidence: the leaver identity records for the period, naming the person, each identity disabled, the trigger timestamp and the disablement timestamp.

text.en: Record the time the authoritative leaver trigger fired for each departure or contract end
Disable the person's identities in every directory listed in the identity register
Log the time each identity was disabled
Calculate the interval from trigger to disablement for each leaver
Attach the leaver identity records with trigger and disablement timestamps

evidenceHint.en: Leaver identity records naming each identity disabled, with trigger timestamp and disablement timestamp

title.en: Reconcile active identities against the authoritative people, contractor and service records

description.en: Extract the active identities from every directory in the register and match them against the current people record, the contractor schedule and the service identity register. List identities with no matching current holder, dormant identities, and holders with identities in directories their role does not require, and drive each to disablement or a recorded exception. Evidence: the reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the disablement or exception decision on each.

text.en: Extract the active identities from every directory in the identity register
Match them against the current people record, the contractor schedule and the service identity register
List identities with no current holder, dormant identities and identities in directories the role does not require
Disable each listed identity or record an exception decision against it
Attach the reconciliation output with the disablement or exception decision on each line

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation output listing orphaned and dormant identities with the disablement or exception decision per line

templates.title: Authentication information
templates.description: Manage allocation and use of authentication info
templates.objective: To ensure credentials reach only a confirmed recipient, are strong enough for what they protect, and are replaced or withdrawn once exposed or no longer needed.
templates.successCriteria:
Every kind of authentication information in use is registered against the systems relying on it, its holders and where it is held.
No credential is issued or replaced without a recorded authorisation and a confirmed recipient, system-held credentials included.
Each kind carries a stated strength requirement and validity period, with a per-system note of how that is upheld.
Exposed or outlived credentials are replaced, and no credential supplied with a product or created at installation remains usable.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of authentication information by system and kind, with holder populations and storage locations.
Collect the issuance and replacement procedure for person-held and system-held credentials, covering authorisation, recipient confirmation and first use.
Gather the strength and validity requirement statement per kind, with the per-system note of how it is upheld.
Retrieve the period's log of issues, replacements and withdrawals, and the record of credentials replaced after exposure.
Obtain the check record stating, per system, whether a supplied or installation credential remains usable.

Analysis:
Sample issuance entries and confirm each names the requester, the performer and the confirmation method actually used.
Compare the stated strength and validity requirements with the configuration enforced on each system named.
Trace a known exposure through to the replacement record and the systems it touched.
Witness an authentication attempt with a documented default credential on a sample of systems to test the check's claim.
Assess whether service account secrets and API keys travel the same issuance route as credentials issued to people.

Output:
A register-to-system coverage statement for authentication information.
Sampled issuance records with the recipient confirmation evidenced or missing on each.
A per-system verdict on supplied and installation-time credentials.

title.en: List the kinds of authentication information in use and where each is held

description.en: For every system a person or a process signs in to, record the kinds of authentication information it accepts — secrets the holder chooses, credentials issued to a named holder, and credentials used by systems and scripts with no person behind them — and where each is kept once it has been issued. Attach the register, one row per system and kind, naming the holder population and the place of custody.

text.en: List every system a person or a process signs in to
Record the kinds each accepts: holder-chosen secrets, credentials issued to a named holder, and credentials used by systems and scripts
Note where each kind of authentication information is kept once issued
Name the holder population for each system and kind
Attach the register, one row per system and kind, with holder population and place of custody

evidenceHint.en: Register of authentication information by system and kind, naming the holder population and where the credential is held

title.en: Set out how a request is authorised and the recipient confirmed before authentication information is issued or replaced

description.en: Write the procedure covering first issue and every later replacement, for both kinds of entry on the register. Where the credential has a person behind it: what establishes that the person asking is the holder, how the credential reaches them without passing through anyone else's hands or records, whether it must be replaced by the holder before it can be used for real work, and what is done when a request arrives and the holder cannot be reached in the usual way. Where the credential belongs to a system, service or script with no person behind it: who may request one, what authorises the request, the named role accountable for the credential once it exists, and how it is placed into the system that will use it without being exposed on the way. Attach the issuance and replacement procedure, covering both kinds.

text.en: Set how a person asking for a credential is established as its holder, for first issue and every replacement
Define how a person's credential reaches them without passing through anyone else's hands or records
State whether the holder must replace it before real use and what is done when the holder cannot be reached as usual
Set who may request a system credential, what authorises the request and the role accountable for it
Define how a system credential is placed into the system that uses it without being exposed on the way
Attach the issuance and replacement procedure covering person-held and system-held credentials

evidenceHint.en: Issuance and replacement procedure covering person-held and system-held credentials: what authorises the request, how the recipient is confirmed, and first use

title.en: State what makes each kind of authentication information strong enough and how long it stays valid

description.en: For each kind on the register, record the requirement — what an acceptable secret or credential must be, whether it may be reused anywhere else, and the point at which it ceases to be valid — and note against each system whether the requirement is upheld by the system itself or depends on the holder observing it, since the second needs a different kind of assurance. Attach the requirement statement together with the per-system note of how it is upheld.

text.en: Record for each kind on the register what an acceptable secret or credential must be
State whether each kind may be reused anywhere else and the point at which it ceases to be valid
Note against each system whether the requirement is enforced by the system or depends on the holder

hint.en: Holder-dependent requirements need a different kind of assurance

text.en: Attach the requirement statement with the per-system note of how it is upheld

evidenceHint.en: Requirement statement per kind of authentication information, with a per-system note of how it is upheld

title.en: Record each issue, replacement and withdrawal of authentication information with the confirmation performed

description.en: Every time authentication information is allocated, replaced or withdrawn, record who asked, who carried it out, how the holder was confirmed and the date, writing the entry as the act is done rather than reconstructing it afterwards. Attach the log for the period.

text.en: Open a log entry for each allocation, replacement or withdrawal of a credential as it is done
Note who asked for the credential change and who carried it out
Record how the holder was confirmed and the date
Attach the log of issues, replacements and withdrawals for the period

evidenceHint.en: Log of issues, replacements and withdrawals for the period, each naming the requester, the performer and the confirmation made

title.en: Replace authentication information that has been exposed or has outlived its purpose

description.en: When a credential is disclosed in the course of support, turns up somewhere it should not be held, is left over from work that has ended, or is held by someone no longer entitled to it, replace or withdraw it and record what was done. Attach the replacement record naming each credential, the reason it was replaced, the systems affected and the date.

text.en: Identify credentials disclosed during support or found held somewhere they should not be
Identify credentials left over from ended work or held by someone no longer entitled to them
Replace or withdraw each identified credential
Record the reason, the systems affected and the date for each credential replaced or withdrawn
Attach the replacement record naming each credential

evidenceHint.en: Replacement record naming each credential replaced or withdrawn, the reason, the systems affected and the date

title.en: Establish that credentials supplied with a product or created at installation can no longer be used

description.en: Work the register system by system and establish for each that any credential that arrived with the product or was created when it was installed has been removed or replaced — by demonstrating that it is refused, or from the system's own list of holders. Record the systems where this could not be established as findings rather than as passes. Attach the check record, one row per system with the outcome.

text.en: Work through the register system by system for credentials supplied with the product or created at installation
Demonstrate that each such credential is refused, or confirm its absence from the system's list of holders
Record as a finding, not a pass, any system where removal or replacement could not be established
Attach the check record, one row per system with its outcome

evidenceHint.en: Check record with one row per system stating what was checked and whether a supplied credential remains usable

templates.title: Access rights
templates.description: Provision, review and revoke access rights
templates.objective: To ensure the rights a person actually holds are the rights an authorised approver granted, and that they contract when the person's role changes or ends.
templates.successCriteria:
Every access profile each system offers is catalogued with what that profile permits.
Each profile has a required approver and a stated minimum content an approval must carry.
Grants made in the period rest on an approval recorded before the grant and kept with it.
Role changes and departures produced a decision on every profile held with the removals executed, and rights no approval or review decision supports are removed or formally accepted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the entitlement catalogue naming each system, the profiles it offers and what each permits.
Collect the approval map giving the required approver and required approval contents for every catalogued profile.
Gather the grants made in the period, each naming the person, the profile, the approval relied on and who executed it.
Retrieve the role-change and departure records showing profiles held, the keep or remove decision on each and the removals executed.
Obtain the completed access review, including the privileged recertification result carried into it.

Analysis:
Pull a live entitlement export from a sample of systems and compare the profiles held against the catalogue.
Test each sampled grant for an approval dated before the grant and given by the approver the map requires.
Follow role changers to confirm the rights their former role carried were withdrawn, not merely added to.
Check the review for holders kept without a named reviewer, and for remove decisions with no matching removal.
Reconcile rights held against approvals and review decisions and account for every right neither supports.

Output:
A held-versus-catalogued profile comparison per sampled system.
A list of grants made without a qualifying prior approval.
An exception list of unsupported rights with the removal or acceptance recorded against each.

title.en: Catalogue the access profiles each system offers and what each one permits

description.en: For every system, list the roles, groups or entitlement sets a person can be given and state in plain words what each one lets the holder see and do, marking those that grant administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach. Attach the entitlement catalogue; without it neither an approver nor a reviewer has anything to judge against.

text.en: List for every system the roles, groups or entitlement sets a person can be given
Describe in plain words what each profile lets its holder see and do
Mark the profiles that grant administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach
Attach the entitlement catalogue naming each system, its profiles and what each permits

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement catalogue naming each system, each profile it offers and what that profile permits

title.en: Record who must approve each profile and what the approval has to state

description.en: Map every profile in the catalogue to the person or role whose agreement is needed before anyone holds it, and set out what an approval must contain — the person, the profile, the business reason, and how long it is needed for. State how the approval is captured so that it can be produced later against the grant it authorised. Attach the approval map covering every profile in the catalogue.

text.en: Map every catalogued profile to the person or role whose agreement is needed before anyone holds it
Set what an approval must state: the person, the profile, the business reason and how long it is needed
Define how an approval is captured so it can be produced later against the grant it authorised
Attach the approval map covering every profile in the catalogue

evidenceHint.en: Approval map giving the required approver and the required contents of an approval for every catalogued profile

title.en: Grant access only against a recorded approval and keep the approval with the grant

description.en: For each grant made in the period record the person, the system, the profile, the approval relied on and who carried the grant out, and turn away requests that arrive without an approval rather than granting first and papering over it afterwards. Attach the grants made in the period, each tied to the approval that authorised it.

text.en: Check each access request for a recorded approval from the approver the map names before granting
Turn away requests that arrive without an approval rather than granting first
Record for each grant the person, system, profile, approval relied on and who carried it out
Attach the grants made in the period, each tied to its authorising approval

evidenceHint.en: Grants made in the period, each naming the person, the profile, the approval relied on and who executed it

title.en: Withdraw the access a person no longer needs when they change role or leave

description.en: On each move or departure, list the profiles the person holds, decide keep or remove against what their new position requires, and execute the removals — paying particular attention to access that survives their account being closed, such as membership of groups, access to shared repositories and mailboxes, rights on locally held accounts, and access delegated to others on their behalf. A move that only adds is the accumulation this task exists to stop. Attach the records showing profiles held before, the decision on each and the removals executed.

text.en: List the profiles a person holds when they move or leave
Decide keep or remove for each profile against what their new position requires

hint.en: A move that only adds access is the accumulation this task exists to stop

text.en: Check for access that survives account closure: group membership, shared repositories and mailboxes, local accounts, delegations
Execute the removals in each system and record when they were done
Attach the records showing profiles held before, the decision on each and the removals executed

evidenceHint.en: Role-change and departure records showing profiles held before, the keep or remove decision on each and the removals executed

title.en: Put every holder of each non-administrative profile to its system owner for a keep or remove decision

description.en: When the access review falls due, give each system owner the current holders of every profile in their systems that the catalogue does not mark as granting administrative or otherwise unrestricted reach, and require an explicit keep or remove decision against each named person, refusing blanket approvals covering a whole list. The profiles the catalogue does mark are recertified where privileged access rights are managed: take that recertification's result into this review and record that it was taken in, rather than deciding those holders again here. Where a system offers no profile outside the marked ones, record that and the recertification carried in. Return the removals for execution and confirm they were carried out. Attach the completed review showing the reviewer, the decision per holder, the removals executed, and the privileged result carried in.

text.en: Give each system owner the current holders of every profile not marked administrative or unrestricted in the catalogue
Require an explicit keep or remove decision against each named person, refusing blanket approvals of a whole list
Take in the privileged access recertification result for the marked profiles and record that it was taken in

hint.en: Do not decide privileged holders again here; carry in that result

text.en: Note any system that offers only marked profiles, and record the recertification carried in for it
Return the removals for execution and confirm they were carried out
Attach the completed review with reviewer, decision per holder, removals executed and privileged result carried in

evidenceHint.en: Completed access review showing the reviewer, a keep or remove decision per holder, the executed removals, and the privileged recertification result carried in

title.en: Account for every right held that no approval or review decision supports

description.en: Take the rights actually held in each system and match them against the approvals recorded and the decisions returned by the last review. List every right with nothing behind it, every administrative profile whose holders were never approved, and every holder whose right outlived the reason it was granted, then drive each line to removal or to an acceptance recorded against a named owner. Attach the comparison with a disposition on every line.

text.en: Extract the rights actually held in each system
Match each right against the recorded approvals and the decisions from the last access review
List rights with nothing behind them, unapproved holders of administrative profiles, and rights that outlived their reason
Drive each line to removal or to an acceptance recorded against a named owner
Attach the comparison of held rights with a disposition on every line

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of held rights against approvals and review decisions, with a removal or recorded acceptance on every line

templates.title: Information security in supplier relationships
templates.objective: To ensure the security expected of a supplier is set by the risk its access carries and is settled before that supplier is given anything to access.
templates.successCriteria:
Every supplier that reaches information or information systems is on the register with its access route and business owner.
Each registered supplier carries a risk tier assigned against stated classification criteria.
The assurance required before onboarding is written per tier, so the requirement is known before a supplier is chosen.
Suppliers onboarded in the period were assessed against their tier before access was granted, and no engaged third party is missing from the register.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the supplier register with the access route and business owner recorded per supplier.
Collect the classification criteria and the risk tier assigned to each registered supplier.
Gather the tiered supplier security requirements document.
Retrieve the completed pre-onboarding assessments for suppliers onboarded during the period.
Obtain the reconciliation of the register against externally held accounts and engaged third parties.

Analysis:
Compare the register against payables, procurement records and externally granted accounts to find suppliers with access but no entry.
Re-apply the classification criteria to a sample of suppliers and test whether the assigned tier follows from them.
Check that each pre-onboarding assessment answers every requirement its tier sets rather than a general questionnaire.
Compare the date of each assessment with the date access was first granted to that supplier.
Establish how unregistered suppliers found in the reconciliation were handled and whether the register was corrected.

Output:
A register completeness statement naming the unregistered suppliers found.
Sampled tier assignments with agreement or disagreement recorded per supplier.
A timeline of assessment against first access for each supplier onboarded in the period.

title.en: Compile a register of suppliers that access information or information systems

description.en: List each supplier, the information or system it reaches, how it reaches it (network access, hosted data, on-site presence, staff augmentation) and the internal business owner. Attach the register; suppliers with no access to information are out of scope and should be excluded deliberately, not overlooked.

text.en: List every supplier the organisation currently engages, drawing on procurement and contract records
Record for each supplier the information or system it reaches and the route: network access, hosted data, on-site presence or staff augmentation
Name the internal business owner accountable for each supplier relationship
Mark each supplier with no access to information as out of scope, with the reason recorded against it

hint.en: Exclude deliberately: a supplier that is simply absent looks the same as one that was overlooked

text.en: Attach the supplier register showing the access route and business owner for every supplier

evidenceHint.en: Supplier register with access route and business owner per supplier

title.en: Classify each registered supplier by the risk its access presents

description.en: Apply a written criterion — sensitivity of information reached, depth of access, dependence of the business on the service — and record the resulting tier against each supplier. Attach the register carrying the tier column plus the criteria used to assign it.

text.en: Write the classification criterion: sensitivity of information reached, depth of access and business dependence on the service
Define the risk tiers the criterion produces and what places a supplier in each
Apply the criterion to every registered supplier and record the resulting tier in a register column
Attach the supplier register with its tier column together with the criteria used to assign it

evidenceHint.en: Supplier register with assigned risk tier and the classification criteria

title.en: State the security assurance required before onboarding a supplier in each tier

description.en: For every tier, write down what must be obtained before access is granted — assessment questionnaire, certification or audit report, technical review, contractual commitments. Attach the tiered requirements so an onboarding decision can be checked against a stated bar.

text.en: Choose for each tier which of an assessment questionnaire, a certification or audit report and a technical review must be obtained
Set the contractual security commitments each tier must have in place before access is granted
Write down what an acceptable result looks like for each item, so an onboarding decision can be checked against a stated bar
Attach the tiered supplier security requirements document

evidenceHint.en: Tiered supplier security requirements document

title.en: Assess each new supplier against its tier's requirements before access is granted

description.en: Run the assurance activity the tier demands, record the findings and any accepted shortfalls, and note who approved granting access. Attach the completed assessment for each supplier onboarded in the period.

text.en: Confirm the new supplier's tier and look up the assurance that tier requires before onboarding
Run each assurance activity the tier demands and record the findings
Record any shortfall accepted, with the reason and the person who accepted it
Record who approved granting access and the date, before any access is provisioned

hint.en: Check the sequence: an approval dated after access was granted shows the assessment did not gate it

text.en: Attach the completed pre-onboarding assessment for each supplier onboarded in the period

evidenceHint.en: Completed pre-onboarding assessment per supplier onboarded in the period

title.en: Reconcile the supplier register against externally held accounts and engaged third parties

description.en: Compare the register with the external identities present in the organisation's systems and with third parties actually engaged by the business, to find suppliers that gained access without being registered. Attach the reconciliation and the disposition of each supplier found outside the register.

text.en: Extract the external identities present in the organisation's systems, such as guest and contractor accounts
Obtain the list of third parties actually engaged by the business, for example from purchasing or payment records
Compare both lists with the supplier register and list every supplier found outside it
Decide and record how each unregistered supplier was handled, such as registering and assessing it or removing its access
Attach the reconciliation listing each unregistered supplier found and its disposition

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing unregistered suppliers found and how each was handled

templates.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
templates.description: Include security requirements in supplier contracts
templates.objective: To ensure the security obligations placed on a supplier are written into the agreement that binds it, so they outlast the people who negotiated them and can be enforced.
templates.successCriteria:
A required-clause set exists and states which clauses apply at each supplier tier.
The standard supplier contract template carries those clauses, so a new agreement reaches the supplier with them already in it.
The clause-coverage matrix shows, supplier by required clause, what each active agreement actually contains.
Suppliers onboarded in the period have an executed agreement or amendment filed against their register entry, and every clause gap has a recorded decision-maker.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the required-clause set and its mapping to supplier tier.
Collect the standard supplier contract template with the security clauses marked.
Gather the clause-coverage matrix of active agreements against required clauses.
Retrieve the executed agreements or security amendments filed for suppliers onboarded in the period.
Obtain the clause-gap list with the decision and decision-maker recorded on each gap.

Analysis:
Read a sample of executed agreements and verify each matrix entry against the contract text rather than the template used.
Test whether the clause set covers subcontracting, incident notification, return or deletion of information and right of audit.
Confirm the template the contracting team works from today is the version carrying the marked clauses.
Check that agreements pre-dating the clause set appear in the matrix and were not set aside as legacy.
Assess whether each gap decision was taken by someone able to accept the exposure it leaves.

Output:
A clause-by-clause coverage result for the sampled agreements.
A list of matrix entries the contract text contradicts.
An account of open clause gaps with the accepting decision-maker named.

title.en: Draw up the set of security clauses a supplier agreement must contain

description.en: Derive the clause set from the supplier tiers — confidentiality, permitted use of information, incident notification, subcontracting consent, personnel screening, return or deletion of information on exit, and the right to verify. State which clauses apply to which tier. Attach the clause set.

text.en: Take the supplier tiers as the basis for deciding which security clauses each agreement must carry
Draft clauses for confidentiality, permitted use of information, incident notification and consent to subcontracting
Draft clauses for personnel screening, return or deletion of information on exit, and the right to verify
Map each clause to the supplier tiers it applies to
Attach the required-clause set with its tier mapping

evidenceHint.en: Required-clause set, mapped to supplier tier

title.en: Insert the required security clauses into the standard supplier contract template

description.en: Amend the organisation's standard agreement and any framework or purchase-order terms so the clause set is the default rather than negotiated case by case. Attach the updated template with the security clauses marked and the version date visible.

text.en: Identify the standard supplier agreement and every framework agreement or purchase-order terms the organisation issues
Amend each so the required clause set is the default wording rather than negotiated case by case
Mark the security clauses in the template and set a visible version date
Withdraw superseded template versions so new supplier agreements start from the amended one
Attach the updated contract template with the security clauses marked

evidenceHint.en: Updated contract template with the security clauses marked

title.en: Record which required clauses each active supplier agreement actually contains

description.en: Read every in-force agreement for registered suppliers and mark, clause by clause, whether it is present, absent or weakened by negotiation. Attach the coverage matrix of supplier against clause — this is what turns the template into an assertion about signed contracts.

text.en: Collect the in-force agreement for every registered supplier
Record any registered supplier for which no in-force agreement can be found
Read each agreement clause by clause against the required set for that supplier's tier
Mark each required clause as present, absent or weakened by negotiation

hint.en: Weakened is the easy one to miss: the clause heading survives but its obligation was negotiated away

text.en: Attach the clause-coverage matrix of supplier against required clause

evidenceHint.en: Clause-coverage matrix, supplier by required clause

title.en: File the executed agreement or amendment for each supplier onboarded in the period

description.en: For every supplier taken on, store the signed agreement (or the signed security amendment to an existing one) against its register entry so the contract is retrievable without asking the business owner. Attach the executed documents filed for the period.

text.en: List the suppliers taken on during the period from the supplier register
Obtain the signed agreement, or the signed security amendment to an existing one, for each new supplier
File each executed document against the supplier's register entry so it is retrievable without asking the business owner
Record any supplier onboarded in the period for which no signed document exists
Attach the executed agreements and amendments filed for the period

evidenceHint.en: Executed agreements or security amendments filed against register entries

title.en: Resolve each active agreement that is missing a required clause

description.en: Take every gap from the coverage matrix and record the route chosen — renegotiation at renewal, a side letter, a compensating technical or operational measure, or a documented acceptance — together with who decided. Attach the gap list with a disposition against every entry.

text.en: Extract every absent or weakened clause from the coverage matrix into a gap list
Choose a route for each gap: renegotiation at renewal, a side letter, a compensating technical or operational measure, or documented acceptance
Record who decided the route for each gap and when
Note the renewal date for each gap deferred to renegotiation
Attach the clause-gap list with a disposition and decision-maker against every entry

evidenceHint.en: Clause-gap list with the decision and decision-maker for each gap

templates.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
templates.objective: To ensure the risk carried in through purchased ICT, its upstream components and its delivery is judged before adoption and re-judged as the supply chain shifts.
templates.successCriteria:
Each acquired ICT product and service is listed with its supplier, where it runs and the service that depends on it.
Dependency declarations have been sought from every ICT supplier, with non-responses recorded rather than left blank.
Security acceptance criteria are applied before adoption, with a decision and decision-maker recorded per acquisition.
Delivered software and firmware are verified for authenticity and integrity before deployment, and entries failing the criteria carry a recorded outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the ICT component list showing product or service, supplier, where it runs and the dependent service.
Collect the per-supplier dependency declarations of subcontractors and upstream components, including the record of non-responses.
Gather the ICT acquisition security acceptance criteria.

templates.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
templates.objective: To ensure a supplier's delivery and security posture stay visible through the engagement, and that changes it makes to its service are judged before they take effect.
templates.successCriteria:
What each supplier owes by way of service and security reporting is recorded, with the frequency due and the recipient.
Reports falling due in the period were received and reviewed, with findings raised where their content warranted it.
Every supplier-notified service change is logged with an impact assessment made before the change took effect.
Suppliers above the risk threshold held their periodic service review, closing with agreed actions and named owners.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the supplier monitoring schedule naming the report due, its frequency and its recipient for each supplier.
Collect the procedure by which a supplier-notified service change is assessed before it takes effect.
Gather the supplier reports received in the period with the review notes and any findings raised.
Retrieve the supplier change log with the impact assessment outcome recorded per change.
Obtain the service review records for suppliers above the risk threshold, with agreed actions and owners.

Analysis:
Compare reports due under the schedule with reports actually received, and identify those never chased.
Read a sample of review notes to establish whether the report's content was tested or the report merely filed.
Set the date of each logged assessment against the date its change took effect.
Confirm findings raised from reports and reviews were tracked to a conclusion rather than recorded once.
Test whether the risk threshold used to call service reviews matches the tiering applied to the same suppliers elsewhere.

Output:
A due-against-received report matrix per supplier.
A list of service changes assessed after they took effect, with the interval on each.
The open actions from service reviews with their owners and ages.

templates.title: Information security for use of cloud services
templates.objective: To ensure the part of cloud security the organisation must provide for itself is identified, configured and checked, and that it can leave a service with its information.
templates.successCriteria:
Each cloud service in use is inventoried with its owner, the classification it holds and the region it runs in.
The split of responsibility with each provider is recorded, so no control rests on the assumption that the other party performs it.
A baseline exists for the organisation's own configuration of each service, and checks against it record every deviation with a disposition.
Services holding business information have an exit plan covering extraction and deletion by the provider, and unapproved cloud found in use has been inventoried.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the cloud service inventory with service, owner, data classification and region.
Collect the shared-responsibility matrix held for each inventoried service.
Gather the customer-side configuration baselines and the exit plans written per service.
Retrieve the baseline check output with its deviations and dispositions.
Obtain the unapproved-cloud review listing services found and their disposition.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory against expense records, single sign-on applications and outbound network destinations to find services in use but uninventoried.
Test the responsibility matrix for controls left unassigned, particularly logging, key management and backup.
Re-run a sample of baseline checks against the live tenant configuration and compare with the recorded result.
Judge whether each exit plan names an extraction format and a deletion confirmation rather than only a notice period.
Check that deviations close with a remediation or an accepted exception instead of carrying forward between periods.

Output:
A list of cloud services in use but absent from the inventory.
Responsibility gaps by service and control area.
Re-run baseline results set against the recorded deviations and their dispositions.

templates.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation has settled in advance who responds to an incident, by what steps and on what record, so the response is not invented while the incident runs.
templates.successCriteria:
An incident classification scheme is published with its categories, severity levels and worked examples.
Response roles are held by named people with deputies and a contact route that actually reaches them.
A handling procedure runs from detection through to closure and an incident record template captures timeline, actions and evidence.
Exercises are run against the procedure, and their findings together with the review of closed incidents produce amendments to the plan.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the incident classification scheme with its categories, severity levels and examples.
Collect the incident response role assignment sheet naming holders, deputies and contact routes.
Gather the incident handling procedure covering detection through to closure.
Retrieve the incident record template and the fields it requires.
Obtain the exercise record with scenario, participants, timings and gaps, and the review of closed incidents.

Analysis:
Check the named role holders against current staff records and test one contact route rather than reading it.
Walk the handling procedure at one severity level and identify steps with no owner or no condition for moving on.
Compare the template's required fields with what closed incident records actually contain.
Read the exercise record for the gaps it exposed and trace each to an amendment of the procedure or the role sheet.
Establish whether the review of closed incidents examined how the procedure performed, not only how the incident ended.

Output:
A role-by-role confirmation of holders, deputies and reachable contact routes.
A list of procedure steps lacking an owner or a closure condition.
The exercise and review findings with the plan amendment made against each.
