Walk the scenario through the documented response steps with the named responders
Record each step that was missing or ambiguous, pointed at a system nobody could reach, or named someone who has left
Raise a correction to the response procedure for each gap found

evidenceHint.en: Exercise report listing the gaps found and the procedure amendment raised for each

templates.title: Learning from information security incidents
templates.description: Learn from incidents to improve security
templates.objective: To ensure knowledge gained from information security incidents is converted into tracked improvements that reduce the recurrence of comparable incidents.
templates.successCriteria:
Every incident meeting the published review threshold has a completed review naming its cause and its contributing factors.
Each cause a review identifies carries an improvement action with a named owner and a current status.
Repeat causes across the period are visible in trend analysis, each with a proposed control change.
Improvement actions recorded as closed are supported by an observed change in the target system.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the post-incident review template and the written threshold stating which incidents require one.
Obtain the incident register for the period and the completed review records it produced.
Collect the improvement action register entries linked to their source incident.
Obtain the period's trend analysis of repeat incident causes.
Gather the verification results for improvement actions recorded as closed.

Analysis:
Compare the incident register against the threshold to find incidents that qualified for a review and did not receive one.
Check that each review names a cause and contributing factors rather than restating the chronology of the incident.
Trace every cause a review identified to an improvement action bearing an owner and a status.
Assess whether the trend analysis counts repeat causes and proposes a control change for each.
Re-perform the verification on a sample of closed actions by inspecting the target system.

Output:
A schedule of qualifying incidents showing which were reviewed within the period.
A traceability listing from review cause to improvement action and its verified state.
A list of repeat causes with no proposed control change and of actions closed without implementation.

title.en: Create the post-incident review format capturing cause and contributing factors

description.en: Define the questions a review must answer: what allowed the incident to occur, what allowed it to continue undetected, what worked in the response, and what changes would reduce recurrence or impact. Attach the format and the threshold of incidents it applies to.

text.en: Write the questions on what allowed the incident to occur and what allowed it to continue undetected
Add questions on what worked in the response and what changes would reduce recurrence or impact
Set the written threshold stating which incidents require a post-incident review
Attach the review template together with the threshold

evidenceHint.en: Post-incident review template plus the written threshold stating which incidents require one

title.en: Hold a post-incident review for each incident above the review threshold

description.en: Convene the responders and the affected system owners after closure, work through the review format, and record the causes and contributing factors agreed. A review is complete when the record names causes, not just a narrative of events.

text.en: Identify the incidents closed in the period that meet the review threshold
Convene the responders and the affected system owners once each incident is closed
Work through the review format and agree the causes and contributing factors
Record the review, naming the causes and contributing factors agreed

hint.en: A narrative of events is not a cause; the record has to say why the incident was possible

evidenceHint.en: Completed review record per qualifying incident, naming causes and contributing factors

title.en: Raise a tracked improvement action for each cause a review identifies

description.en: Convert every cause recorded in a review into an action with a named owner and a target, entered in the tracker rather than left in the review document. Link each action back to the incident it came from so closure can be traced.

text.en: Write the improvement action each cause recorded in a review calls for
Enter each action in the tracker with a named owner and a target date
Link each tracked action to the incident it came from
Check that no cause in a completed review is left without a tracked action

evidenceHint.en: Action register entries linked to their source incident, each with owner and status

title.en: Analyse incident causes across the period for repeat occurrences

description.en: Group the period's incidents by cause and category to find causes that recurred, and state for each repeat whether the earlier improvement action was absent, incomplete, or ineffective. Propose the control change indicated.

text.en: Group the period's incidents by cause and by category
Count the incidents behind each cause and pick out those that recurred
Trace each repeat cause to its earlier improvement action and record whether it was absent, incomplete or ineffective
Propose the control change each repeat cause indicates

evidenceHint.en: Trend analysis naming repeat causes, their incident counts, and the control change proposed for each

title.en: Confirm the improvement actions from earlier reviews were implemented

description.en: Take the actions raised from prior post-incident reviews and check the change actually landed in the system, procedure or configuration named — not merely that the ticket was closed. Record any action closed without the change taking effect.

text.en: List the improvement actions raised from prior post-incident reviews, closed ones included
Inspect the system, procedure or configuration each action names for the change itself

hint.en: A closed ticket is not evidence; look in the target system for the change it promised

text.en: Record the change observed in the target for each action
List every action closed without its change taking effect

evidenceHint.en: Verification listing each action, the change observed in the target system, and any closed-but-unimplemented actions

templates.title: Collection of evidence
templates.description: Collect and preserve evidence for incidents
templates.objective: To ensure evidence relating to information security events is acquired and preserved so that its integrity and origin remain demonstrable when it is later relied upon.
templates.successCriteria:
Each evidence type has a documented method for identifying, acquiring and preserving it.
Every collected item carries an unbroken custody record from collection to release, showing handler, time and each transfer.
Acquired items sit in the designated repository under a recorded integrity hash, reachable only by named handlers.
Re-verification reproduces the recorded hash for stored items, and every mismatch has a recorded disposition.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the evidence-handling procedure with the acquisition and preservation method recorded per evidence type.
Obtain the blank chain-of-custody record and the completed custody records for items collected in the period.
Obtain the repository listing showing item identifier, integrity hash and acquisition date.
Obtain the repository access list and the output of the most recent hash re-verification run.

Analysis:
Check the procedure covers every evidence type the organisation can expect to acquire, volatile sources included.
Follow a sample of items through their custody records looking for gaps in handler, time or transfer history.
Reconcile items recorded as collected against the repository listing to find items acquired but never deposited.
Compare the repository access list against the handlers the procedure authorises.
Examine the re-verification output for hash mismatches and confirm a disposition was recorded for each.

Output:
A custody continuity result for each item sampled.
A reconciliation of items collected against items held under a recorded hash.
A statement of hash mismatches and of repository access held outside the authorised handler list.

title.en: Document how each evidence type is identified, acquired and preserved

description.en: For each type the organisation would need to collect (disk images, memory captures, log exports, cloud audit trails, physical media), record the acquisition method, the tooling used, and how the copy is preserved so it stays usable. Attach the procedure.

text.en: List the evidence types the organisation would need to collect: disk images, memory captures, log exports, cloud audit trails, physical media
State how an item of each type is identified and recorded at the point of collection
Record the acquisition method and the tooling used for each evidence type
Record how the acquired copy of each type is preserved so it stays usable
Attach the evidence-handling procedure

evidenceHint.en: Evidence-handling procedure with an acquisition and preservation method per evidence type

title.en: Create the chain-of-custody record used for every collected item

description.en: Build the record that travels with an item: unique identifier, what it is, who collected it, when and from where, and a row for each subsequent transfer of custody. Attach the blank record and one completed example.

text.en: Define the item fields: unique identifier, what it is, who collected it, and when and where it was collected
Add a row for each later transfer of custody, naming who handed it over, who received it and when
Fill in one completed example to show how the custody record is used
Attach the blank chain-of-custody record and the completed example

evidenceHint.en: Blank chain-of-custody record plus one completed example

title.en: Record custody for each evidence item from collection through to release

description.en: Complete a custody record at the moment each item is collected and add a row at every handover, including transfers to external parties. An item with a gap in its custody chain is recorded as such rather than back-filled.

text.en: Open a custody record at the moment each evidence item is collected
Add a custody row at every handover, including transfers to external parties
Record the release of each item when it leaves the organisation's custody
Mark any gap in an item's custody chain as a gap rather than back-filling it

hint.en: A back-filled entry hides the gap; a recorded gap can still be explained to whoever relies on the item

evidenceHint.en: Custody records for the period's collected items, each showing handler, time and transfer history

title.en: Store each acquired item in the designated repository with an integrity hash

description.en: On acquisition, compute a hash of the item, record it against the item identifier, and place the item in the controlled repository with access restricted to the handling team. Attach the repository listing showing item, hash and acquisition date.

text.en: Compute a hash of each evidence item at the time of acquisition
Record the hash against the item's identifier
Place the item in the controlled evidence repository
Restrict repository access to the handling team and export the access list
Attach the repository listing with item, hash and acquisition date, and the access list

evidenceHint.en: Repository listing with item identifier, hash and acquisition date, plus the repository access list

title.en: Re-verify stored evidence against its recorded hash

description.en: Recompute the hash of each item held in the repository and compare it with the value recorded at acquisition. Report every mismatch or missing item, and record what happened to it.

text.en: Recompute the hash of every item held in the evidence repository
Compare each recomputed hash with the value recorded at acquisition
Report every mismatch and every item missing from the repository
Record what happened to each mismatched or missing item

evidenceHint.en: Verification run output listing item, expected hash, observed hash, and the disposition of each mismatch

templates.title: Information security during disruption
templates.objective: To ensure a stated minimum level of security still holds while the organisation runs in a degraded or fallback mode, and that every relaxation is authorised and later reversed.
templates.successCriteria:
Each continuity mode has a recorded list of the controls it degrades or bypasses.
A minimum security requirement is stated for every continuity mode, with the relaxations accepted alongside it.
The fallback environment enforces the access control set for it and its logs reach the central destination.
Every control relaxed during a disruption shows an authoriser, a start time and a confirmed restoration.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of continuity modes with the controls each one degrades or bypasses.
Obtain the minimum security requirements recorded per mode and the relaxations accepted with them.
Obtain the fallback environment configuration export and log samples showing delivery to the central destination.
Obtain the relaxation log for disruptions in the period and the most recent disruption test report.

Analysis:
Compare the modes listed against the continuity plans to find operating modes with no control impact recorded.
Check the fallback configuration against the access control and logging requirements written for that mode.
Trace the log samples to the central destination and confirm they are retained there for the stated period.
Review the relaxation log for entries lacking an authoriser or a restore time, and confirm restoration in the live system.
Compare each stated minimum requirement against the control state the test actually observed.

Output:
A per-mode statement of degraded controls set against the minimum requirements written for them.
A confirmation of the fallback environment's access control and log delivery posture.
A list of relaxations left unrestored and of minimum requirements the test found breached, with remediation per item.

title.en: Identify the security controls bypassed or weakened in each continuity mode

description.en: Walk each continuity and failover arrangement (alternate site, degraded mode, manual workaround, emergency access) and list the controls that stop applying or apply more weakly there — authentication, logging, segregation, monitoring. Attach the resulting list keyed by mode.

text.en: List each continuity and failover arrangement: alternate site, degraded mode, manual workaround, emergency access
Walk each arrangement and note which of authentication, logging, segregation and monitoring stop applying in it
Note the controls that still apply in each mode but more weakly than normal
Attach the list of degraded or bypassed controls keyed by continuity mode

evidenceHint.en: List of continuity modes, each with the controls that degrade or are bypassed in it

title.en: Record the minimum security requirements that must hold while operating in fallback

description.en: For each continuity mode, state which of the degraded controls must nevertheless be maintained and to what level, and which relaxations are accepted for the duration of a disruption. Attach the requirements statement with the acceptance for each relaxation.

text.en: Decide for each degraded control in each continuity mode whether it must still be maintained
State the level each maintained control must hold to while in that mode
Record the relaxations accepted for the duration of a disruption and who accepted each
Attach the minimum security requirements per mode with the acceptance for each relaxation

evidenceHint.en: Minimum security requirements per continuity mode, with the accepted relaxations recorded

title.en: Configure the fallback environment to enforce its access control and logging requirements

description.en: Apply the access restrictions, authentication and log forwarding the requirements demand to the alternate site or degraded-mode systems, so they are in place before a disruption rather than configured during one. Attach the configuration export and the log destination showing events arriving from the fallback environment.

text.en: Apply the required access restrictions and authentication to the alternate site or degraded-mode systems ahead of any disruption
Configure log forwarding from the fallback environment to the central log destination
Confirm events from the fallback environment are arriving at the central destination
Attach the fallback configuration export and log samples showing events reaching the destination

evidenceHint.en: Fallback environment configuration export plus log samples proving events reach the central destination

title.en: Record the authorisation and restoration of every control relaxed during a disruption

description.en: When a control is relaxed or emergency access granted during a disruption, log the control, who authorised it, when it started, and when normal operation was restored. Close the loop by confirming the control is back in force after the event.

text.en: Log each control relaxed or emergency access granted during a disruption, with who authorised it
Record when each relaxation started and when normal operation was restored
Check each relaxation against those accepted in the minimum requirements for that mode
Confirm after the event that every relaxed control is back in force and record the confirmation

evidenceHint.en: Relaxation log with control, authoriser, start time, restore time and the post-event confirmation

title.en: Test a disruption scenario and check the minimum requirements actually held

description.en: Invoke or simulate one continuity mode and observe whether the requirements stated for it were met — was access still restricted, were logs still captured, was segregation preserved. Record each requirement as held or breached, with the remediation for breaches.

text.en: Choose one continuity mode and invoke or simulate it
Observe whether access stayed restricted, logs were still captured and segregation was preserved
Record each stated minimum requirement for the mode as held or breached
Record the remediation for each requirement breached

evidenceHint.en: Test report comparing each stated minimum requirement to the observed control state, with remediation per breach

templates.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
templates.objective: To ensure ICT services can be restored within the recovery time and recovery point targets that the business processes depending on them actually require.
templates.successCriteria:
Every in-scope ICT service inherits a recovery time and recovery point target from the business process it supports.
Each service has a runbook giving restore steps, dependency order and the check that confirms the restore succeeded.
The backup, replication or standby arrangement provisioned for a service is capable of meeting that service's target.
Exercises record an achieved recovery time and point, and the runbook corrections they prompt are made.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the mapping of ICT services to business processes with the recovery time and point target each service inherits.
Obtain the recovery runbook held for each in-scope service.
Obtain configuration evidence for the backup, replication or standby arrangement behind each service.
Obtain exercise records showing start and finish times with the achieved recovery time and point.
Obtain the most recent reconciliation of runbooks against the ICT architecture.

Analysis:
Check the target held against each ICT service matches the one its business process requires.
Assess whether runbooks state dependency order and a success check, not restore steps alone.
Compare backup frequency, replication lag and standby capacity against the target each is meant to satisfy.
Measure achieved recovery times from the exercise records against target and confirm corrections reached the runbook.
Review the reconciliation for services holding no runbook and for runbooks naming retired systems.

Output:
A service-level table of required against achieved recovery time and recovery point.
An assessment of whether each provisioned arrangement can meet the target set for its service.
A list of services without a current runbook and of exercise corrections still outstanding.

title.en: Map each ICT service to the recovery time and recovery point its business process requires

description.en: Take the recovery objectives set for the business processes and trace them down to the ICT services, data stores and third-party dependencies each process relies on, so every service carries a target it inherited rather than one invented for it. Attach the mapping.

text.en: Collect the recovery time and recovery point objectives set for each business process
Trace each process to the ICT services, data stores and third-party dependencies it relies on
Assign each ICT service the recovery targets it inherits from the processes that depend on it

hint.en: Where several processes share a service, it inherits the tightest of their targets

text.en: Attach the service-to-process mapping with the targets each service inherited

evidenceHint.en: Service-to-process mapping showing the recovery time and recovery point target inherited by each ICT service

title.en: Write the recovery runbook for each ICT service, including dependency order

description.en: For each in-scope service, document the steps to restore it: where the backup or standby lives, the order dependencies must come up in, the credentials and access needed, and how restoration is confirmed successful. Attach the runbook set.

text.en: Record where each in-scope service's backup or standby lives
Set out the order in which the service's dependencies must be brought up
List the credentials and access the restore needs
Write the restore steps and the check that confirms the service was restored successfully
Attach the recovery runbook set

evidenceHint.en: Recovery runbook per in-scope service, showing restore steps, dependency order and the success check

title.en: Provision the redundancy and backup arrangements the recovery targets require

description.en: Where the mapped target cannot be met by the current arrangement, put the standby capacity, replication or backup frequency in place that makes it achievable, and record for each service what was provisioned. Attach the configuration evidence per service.

text.en: Compare each service's current backup, replication or standby arrangement with its mapped recovery targets
List the services whose targets the current arrangement cannot meet
Put in place the standby capacity, replication or backup frequency each listed service needs
Record what was provisioned for each service
Attach the configuration evidence per service

evidenceHint.en: Per-service configuration evidence of the backup, replication or standby arrangement supporting its target

title.en: Exercise the recovery runbook for an ICT service and record the achieved recovery time

description.en: Run the runbook against a real restore into an isolated environment, timing it end to end and checking the restored data against the recovery point target. Record where the runbook was wrong or incomplete and correct it.

text.en: Restore the service into an isolated environment by following its runbook
Time the restore end to end and compare the achieved recovery time with the target
Check the restored data against the recovery point target
Correct the runbook wherever it proved wrong or incomplete and record each correction

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record with start and finish times, achieved recovery time and point against target, and the runbook corrections made

title.en: Reconcile the recovery runbooks against the current ICT architecture

description.en: Compare the services and dependencies named in the runbooks with those actually running, and find services introduced or re-platformed since the runbooks were written that no plan covers. Record each unmatched service and the runbook raised for it.

text.en: List the ICT services and dependencies actually running in the current architecture
Compare them with the services and dependencies the recovery runbooks name
Record each service introduced or re-platformed since the runbooks were written that no runbook covers
Record each runbook that still references a retired system
Raise a runbook for each uncovered service and record the action taken against each mismatch

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation listing services with no runbook, runbooks referencing retired systems, and the action for each

templates.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
templates.description: Identify and comply with legal requirements
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation knows which legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual security obligations bind it, keeps that knowledge current, and can show each one is satisfied.
templates.successCriteria:
The obligations register names the source instrument, the jurisdiction and the affected service for every entry.
Each obligation is mapped to the controls and system owners that satisfy it, with the unmapped ones listed separately.
Every obligation names a monitoring source and the person watching it for change.
Register amendments record the date, the source that triggered them and the owners notified.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of legal, regulatory and contractual security obligations.
Obtain the obligation-to-control mapping together with the separate list of unmapped obligations.
Obtain the monitoring source and named watcher recorded against each obligation.
Obtain the obligations register change history for the period.
Obtain the compliance assessment of in-scope services against the obligations mapped to them.

Analysis:
Test the register for completeness against contracts signed and jurisdictions entered during the period.
Check the mapped control addresses the requirement the obligation states and that its system owner is in post.
Assess whether each monitoring source would surface a change and whether the watcher is still employed.
Compare register amendments against what the monitored sources published in the period.
Review the compliance assessment for services marked as meeting an obligation without supporting evidence.

Output:
A completeness result for the register against the period's new contracts and jurisdictions.
A list of obligations holding no mapped control, no system owner or no monitoring source.
A gap schedule drawn from the compliance assessment, naming the remediation owner for each gap.

title.en: Compile the register of legal, regulatory and contractual security obligations

description.en: Enumerate the obligations that bear on information security for each jurisdiction the organisation operates in and each service it delivers, drawing from statute, sector regulation and customer contracts. Record for each the source instrument and the part of the business it binds. Attach the register.

text.en: List the jurisdictions the organisation operates in and the services it delivers
Identify the information security obligations in statute and sector regulation for each jurisdiction
Identify the information security obligations in customer contracts for each service
Record for each obligation its source instrument and the part of the business it binds
Attach the obligations register

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register with source instrument, jurisdiction and affected service per entry

title.en: Map each register entry to the controls and system owners that satisfy it

description.en: For every obligation, name the control, process or system that meets it and the owner accountable for that control, so an obligation with no control behind it becomes visible. Attach the mapping and list the entries that currently map to nothing.

text.en: Name the control, process or system that meets each obligation in the register
Name the owner accountable for each of those controls
List the obligations that currently map to no control
Attach the obligation-to-control mapping with the unmapped obligations listed separately

evidenceHint.en: Obligation-to-control mapping, with the unmapped obligations listed separately

title.en: Record the monitoring source that signals a change for each obligation

description.en: For each register entry, name where a change would be noticed — regulator publication, counsel briefing, contract renewal, industry body — and who watches it. This is what keeps the register current rather than a point-in-time snapshot.

text.en: Name for each register entry where a change would be noticed: regulator publication, counsel briefing, contract renewal or industry body
Name the person who watches each monitoring source
Add the source and the watcher to the register as a column or annex
Confirm with each watcher which obligations and sources they are responsible for

evidenceHint.en: Register column or annex naming the monitoring source and the watcher for each obligation

title.en: Amend the register when a monitored source reports a changed obligation

description.en: When a monitored source reports a new or amended requirement, update the affected register entries, re-check the control mapping still satisfies the changed wording, and notify the owners whose controls are affected. Keep the change history rather than overwriting.

text.en: Update the affected register entries when a monitored source reports a new or amended requirement
Re-check that the mapped controls still satisfy the changed wording
Notify the owners whose controls are affected by the change
Log the date, the triggering source and the requirement amended in the register's change history, without overwriting earlier entries

evidenceHint.en: Register change history showing the date, the source that triggered it, the requirement amended and the owners notified

title.en: Assess each in-scope service against its mapped obligations and record gaps

description.en: Take the services in the register and test whether the mapped controls are actually operating as the obligation requires, rather than merely assigned. Record each obligation as met or gapped, with the remediation and owner for every gap.

text.en: Take each in-scope service and the obligations mapped to it
Test whether each mapped control is operating as the obligation requires

hint.en: A control assigned to an owner is not yet a control shown to operate

text.en: Record each obligation as met or gapped for the service
Assign a remediation and an owner to every gap

evidenceHint.en: Compliance assessment listing obligation, service, met/gapped status and the remediation owner per gap

templates.title: Intellectual property rights
templates.objective: To ensure software and third-party material are used only within the rights the organisation actually holds, and that the obligations attaching to those rights are honoured on release.
templates.successCriteria:
Every licensed product and third-party item in use appears in the inventory against its licence or purchase record.
Permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights are recorded per licence, and deployed installations stay within them.
Software reaches managed endpoints only through the approved acquisition route and approved repositories.
Each release ships a component manifest with resolved licences and the attribution those licences require.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of licensed software and third-party material with the licence or purchase reference per row.
Obtain the entitlement summary stating permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights per licence.
Obtain the endpoint and repository configuration restricting installation, with the approved acquisition route.
Obtain a recent build's component manifest with resolved licences and the attribution notice shipped with it.
Obtain the entitlement reconciliation and the latest scan for software absent from the inventory.

Analysis:
Check inventory rows carry a licence or purchase reference and that the reference permits the use observed.
Recount installations per product against permitted seats and confirm each over-deployment was actually resolved.
Attempt an install from an unapproved source on a sample endpoint and confirm the restriction refuses it.
Trace manifest dependencies to their resolved licences and check the shipped attribution covers them.
Review the scan output for software found outside the inventory and confirm each item received a disposition.

Output:
A licence position per product giving entitlement, deployed count and the resolution of any excess.
A result on whether installation is confined to the approved acquisition route.
A list of unlicensed or unattributed components found in builds or on endpoints, with the disposition of each.

title.en: Inventory the licensed software and third-party material in use

description.en: List the commercial software, subscriptions, datasets, media and other third-party material the organisation uses, and hold the licence, purchase record or terms of use alongside each entry. Attach the inventory with the source document referenced per row.

text.en: List the commercial software and subscriptions the organisation uses
Add the datasets, media and other third-party material in use
Hold the licence, purchase record or terms of use alongside each entry
Attach the inventory with the source document referenced on every row

evidenceHint.en: Software and third-party material inventory, each row referencing its licence or purchase record

title.en: Record the permitted seats, deployments and redistribution limits for each licence

description.en: Read the terms of each licence held and extract what it actually permits — how many users or installs, which environments, whether the material may be modified or passed to customers — so entitlement can be compared with use. Attach the entitlement summary per licence.

text.en: Read the terms of each licence held in the inventory
Extract the permitted number of users or installs and the environments each licence covers
Extract whether each licensed item may be modified or passed to customers
Attach the entitlement summary per licence

evidenceHint.en: Entitlement summary per licence stating permitted seats, environments and redistribution rights

title.en: Restrict software acquisition and installation to approved sources

description.en: Configure the endpoint and server controls so software arrives through the managed catalogue or approved repositories rather than arbitrary downloads, and route purchase requests through the procurement path that records a licence. Attach the policy configuration and the request route.

text.en: Name the managed catalogue and approved repositories software may be installed from
Configure endpoint and server controls to block installation from any other source
Route software purchase requests through the procurement path that records a licence
Attach the installation restriction configuration and the documented acquisition route

evidenceHint.en: Endpoint and repository configuration showing the installation restriction, plus the documented acquisition route

title.en: Record the open-source components in each product build with their licence obligations

description.en: Generate a component manifest for the build, resolve the licence of every dependency, and flag those carrying attribution, notice or reciprocal-licensing obligations so they can be honoured in what ships. Attach the manifest and the notice file it produces.

text.en: Generate a component manifest for the product build
Resolve the licence of every dependency in the manifest

hint.en: Include transitive dependencies, not only those the build declares directly

text.en: Flag the dependencies carrying attribution, notice or reciprocal-licensing obligations
Produce the attribution notice file that ships with the release
Attach the manifest and the notice file

evidenceHint.en: Build component manifest with resolved licence per dependency, and the attribution notice shipped with the release

title.en: Reconcile deployed installations against purchased entitlements

description.en: Count actual installs and active seats per product from the management tooling and compare them against the entitlement summary. Record every over-deployment and whether it was resolved by removing installs or buying additional licences.

text.en: Count actual installs and active seats per product from the management tooling
Compare each count with the permitted seats and installs in the entitlement summary
Record every over-deployment found
Resolve each over-deployment by removing installs or buying additional licences, and record which

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation showing installs and seats against entitlement per product, with the resolution of each over-deployment

title.en: Scan managed endpoints for software absent from the licence inventory

description.en: Run a discovery scan across managed devices and servers, subtract what the inventory accounts for, and investigate the remainder — unlicensed installs, personal copies, unapproved tooling. Record the disposition of each item found.

text.en: Run a discovery scan across managed devices and servers
Subtract the software the licence inventory accounts for from the scan results
Investigate each remaining item as an unlicensed install, a personal copy or unapproved tooling
Record the disposition of each item found

evidenceHint.en: Scan output listing software found but not in the inventory, with the disposition recorded per item

templates.title: Protection of records
templates.description: Protect records per legal and business requirements
templates.objective: To ensure records stay complete, unaltered and retrievable for as long as the requirement behind them demands, and are not destroyed before that period ends.
templates.successCriteria:
Every record class has an accountable owner, a named authoritative store and the requirement fixing its retention.
The approved retention schedule gives each class a period and the event that starts it.
Records the period gained sit under the protection recorded for their class against alteration and early destruction.
Sampled records come back complete, unaltered and readable, and each exception is logged with its resolution.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the records inventory listing each record class with its authoritative store, owner and retention requirement.
Obtain the approved retention schedule giving the period and the retention-start event per class.
Obtain the per-store evidence of the measure preventing alteration and early destruction for each class.
Obtain the period's coverage sheet for newly gained records and the records protection exception log.
Obtain the results of the retrieval sample performed on stored records.

Analysis:
Compare the inventory against the stores actually in use to find record classes held but never listed.
Check each retention period traces to the requirement cited and that its start event is determinable from the record itself.
Attempt an alteration and an early deletion in a sample store as an ordinary user and observe whether the measure holds.
Review the coverage sheet for classes whose new records fell outside the recorded protection and confirm each resolution.
Assess the retrieval results for records returned incomplete, altered or unreadable and follow the remediation raised.

Output:
An inventory completeness result measured against the stores in use.
A per-class statement of retention period, protection measure and whether the period's records fall under it.
A retrieval test result naming the exceptions found and the remediation owner for each.

title.en: Inventory the record classes held and the requirement fixing each one's retention

description.en: List each class of record the organisation holds — contracts, financial records, personnel files, audit trails, incident records — and against each one name the store holding its authoritative copy, the person accountable for it, and the specific legal, regulatory, contractual or business requirement that sets how long it must be kept. Where an information asset inventory already lists these holdings, take the classes from it rather than surveying them again; what this task adds is the requirement column. Where no external requirement applies and the period is a business decision, say so and name the decision rather than leaving the cell blank. Attach the completed inventory as the population the rest of this control works from.

text.en: List each record class held, taking the classes from the information asset inventory where it already lists them
Name the store holding each class's authoritative copy and the person accountable for it
Record the legal, regulatory, contractual or business requirement that sets how long each class must be kept
Name the business decision behind any retention period no external requirement sets, rather than leaving the cell blank
Attach the completed records inventory

evidenceHint.en: Records inventory listing each record class, the store holding its authoritative copy, its accountable owner, and the requirement fixing its retention

title.en: Publish a retention schedule giving each record class a period and the event that starts it

description.en: Turn the inventory into the schedule the rest of the organisation works from: for every record class state the retention period, the event that starts the clock — creation, contract end, employment end, case closure — and carry across the requirement behind it. The schedule settles when a record stops being protected and nothing past that point: how the information is then removed, and from which holdings, is worked out against this schedule by the information deletion control rather than restated here, so the schedule carries no disposal method column. Attach the approved schedule.

text.en: Set a retention period for every record class in the inventory
State the event that starts each class's retention clock, such as creation, contract end, employment end or case closure
Carry across from the inventory the requirement behind each period
Leave disposal methods out of the schedule

hint.en: How information is removed after the period is settled by the information deletion control

text.en: Obtain approval of the schedule and publish it where the organisation works from it
Attach the approved retention schedule

evidenceHint.en: Approved retention schedule giving the period, the event that starts it and the requirement behind it for every record class

title.en: Restrict alteration and early destruction of records for the length of their retention period

description.en: For each store named in the inventory, put in place what stops a record being altered or destroyed before its retention date — write-once storage, a retention lock, withdrawal of delete rights from routine operator accounts, a locked cabinet for paper originals — and record which measure protects which record class. Where a store cannot enforce it, record the compensating measure relied on instead rather than leaving the class unaddressed. Attach the configuration exports, permission listings or written descriptions that show what is actually in force for each class.

text.en: Take each store named in the inventory and the record classes it holds
Put in place the measure preventing early alteration or destruction: write-once storage, retention lock, withdrawn delete rights or a locked cabinet
Record which measure protects which record class
Record the compensating measure relied on wherever a store cannot enforce protection
Attach the configuration exports, permission listings or descriptions showing what is in force for each class

evidenceHint.en: Per-store record of the measure protecting each record class from alteration and early destruction, with the exports, permission listings or descriptions evidencing each

title.en: Place the records each class gained this period under the protection recorded for it

description.en: For every record class that gained records during the period, confirm the new records sit in the store named for that class and under the measure recorded against it, and list those that do not — records left in a working area, an unprotected export, a mailbox or a local drive — with what was done about each. The output is coverage per record class for the period, not a listing of individual records, so a class that gained nothing is recorded as such rather than omitted.

text.en: Identify which record classes gained records during the period
Record each class that gained nothing as such rather than omitting it
Confirm the new records in each class sit in its named store under its recorded protection
List records found outside protection, such as in a working area, an unprotected export, a mailbox or a local drive, and what was done
Compile the coverage sheet with one line per record class for the period

evidenceHint.en: Coverage sheet for the period: each record class, whether the records it gained sit under its recorded protection, and the resolution of each that did not

title.en: Record every record destroyed early, altered without authority, or missing when called for

description.en: Capture each occasion in the period when a record still inside its retention period was destroyed before its date, changed without authority, or could not be produced when it was asked for. Give the record class, what happened, how it came to light, and what was done — recovery from another copy, correction of the protection that failed, or acceptance of the loss with its consequence stated. Where nothing occurred, close the period with a nil entry, so an empty log reads as a period examined rather than a period skipped.

text.en: Capture each occasion a record within its retention period was destroyed early, altered without authority, or could not be produced
Give the record class, what happened and how it came to light for each entry
Record the resolution: recovery from another copy, correction of the failed protection, or acceptance of the loss with its consequence
Close the period with a nil entry where nothing occurred

hint.en: A nil entry shows the period was examined; an empty log cannot be told apart from one nobody kept

evidenceHint.en: Records protection exception log for the period, one entry per early destruction, unauthorised alteration or failure to produce, with its resolution — or a nil entry for the period

title.en: Retrieve a sample of records and confirm each is complete, unaltered and readable

description.en: Draw a sample across the classes in the inventory, weighted towards the longest retention periods, legacy media and obsolete file formats, and retrieve each record. Confirm it opens, that it is complete against what the class says it should contain, and that it carries no unexplained change since it was filed. Where a record cannot be read or has lost content, record the migration, format conversion or recovery needed and who owns it. Attach the results listing what was sampled and the outcome of each retrieval.

text.en: Draw a sample across the record classes, weighted towards the longest retention periods, legacy media and obsolete formats
Retrieve each sampled record and confirm it opens
Check each record is complete against what its class should contain and carries no unexplained change since filing
Record the migration, format conversion or recovery needed for any unreadable or incomplete record, and its owner
Attach the retrieval results listing what was sampled and the outcome of each retrieval

evidenceHint.en: Retrieval results listing the records sampled, whether each was complete, unaltered and readable, and the remediation raised for each failure

templates.title: Privacy and protection of PII
templates.objective: To ensure personally identifiable information is processed only for recorded purposes under the privacy obligations binding each activity, including where it crosses a border.
templates.successCriteria:
Every processing activity handling PII is recorded with its PII categories, purpose, systems and controller or processor role.
Each processing activity carries the privacy obligations that bind it, drawn from the obligations register.
Every cross-border PII flow names its destination, its recipient and the safeguard relied on.
Requests from individuals about their PII reach the live intake and are logged with the action taken and a closure date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the record of processing activities covering PII categories, purpose, systems and the role held.
Obtain the privacy obligations register with its mapping to processing activities.
Obtain the transfer register naming destination, recipient and safeguard for each cross-border flow.
Obtain the request-handling procedure with the configuration export showing live intake and routing.
Obtain the period's request log and the latest assessment of activities against their obligations.

Analysis:
Reconcile the processing record against the systems known to hold PII to find processing nobody recorded.
Check the obligations mapped to an activity match its jurisdictions, its purposes and the role the organisation holds.
Confirm a safeguard is in force for every listed transfer and look for PII flows absent from the transfer register.
Trace a test request through the live intake and confirm it routes to the handler the procedure names.
Measure logged requests against their response deadlines and examine the action taken on a sample.

Output:
A processing record completeness result against the systems holding PII.
A transfer schedule stating the safeguard relied on and naming any flow without one.
A request-handling result covering intake, timeliness and outcome, with the assessment's gaps and their owners.

title.en: Record every processing activity that handles personally identifiable information

description.en: Enumerate the activities in which the organisation collects, uses, stores or shares PII. For each, record the categories of PII involved, the purpose, the systems and storage locations holding it, and whether the organisation acts as controller or processor. Engineering supplies the system and storage detail. Attach the completed processing record.

text.en: Enumerate the activities in which the organisation collects, uses, stores or shares PII
Record the categories of PII and the purpose for each processing activity
Obtain from engineering the systems and storage locations holding the PII for each activity
Record whether the organisation acts as controller or processor for each activity
Attach the completed processing record

evidenceHint.en: Processing record listing each activity with PII categories, purpose, systems and controller/processor role

title.en: Register the privacy obligations applying to each processing activity

description.en: Identify the privacy legislation, regulator guidance and customer contract clauses that bind each processing activity in the jurisdictions where it takes place, and map each obligation to the activities it applies to. This is what later assessments are measured against, so an obligation with no activity mapped to it, or an activity with no obligation, must be explained. Attach the register.

text.en: Identify the privacy legislation, regulator guidance and customer contract clauses in each jurisdiction where processing takes place
Map each privacy obligation to the processing activities it binds
Explain any obligation with no activity mapped to it and any activity with no obligation
Attach the privacy obligations register

evidenceHint.en: Obligations register mapping each privacy obligation to the processing activities it binds

title.en: Document the safeguard relied on for each cross-border transfer of PII

description.en: For every flow of PII out of the jurisdiction where it was collected — including onward flows to sub-processors and support access from other regions — record the destination, the recipient, and the mechanism relied on to permit the transfer. Where the review finds no cross-border flows, record that conclusion and how it was reached. Attach the transfer register.

text.en: Trace each flow of PII out of the jurisdiction where it was collected
Add onward flows to sub-processors and support access from other regions
Record the destination, the recipient and the mechanism relied on to permit each transfer
Record the conclusion and how it was reached where no cross-border flows are found
Attach the transfer register

evidenceHint.en: Transfer register listing destination, recipient and the safeguard relied on for each cross-border PII flow

title.en: Implement the handling route for requests from individuals about their PII

description.en: Define and stand up the path a request takes from receipt to closure: where requests arrive, how the requester's identity is verified, who searches which systems, and who approves the response. Configure the intake channel and the routing so a request cannot sit unassigned. Attach the procedure and evidence the intake channel is live.

text.en: Set where requests from individuals arrive and how the requester's identity is verified
Assign who searches which systems and who approves the response
Configure the intake channel and routing so no request can sit unassigned
Test the intake with a sample request to show the channel is live
Attach the request-handling procedure and a screenshot or configuration export of the live intake

evidenceHint.en: Request-handling procedure plus a screenshot or configuration export showing the live intake and routing

title.en: Log every request received from an individual about their PII and its outcome

description.en: Maintain the log of requests handled in the period: date received, request type, systems searched, action taken, date closed. The log is what shows the route in the previous task is actually being used rather than merely documented, so it should also record requests that were refused and the reason.

text.en: Log each request from an individual on receipt with the date and the request type
Record the systems searched and the action taken for each request
Record the closure date of each request
Log refused requests with the reason for refusal

evidenceHint.en: Request log for the period, one row per request with receipt date, type, action taken and closure date

title.en: Assess each processing activity against the obligations mapped to it

description.en: Walk the processing record against the obligations register and judge, per activity, whether the obligations mapped to it are being met — checking the PII actually held against the purpose recorded, and the safeguards in place against those the obligations require. Record each gap with an owner and a remediation action. Attach the assessment.

text.en: Walk the processing record against the obligations register, activity by activity
Compare the PII actually held with the purpose recorded for the activity

hint.en: Look at the data in the systems, not at the description in the processing record

text.en: Compare the safeguards in place with those the mapped obligations require
Record each gap with an owner and a remediation action
Attach the assessment covering every processing activity

evidenceHint.en: Assessment covering every processing activity, with gaps found, owners assigned and remediation actions

templates.title: Independent review of information security
templates.objective: To obtain an opinion on the information security management approach from someone outside the function that operates it, and to act on what that opinion finds.
templates.successCriteria:
The terms of reference state the review scope, the reviewer's access rights and the criterion by which independence is judged.
The review programme sets an interval, names the next review and lists the events that trigger one out of cycle.
The review report ties each finding to the evidence the reviewer examined.
Management holds a recorded decision against every finding, and findings close only on verified evidence.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the terms of reference for the independent review, including the independence criterion it sets.
Obtain the review programme showing the interval, the next scheduled review and the out-of-cycle triggers.
Obtain the most recent independent review report with its findings and their supporting evidence.
Obtain the minutes or management record showing the report was presented and decisions taken.
Obtain the findings tracker with owner, action, target date and closure evidence.

Analysis:
Test the reviewer against the independence criterion, including any reporting line into the function reviewed.
Check the review covered the scope stated and that the reviewer received the access the terms of reference grant.
Compare the review date against the programme interval and look for triggering events that passed without a review.
Verify each report finding has a recorded management decision rather than a general acknowledgement of the report.
Test closed findings against their closure evidence and judge whether that evidence demonstrates the change.

Output:
An independence conclusion for the reviewer who performed the review.
A timeliness result for the review against its programme and its out-of-cycle triggers.
A findings disposition schedule giving management decision, closure evidence and any finding closed without it.

title.en: Define the scope of the independent review and who is eligible to perform it

description.en: Write the terms of reference: which policies, processes, systems and controls the review covers, what evidence the reviewer may request, and the independence criterion the reviewer must satisfy — that they do not manage or operate the area under review. Naming the criterion in advance is what stops the review being staffed with the people who run the controls. Attach the agreed terms of reference.

text.en: List the policies, processes, systems and controls the independent review covers
State the evidence the reviewer may request
Write the independence criterion: the reviewer does not manage or operate the area under review
Agree the terms of reference with the management body commissioning the review
Attach the agreed terms of reference

evidenceHint.en: Terms of reference stating review scope, reviewer access rights and the independence criterion

title.en: Set the review programme, including the events that trigger a review out of cycle

description.en: Record when reviews take place — the planned interval between them and the next scheduled date — and list the changes significant enough to trigger a review before that date, such as a major system migration, a change in regulatory scope, or a serious incident. Attach the approved programme.

text.en: Set the planned interval between independent reviews and the next scheduled date
List the changes that trigger a review out of cycle, such as a major system migration, a change in regulatory scope or a serious incident
Obtain management approval of the review programme
Attach the approved review programme

evidenceHint.en: Review programme showing the interval, the next scheduled review and the events triggering an out-of-cycle review

title.en: Carry out the independent review and issue a report of the findings

description.en: Have the reviewer named under the independence criterion execute the review across the scope in the terms of reference, examining evidence rather than relying on assertions from control owners. The report should state what was examined, the method used, and each finding with the evidence supporting it. Attach the issued report.

text.en: Confirm the reviewer meets the independence criterion before the review starts
Examine evidence across the scope in the terms of reference

hint.en: Assertions from control owners are not evidence; the reviewer looks at the records themselves

text.en: Record what was examined and the method used
Write each finding with the evidence supporting it
Issue the review report and attach it

evidenceHint.en: Independent review report stating scope, method examined, and each finding with its supporting evidence

title.en: Present the review report to management and record the decisions taken on it

description.en: Put the report to the management body that owns information security, and minute what was decided for each finding — accepted with a remediation action, accepted as a risk, or disputed with the reason. A report filed without a management decision leaves the findings owned by nobody.

text.en: Put the review report on the agenda of the management body that owns information security
Present the report and take a decision on each finding
Minute each decision as accepted with a remediation action, accepted as a risk, or disputed with the reason
Assign an owner to each remediation action accepted

evidenceHint.en: Minutes or management record showing the report was presented and the decision recorded against each finding

title.en: Track each review finding through to verified closure

description.en: Maintain the tracker carrying the findings from the report: owner, agreed action, target date, and the evidence that closed it. A finding is closed only when someone has confirmed the fix, not when the owner says the work is done. Attach the tracker showing the current state of every finding from the latest review.

text.en: Enter every finding from the latest review in the tracker with its owner, agreed action and target date
Collect the closure evidence when an owner reports the work done
Have someone other than the owner confirm the fix before the finding is closed
Attach the findings tracker showing the current state of every finding

evidenceHint.en: Findings tracker with owner, action, target date and the closure evidence for each finding

templates.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
templates.objective: To ensure managers routinely verify that their own areas operate the way the security policies and standards require, and that failures become tracked nonconformities.
templates.successCriteria:
Every security policy and standard names the area checked against it and the manager accountable for that check.
Each check defines the items inspected, the sample taken and the criterion by which a pass is judged.
Checks measurable from system data run automatically, each mapped to the policy requirement it covers.
Every failed check has a nonconformity record naming cause, corrective action, owner and target date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the mapping of policies and standards to areas of responsibility and responsible managers.
Obtain the check definition per policy giving items inspected, sample and pass criterion.
Obtain the automated rule or query definitions with the policy requirement each one covers.
Obtain the completed compliance check records for the period and the nonconformity records raised from them.
Obtain the coverage comparison of checks performed against the policy mapping.

Analysis:
Check the managers named in the mapping hold the areas assigned to them and are currently in post.
Assess whether each pass criterion is objective enough that two managers would reach the same verdict.
Re-perform a sample of the automated rules and compare the result to the record the manager filed.
Confirm every failed check produced a nonconformity record and that its recorded cause goes past the symptom.
Review the coverage comparison for policies or areas unchecked in the period and the reason offered for each.

Output:
A coverage statement of policies checked against policies mapped for the period.
A re-performance result for the sampled checks set against the records filed.
A nonconformity schedule with cause, corrective action and status, naming failed checks that raised none.

title.en: Map each security policy and standard to the manager whose area is checked against it

description.en: List the policies, rules and standards in force, and against each one name the area of responsibility it applies to and the manager who checks compliance within that area. A policy with no area mapped to it will never be checked, so the gaps this exposes are the point of the exercise. Attach the completed mapping.

text.en: List the security policies, rules and standards in force
Name the area of responsibility each policy or standard applies to
Name the manager who checks compliance within each area
List the policies left with no area or manager mapped to them
Attach the completed policy-to-manager mapping

evidenceHint.en: Mapping of each policy and standard to its area of responsibility and the responsible manager

title.en: Define what a manager inspects to judge compliance with each policy

description.en: For each policy in the mapping, write down the check: what the manager looks at, how much of it (full population or a stated sample size), and the criterion that separates a pass from a failure. Without a stated criterion, two managers checking the same policy will reach different verdicts and neither result is comparable. Attach the check definitions.

text.en: Write down for each mapped policy what the manager looks at
State how much is inspected, the full population or a stated sample size
Set the criterion that separates a pass from a failure

hint.en: Without a stated criterion, two managers checking the same policy reach verdicts that cannot be compared

text.en: Attach the check definitions

evidenceHint.en: Check definition per policy giving the items inspected, the sample, and the pass criterion

title.en: Automate the compliance checks that can be measured from system data

description.en: For those policy requirements a system can evaluate directly — configuration baselines, patch levels, access rights, encryption settings — build the queries or tooling rules that measure conformance and report exceptions, and record which policy requirement each rule covers. Requirements no rule can cover stay on the manual checks defined above. Attach the rule definitions and their coverage mapping.

text.en: Identify the policy requirements a system can evaluate directly, such as configuration baselines, patch levels, access rights and encryption
Build the queries or tooling rules that measure conformance and report exceptions
Record which policy requirement each rule covers
Mark the requirements no rule covers as remaining on the manual checks
Attach the rule definitions and their coverage mapping

evidenceHint.en: Automated rule or query definitions with the mapping showing which policy requirement each one covers

title.en: Record each manager's compliance check result for the period

description.en: Collect the completed checks for the period: area checked, policy checked against, date, what was sampled, and the result. This is the record that shows the checks were performed by the responsible manager rather than assumed, so a check not returned is itself a finding to chase.

text.en: Collect the completed compliance checks returned for the period
Record for each check the area, the policy, the date, what was sampled and the result
Confirm each check was performed by the manager responsible for that area
Chase every check not returned and record it as a finding

evidenceHint.en: Completed compliance check records for the period, one per area and policy, with sample and result

title.en: Raise a nonconformity record for every failed check, with its cause and corrective action

description.en: Where a check fails or an automated rule reports an exception, open a record capturing what did not conform, why it happened, the corrective action agreed, its owner and target date. Closing the individual exception without recording the cause leaves the same failure free to recur next period.

text.en: Open a nonconformity record for every failed check and every exception an automated rule reports
Reference in each record the manual check or automated rule that raised it
Record what did not conform and why it happened

hint.en: Record the cause, not only the fix; closing the exception alone leaves the failure free to recur

text.en: Agree the corrective action with its owner and target date

evidenceHint.en: Nonconformity records for the period, each with cause, corrective action, owner and target date

title.en: Compare check coverage against the policy mapping and list what went unchecked

description.en: Take the checks actually recorded this period and set them against the full mapping of policies to areas, then list every policy or area with no check performed and the reason. Coverage is the measure that stops the compliance regime quietly shrinking to the few areas that always report. Attach the coverage comparison.

text.en: List the compliance checks actually recorded this period
Set them against the full mapping of policies to areas
List every policy or area with no check performed and the reason
Attach the coverage comparison

evidenceHint.en: Coverage comparison naming every policy or area with no check recorded in the period, and the reason

templates.title: Documented operating procedures
templates.objective: To ensure the activities that keep systems and facilities running are performed the same way by whoever is on duty, from instructions matching the systems as they now stand.
templates.successCriteria:
Every operational activity identified as needing a documented procedure has one written.
Operators can reach the procedures for their activities, and edit rights sit only with the procedure owners.
A change to an underlying system or process is followed by a revision of the procedures covering it.
A walkthrough with the operator who performs the activity finds the procedure matches what the work involves.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of operational activities with the facility or system each covers and whether a procedure exists.
Obtain the procedure documents written for the activities the list flagged as undocumented.
Obtain the repository location and a permissions export showing operator read access and restricted edit rights.
Obtain the procedure version history for the period with the change that prompted each revision.
Obtain the walkthrough records naming the operator and the discrepancies found.

Analysis:
Compare the activity list against shift handovers and change records to find work performed with no listed procedure.
Check each procedure covers start, run, restart and failure handling rather than the routine path alone.
Test operator access to the repository and confirm edit rights stop at the named procedure owners.
Correlate the period's system changes against procedure revisions to find procedures left describing the old system.
Review the walkthrough records and confirm each discrepancy found reached the published procedure.

Output:
A coverage result of listed operational activities against procedures actually held.
An access and edit-rights result for the procedure repository.
A currency result correlating system changes to revisions, naming walkthrough discrepancies still uncorrected.

title.en: List the operational activities that require a documented procedure

description.en: Enumerate the activities performed on the information processing facilities — system start-up and shutdown, backup and restore, batch and job scheduling, media handling, patching and deployment, monitoring response — and record for each whether a procedure exists today and where it is held. The list of activities with no procedure is the work queue for the next task. Attach the list.

text.en: Enumerate the operational activities: start-up and shutdown, backup and restore, job scheduling, media handling, patching and deployment, monitoring response
Record the facility or system each activity is performed on
Record whether a procedure exists today for each activity and where it is held
Mark the activities with no procedure as the drafting work queue
Attach the list of operational activities

evidenceHint.en: List of operational activities with the facility or system each covers and whether a procedure exists

title.en: Write a procedure for each listed activity that has none

description.en: Produce the missing procedures. Each one should carry the steps in the order performed, the prerequisites and access needed to start, what to do when a step fails, and who to escalate to — enough for a competent operator who has not performed the activity before to complete it. Attach the drafted procedures.

text.en: Take each activity the list flagged as having no procedure
Write the steps in the order they are performed
Add the prerequisites and access needed to start, what to do when a step fails, and who to escalate to
Check each draft could be followed by a competent operator who has not performed the activity before
Attach the drafted procedures

evidenceHint.en: The drafted procedure documents, covering every activity the list flagged as undocumented

title.en: Publish the procedures where operators can reach them and limit who may edit them

description.en: Put the procedures in a single location the operators who need them can access — including during an outage, where the procedure covers recovery — and restrict edit rights to their owners so the operating instruction cannot be altered by anyone reading it. Attach the repository location and the access and edit permissions on it.

text.en: Choose a single location operators can reach, including during an outage for recovery procedures
Publish every operating procedure to that location
Restrict edit rights on each procedure to its owner
Attach the repository location and a permissions export showing operator read access and restricted edit rights

evidenceHint.en: Repository location plus a permissions export showing read access for operators and restricted edit rights

title.en: Update the affected procedure whenever its underlying system or process changes

description.en: When a change lands on a facility covered by a procedure, revise the procedure in the same change and record the new version. The evidence for the period is the version history: it shows procedures moving in step with the systems they describe rather than describing a configuration that has since been replaced.

text.en: Identify the procedures affected when a change lands on a covered facility
Revise each affected procedure in the same change
Record the new version with the change that prompted it
Compare the period's changes with the version history to find changes with no matching revision

evidenceHint.en: Procedure version history for the period, showing each revision and the change that prompted it

title.en: Walk each procedure through with the operator who performs the activity

description.en: Sit with the operator and follow the written procedure step by step against how the activity is actually carried out, noting every step that is wrong, missing, out of order, or routinely skipped. Record the discrepancies found and the correction made to the document. Attach the walkthrough records.

text.en: Sit with the operator who performs the activity and follow the written procedure step by step
Compare each written step with how the activity is actually carried out
Note every step that is wrong, missing, out of order or routinely skipped
Correct the procedure for each discrepancy found
Attach the walkthrough record naming the operator, the discrepancies and the corrections

evidenceHint.en: Walkthrough record per procedure naming the operator, the discrepancies found and the corrections made

templates.title: Screening
templates.objective: To ensure the background of everyone given access to organisational information is verified to the degree their role warrants, before that access is granted.
templates.successCriteria:
Every role carries a sensitivity level and the verification types that level attracts.
Checks performed in a jurisdiction stay within what it permits, under a recorded consent basis and retention limit.
Agency and contractor staff are screened on the same terms as direct hires.
Access is granted only once a screening result has been adjudicated and recorded for that person.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the role-to-check matrix listing roles, sensitivity levels and the verification types required.
Obtain the per-jurisdiction screening statement covering lawful checks, consent basis and retention limits.
Obtain the screening procedure naming initiator, performer, adjudicator and the access-grant point.
Obtain the screening register for the period with checks run, dates and adjudication decisions.
Obtain the joiner and contractor population for the period and the organisation's own sample test over it.

Analysis:
Reconcile the roles in the matrix against the roles the HR system holds, contractor engagements included.
Compare the checks actually run in each jurisdiction against what that jurisdiction's statement permits.
Compare each person's adjudication date against the date their access was granted.
Examine adjudications where a check returned an adverse result and confirm the decision was taken at the level required.
Re-perform the sample test on an independent selection of joiners and compare the exceptions found and resolved.
Test held screening results against the retention limit to find results kept beyond it.

Output:
A schedule of the period's joiners giving checks run, adjudication date and access-grant date.
A list of people granted access before adjudication and of roles screened below their matrix requirement.
A jurisdiction result covering permitted checks, consent basis and retention of results.

title.en: List the roles requiring background verification and the checks each attracts

description.en: Classify every role, employee and contractor alike, by the sensitivity of the information and systems it reaches, then record which verification types (identity, right to work, employment history, qualifications, criminal record, financial) apply at each sensitivity level. Attach the role-to-check matrix, with the sensitivity rationale for any role attracting checks beyond identity.

text.en: List every role in the organisation, employee and contractor alike, with the information and systems each reaches

hint.en: Contractor and agency roles belong in the matrix too; they are the rows most often left out

text.en: Assign each role a sensitivity level from the most sensitive information or system it reaches
Record which verification types apply at each sensitivity level, from identity and right to work to criminal record and financial checks
Write the sensitivity rationale for every role that attracts checks beyond identity
Attach the role-to-check matrix showing each role, its sensitivity level and the verification types it attracts

evidenceHint.en: Role-to-check matrix listing every role, its sensitivity level and the verification types it attracts

text.en: List every country the organisation hires in
