templates.title: Terms and conditions of employment
templates.description: Include security responsibilities in employment terms
templates.objective: To ensure everyone who reaches organisational information is bound by written security obligations suited to how they are engaged, accepted before they begin work.
templates.successCriteria:
Every contract and engagement type through which people reach information is listed with a named owner.
Each template carries the clauses mapped to it, or a recorded and approved reason for the omission.
New starters hold a signed acceptance recording their engagement type and the clause-set version accepted.
Staff remaining on superseded terms are identified, with the clauses they lack named and a re-papering plan running.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of contract and engagement templates in use with the owner of each.
Obtain the approved security clause set and the obligation recorded against each clause.
Obtain the clause-to-template mapping, including the deliberate omissions and their stated reason.
Obtain the acceptance records for the period's starters with engagement type and clause-set version.
Obtain the gap list of staff on superseded terms together with the re-papering plan.

Analysis:
Compare the template list against the engagement types HR and procurement actually issued in the period.
Read a sample of live contracts and confirm the clauses they carry match the mapping, not just the mapping itself.
Check each recorded omission carries a reason and an approval rather than a bare note.
Reconcile the period's starters against acceptance records to find people at work without signed security terms.
Test the re-papering plan for target dates already passed with staff still on the superseded clause set.

Output:
A template coverage result against the engagement types actually issued.
A starter acceptance schedule naming anyone working without a recorded acceptance.
A re-papering position giving staff on superseded terms, the clauses they lack and the plan's status.

title.en: List every contract and engagement type through which people reach your information

description.en: Enumerate the paper that binds people to the organisation: employment contracts by country, fixed-term and intern agreements, contractor and agency terms, and any letter of engagement. Record the template owner for each. Attach the list, which becomes the population the security clauses must be inserted into.

text.en: List the employment contract templates in use in each country
Add the fixed-term, intern, contractor and agency agreements and any letters of engagement in use
Record the owner of each contract and engagement template
Attach the template list as the population the security clauses must go into

evidenceHint.en: List of contract and engagement templates in use, with the owner of each

title.en: Draft the security clauses that employment terms must carry

description.en: With Legal, write the clause set stating the individual's information security obligations: confidentiality, acceptable use of systems and data, handling of classified information, return of assets, the consequences of disregard, and which duties survive the engagement. Attach the approved clause set with a note of the obligation each clause carries.

text.en: Draft with Legal the clauses on confidentiality, acceptable use of systems and data, and handling of classified information
Add clauses on the return of assets and the consequences of disregarding the security obligations
Mark which security duties survive the end of the engagement
Note against each clause the obligation it imposes on the individual
Obtain approval of the clause set and attach it with the obligation noted per clause

evidenceHint.en: Approved security clause set with the obligation each clause imposes

title.en: Insert the approved clauses into each contract template on the list

description.en: Work through the template population and place the clauses into each, adapting wording where a jurisdiction or engagement type requires it. Attach the updated templates plus a mapping showing which clause landed in which template, and record any template where a clause was deliberately omitted and why.

text.en: Place the approved security clauses into each template on the contract list
Adapt clause wording where a jurisdiction or engagement type requires it
Record each template where a clause was deliberately omitted, with the reason
Draw up the mapping showing which clause landed in which template
Attach the updated templates together with the clause-to-template mapping

evidenceHint.en: Updated templates plus a clause-to-template mapping, including deliberate omissions and their reason

title.en: Record each new starter's signed acceptance of the security terms

description.en: As each person joins, file the signed contract or separate acknowledgement evidencing they accepted the security obligations, and note the version of the clause set they signed. Attach the acceptance record for the period so any starter without one is visible.

text.en: File each new starter's signed contract or separate security acknowledgement as they join
Note the clause-set version, engagement type and signature date for each starter
Compare the acceptance record against the period's starters and flag anyone with no signed acceptance
Attach the acceptance record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance record for the period: person, engagement type, clause-set version, signature date

title.en: Compare contracts held for existing staff against the current clause set

description.en: Check what people already engaged actually signed against the clause set now approved, and identify who is on superseded terms. Attach the gap list naming the affected people or cohorts, the clauses they lack, and the plan for re-papering or obtaining a supplementary acknowledgement.

text.en: List the clause-set version each person already engaged actually signed
Compare each signed version with the clause set now approved and identify who is on superseded terms
Record the clauses each affected person or cohort lacks
Agree for each gap whether to re-paper the contract or obtain a supplementary acknowledgement
Attach the gap list with the affected people or cohorts and the re-papering plan

evidenceHint.en: Gap list of staff on superseded terms, the missing clauses, and the re-papering plan

templates.title: Information security awareness, education and training
templates.objective: To ensure every person working for the organisation receives, and can be shown to have received, the security instruction their particular duties call for.
templates.successCriteria:
Each workforce audience has a recorded topic set and repeat interval, with the reason it was separated out.
Every audience-topic pairing names current material and the owner who keeps it aligned with policy.
Completion is evidenced in the form agreed for that topic, and outstanding names are closed or excepted.
The measure of changed conduct is reported, and material is either amended or recorded as standing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the audience-to-topic map with each audience's repeat interval and the reason it was separated out.
Obtain the inventory of material, its owners, and the date each was last checked against current policy.
Obtain the written statement of what counts as evidence that a person has covered a topic, and who holds it.
Obtain the period's completion record and the outstanding list with its escalations.
Obtain the effectiveness assessment for the period.

Analysis:
Sample roles and confirm each sits in an audience whose topic set matches the duties that role performs.
Trace each topic to named material and confirm the owner's last check post-dates the most recent policy change.
Reperform the completion count for one audience from the underlying evidence rather than from the summary.
Follow outstanding names from the earliest period shown to a closure date or a recorded exception with an approver.
Test whether the effectiveness measure reports conduct rather than attendance, and whether its result drove the change or the stated conclusion.

Output:
Coverage statement per audience: topics required, topics delivered, people outstanding.
Schedule of material whose owner check pre-dates the current policy text.
Exception listing of outstanding names carried across more than one period.
List of effectiveness measures reporting attendance only, with the conduct measure recommended for each.

title.en: Split the workforce into audiences and record the security topics each one needs

description.en: Group people by what their work exposes — everyone, those who build or administer systems, those who handle the most sensitive information, those who decide what happens to it — and for each group record the topics it must cover, the depth expected, and how often a topic is repeated. Attach the audience-to-topic map, including the reason each specialised audience was separated out and which topics apply to contractors and temporary staff as well as employees.

text.en: Group the workforce into audiences by what their work exposes: everyone, system builders and administrators, sensitive-information handlers, decision-makers
Record the security topics each audience must cover and the depth expected
Set how often each topic is repeated for each audience
Write down why each specialised audience was separated out
Mark which topics apply to contractors and temporary staff as well as employees
Attach the audience-to-topic map

evidenceHint.en: Audience-to-topic map with the repeat interval and the reason each audience was separated out

title.en: Name the material that covers each topic and who keeps it current

description.en: Work down the map and attach to every audience-topic pairing a specific piece of material — a session, a written brief, a walkthrough, a purchased course, whatever you actually use — naming its owner and the date it was last checked against your own policies rather than generic advice. Attach the inventory; any pairing with nothing behind it is the gap to close first, and should be listed as such.

text.en: Name the session, brief, walkthrough or course behind each audience-topic pairing on the map
Record the owner who keeps each piece of training material current
Check each piece of material against the organisation's own policies rather than generic advice, and record the date
List every audience-topic pairing with nothing behind it as a gap to close first
Attach the training material inventory

evidenceHint.en: Inventory naming the material behind every audience-topic pairing, its owner, and the date last checked against current policy

title.en: Decide what counts as evidence that a person has covered a topic

description.en: Before delivery starts, write down what will be accepted as proof for each topic — an attendance record, a signed acknowledgement, an assessment result, a supervisor's confirmation — and who holds it. This keeps the completion record comparable whether a topic is delivered in a room, at a desk, or in writing, and stops the record depending on the way the topic happened to be delivered. Attach the statement of accepted evidence per topic.

text.en: List for each topic the proof that will be accepted: attendance record, signed acknowledgement, assessment result or supervisor confirmation
Name who holds each form of accepted training evidence
Confirm the accepted proof for a topic is the same whether it is delivered in a room, at a desk or in writing

hint.en: Proof tied to one delivery method stops the completion record being comparable when the method changes

text.en: Fix the statement of accepted evidence before delivery starts and attach it

evidenceHint.en: Written statement of the evidence accepted for each topic and who holds it

title.en: Record each delivery of a topic and who received it

description.en: As each topic is delivered, capture the date, the audience it was aimed at, the people who took it, and the evidence held for each, including new joiners covering their induction topics. Attach the completion record for the period, laid out so that a person who has not yet covered a topic their audience requires is visible on the face of it rather than inferred by cross-referencing.

text.en: Capture the date and the intended audience each time a topic is delivered
Record who took the topic and the evidence held for each person
Add new joiners to the completion record as they cover their induction topics
Lay out the record by person against required topics so anyone not yet covered shows without cross-referencing
Attach the training completion record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Completion record for the period: person, audience, topic, delivery date and the evidence held

title.en: Pursue the people whose required topics are still outstanding

description.en: Take the outstanding names from the completion record, raise each with the person's manager, and follow it to either completion or a recorded exception carrying a reason and an end date. Attach the outstanding list for the period showing how long each name has been overdue, the escalation made, and the date it closed.

text.en: Take the names with outstanding required topics from the completion record
Raise each outstanding name with the person's manager
Follow each name to completion or to a recorded exception with a reason and an end date
Record how long each name has been overdue, the escalation made and the date it closed
Attach the outstanding training list for the period

evidenceHint.en: Outstanding list per period with the escalation made and the closure date or recorded exception for each name

title.en: Judge whether the awareness and training programme is changing conduct

description.en: Pick a measure that observes what people do rather than that they attended, and state why it is a fair proxy for the behaviour the programme was meant to produce. Record the result for this period, set against the previous period where there is one and stated as the baseline where there is not. Then say what follows from it: the audience or topic whose material you are changing and what is changing, or a recorded conclusion that the material stands as it is, with the reason for that conclusion. Attach the assessment naming the measure, the result and the conclusion drawn.

text.en: Choose a measure that observes what people do rather than whether they attended

hint.en: Completion rates measure attendance, not conduct, so they cannot serve as the measure

text.en: State why the measure is a fair proxy for the behaviour the programme is meant to produce
Record this period's result against the previous period, or as the baseline if there is none
Decide which audience or topic material changes and how, or record why the material stands
Attach the effectiveness assessment naming the measure, the result and the conclusion drawn

evidenceHint.en: Effectiveness assessment naming the measure, the result for the period, and either the material being changed or the recorded conclusion that it stands

templates.title: Disciplinary process
templates.description: Define disciplinary process for policy violations
templates.objective: To ensure a security violation leads to a proportionate and consistent sanction decided under a known procedure rather than at the discretion of the moment.
templates.successCriteria:
A written procedure for security violations names the deciding role at every step.
Severity factors map to grades, and each grade carries a stated sanction range.
Incidents meeting the referral criteria reach the named HR recipient by the defined route.
Sanctions in closed cases sit within the range their grade allows, or the departure is resolved and recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the disciplinary procedure written for information security violations.
Obtain the grading table of severity factors and the sanction range attached to each grade.
Obtain the criteria for referring a security incident into the disciplinary process and the handover route.
Obtain the referral log for the period, or the nil return, and the consistency review note.

Analysis:
Read the procedure for a named deciding role at each step and identify any step leaving the decision unattributed.
Take the period's security incidents, determine which met the referral criteria, and confirm each of those appears in the referral log.
Recompute the grade for a sample of logged cases from the severity factors and compare it with the grade recorded.
Compare the sanction applied in each closed case with the range its grade allows.
Confirm the consistency review named the cases compared and carried each inconsistency to a resolution.

Output:
Reconciliation of referable incidents to referral log entries, naming those never referred.
Schedule of cases whose recorded grade differs from the grade the severity factors produce.
Listing of sanctions falling outside the range set for their grade.
Statement of whether the period produced a nil return and the basis on which it was accepted.

title.en: Write the disciplinary procedure for information security violations

description.en: Set out the path a confirmed violation takes: who receives the referral, how the person is informed and heard, who decides, what record is kept, and how appeal works. State how the procedure interacts with the general HR disciplinary process rather than duplicating it. Attach the procedure with the deciding role named at each step.

text.en: Name the role that receives the referral of a confirmed security violation
Set out how the person concerned is informed and given a hearing
Name the role that decides the outcome and state what record is kept of the decision
Describe how an appeal against a security sanction works and which role decides it
State where the procedure hands over to the general HR disciplinary process instead of duplicating it
Attach the security disciplinary procedure with the deciding role named at each step

evidenceHint.en: Disciplinary procedure for security violations, naming the deciding role at each step

title.en: Grade the severity of violations and set the sanction range for each grade

description.en: Define the grades a violation can attract and the factors that place it there, such as intent, recurrence, the sensitivity of information involved and actual harm caused, then record the sanction range available at each grade. Attach the grading table, so two similar cases cannot draw wildly different treatment.

text.en: Define the severity grades a security violation can attract
List the factors that place a case in each grade, such as intent, recurrence, information sensitivity and harm caused
Record the sanction range available at each grade
Check that two similar cases would land in the same grade and sanction range
Attach the violation grading table

evidenceHint.en: Grading table mapping severity factors to grades and the sanction range for each grade

title.en: Define when a security incident is referred into the disciplinary process, and to whom

description.en: Agree with incident handling the conditions under which a case stops being purely technical and becomes a conduct matter, who makes that call, and the named recipient in HR. Attach the referral criteria and the handover route, including how evidence is passed without widening access to it.

text.en: Agree with incident handling the conditions under which a technical case becomes a conduct matter
Name the role that decides a security incident should be referred
Name the HR recipient of each disciplinary referral
Set out how incident evidence is handed to HR without widening access to it
Attach the referral criteria and handover route

evidenceHint.en: Written referral criteria and handover route, naming the role that refers and the HR recipient

title.en: Log each disciplinary referral arising from a security violation and its outcome

description.en: Record every referral as it is raised: the date, the grade applied, the decision, the sanction and the closure date, holding the log under HR confidentiality with access restricted to the deciding roles. Attach the referral log for the period, or a nil return if none arose.

text.en: Record each disciplinary referral as it is raised, with the date and the grade applied
Add the decision, the sanction and the closure date as each case concludes
Restrict access to the referral log to the deciding roles under HR confidentiality
Attach the referral log for the period, or a nil return if no referral arose

evidenceHint.en: Referral log for the period (or a nil return): one row per case with grade, decision and closure date

title.en: Compare closed cases against the grading table for consistency of sanction

description.en: Review the cases closed in the period against the grades and sanction ranges, looking for like cases treated differently or sanctions falling outside the defined range. Attach the review note with the cases compared, any inconsistency found, and whether the fix is to the table or to how it is being applied.

text.en: List the cases closed in the period with the grade and sanction applied to each
Compare like cases with each other for differing treatment
Check every sanction applied falls inside the range set for its grade
Decide for each inconsistency whether the fix is to the grading table or to how it is applied
Attach the consistency review note with the cases compared and any inconsistency found

evidenceHint.en: Consistency review note listing the cases compared and any inconsistency and its resolution

templates.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
templates.objective: To ensure obligations that outlast an engagement remain enforceable, and that duties, information and relationships pass to a named successor rather than leave with the person.
templates.successCriteria:
A schedule records each surviving responsibility with its duration, source instrument, and whether it bites on departure, on an internal move, or both.
Every way an engagement can end or change, the no-notice variant included, has a named trigger and responsible role.
Leavers and movers are accounted for line by line against the acknowledgement record, with a reason for each gap.
Each transferred duty names its successor, and any duty left unassigned names its interim holder.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the schedule of responsibilities that survive a departure or a change of role.
Obtain the procedure naming the trigger and responsible role for each departure and change type.
Obtain the handover definition covering the duties, information and relationships that must be transferred.
Obtain the period's leavers and movers, their acknowledgement records and their completed handover records.
Obtain the sample test of departures and moves.

Analysis:
Confirm each surviving responsibility cites the instrument that creates it and states how long it runs.
Check the procedure covers internal moves and no-notice departures, not resignation with notice alone.
Account for the period's leavers and movers one by one against the acknowledgements and examine the reason held for every gap.
Read a sample of handover records for a named successor against each duty and an interim holder for any duty left open.
Test whether the sample named its population, stated which change types the period did and did not produce, and closed each exception.

Output:
Reconciliation of leavers and movers to acknowledgements, with unacknowledged names and their stated reasons.
Schedule of surviving responsibilities lacking a duration or a source instrument.
Listing of duties transferred with neither a successor nor an interim holder.
Statement of the change types the period did not produce and what that leaves untested.

title.en: Write the schedule of responsibilities that survive a departure or a change of role

description.en: Working from the engagement terms and confidentiality agreements already in place, list the obligations that continue to bind a person once they leave or move to a different role, the duration of each, and the instrument each comes from. Attach the schedule, distinguishing the obligations that apply on an internal move from those that apply on departure — they are not the same set, and a mover keeps working for you.

text.en: Gather the engagement terms and confidentiality agreements already in place

hint.en: A mover keeps working for you, so the internal-move set is not the departure set

text.en: Attach the schedule of surviving responsibilities

evidenceHint.en: Schedule of surviving responsibilities with duration, source instrument, and whether it bites on departure, on an internal move, or both

title.en: Name the trigger and the responsible person for every way an engagement can end or change

description.en: Cover resignation, the end of a fixed term, dismissal with no notice, retirement, an internal move, and a contractor rolling off. For each, record what starts the process, who holds the conversation about continuing responsibilities, and who obtains the acknowledgement. Attach the procedure, including the variant used when a person leaves the same day and the usual sequence is unavailable.

text.en: List each way an engagement can end or change: resignation, end of fixed term, dismissal without notice, retirement, internal move, contractor roll-off
Record what starts the process for each departure or change type
Name who holds the conversation about continuing responsibilities and who obtains the acknowledgement

title.en: Define what a leaver or mover must hand over, and to whom

templates.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
templates.objective: To ensure information reaches another party only under terms stating what may be done with it, for how long the restriction runs, and what follows a breach.
templates.successCriteria:
Each counterparty type carries a recorded decision on whether a confidentiality agreement is required, and the reason.
Agreements in use contain every element the required-content standard makes mandatory.
No counterparty receives information before its executed agreement is on the register.
Expiries and missing signed copies are identified by review and acted on.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of counterparty types with the confidentiality decision recorded against each.
Obtain the required-content standard, the approved template set, and the escalation route for third-party paper.
Obtain the agreement register with counterparty, template, signature date, term, expiry and accepted deviations.
Obtain the register review output for the period.

Analysis:
Compare each approved template against the required-content standard element by element.
Select counterparties that received information during the period and confirm the signature date precedes the first disclosure.
Examine agreements written on the counterparty's own paper and confirm each deviation was escalated and accepted by a role entitled to accept it.
Recalculate expiry from term and signature date and compare it with the expiry the register shows.
Confirm each gap the review raised carries an action and an outcome.

Output:
Element-by-element comparison of every template against the required-content standard.
Listing of disclosures that preceded an executed agreement.
Schedule of agreements expired or expiring, showing the register date beside the recalculated one.
Record of accepted deviations and the authority that accepted each.

title.en: Identify every relationship in which a confidentiality agreement is required

description.en: Enumerate the counterparties who reach your information, such as employees, contractors, suppliers and their subcontractors, prospects under evaluation, auditors, and site visitors, and record for each whether a signed agreement is required or is covered by another instrument. Attach the list with the requirement decision and its reason.

text.en: List the counterparties who reach your information: employees, contractors, suppliers, subcontractors, prospects, auditors and site visitors

Record the reason for each requirement decision

evidenceHint.en: List of counterparty types with the confidentiality requirement decision and reason for each

title.en: Record what a confidentiality agreement must contain to be acceptable

description.en: Define the mandatory content: how confidential information is identified, permitted use and permitted recipients, the duration of the obligation, return or destruction on termination, what happens on a breach, and governing law. Attach the required-content standard, so a counterparty's own paper can be assessed against it rather than argued case by case.

text.en: Define how confidential information must be identified in an acceptable agreement

evidenceHint.en: Required-content standard listing each mandatory element of an acceptable agreement

title.en: Produce the approved agreement templates for each relationship type

description.en: Draft or adapt the templates covering the relationship types identified, including one-way and mutual forms, and note which template serves which relationship. Attach the approved templates and the mapping, together with the escalation route for a counterparty who insists on their own paper.

text.en: Draft or adapt one-way and mutual agreement templates for the relationship types identified
Map each template to the relationship type it serves
Set the escalation route for a counterparty who insists on their own paper
Obtain approval of the templates and attach them with the mapping and escalation route

evidenceHint.en: Approved template set, the relationship each serves, and the escalation route for third-party paper

title.en: Record the executed agreement for each counterparty before information is shared

description.en: Log every agreement as it is signed: counterparty, template used, whether it was amended, signature date, term and expiry. Where the counterparty's own paper was accepted, note the assessment against the required-content standard. Attach the agreement register for the period.

text.en: Log each agreement as it is signed, with the counterparty, the template used and the signature date
Record the term, the expiry date and whether the template was amended
Note the assessment against the required-content standard wherever the counterparty's own paper was accepted
Confirm the agreement is executed and logged before any information is shared with the counterparty
Attach the agreement register for the period

evidenceHint.en: Agreement register: counterparty, template, signature date, term, expiry and any accepted deviation

title.en: Review the register for agreements expiring or missing a signed copy

description.en: Work through the register for agreements past or near expiry, relationships still active with no executed agreement, and rows where no countersigned copy was ever filed. Attach the review output listing each finding, the counterparty affected, and whether the agreement was renewed, chased or the relationship stopped.

text.en: Identify agreements in the register that are past or near expiry
Find relationships still active with no executed agreement
Find register rows where no countersigned copy was ever filed
Record for each finding whether the agreement was renewed, chased or the relationship stopped
Attach the register review output listing each finding and the counterparty affected

evidenceHint.en: Register review output listing expiries, gaps and the action taken on each

templates.title: Remote working
templates.objective: To ensure work away from organisational premises happens only where it has been authorised, and under protections suited to the places it is actually done.
templates.successCriteria:
Each authorised role names its approving manager, its permitted locations, and the duties or information excluded from working away.
The rules address equipment, surroundings, papers and portable items, shared spaces and loss.
The register shows, for every remote worker, what was issued and the date of any withdrawal.
Shortfalls found on confirmation are corrected or the arrangement is withdrawn.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the authorisation record of roles permitted to work away, with locations and exclusions.
Obtain the remote-working rules and the per-location statement of what the organisation supplies and what the person supplies.
Obtain the remote-working register for the period, withdrawals included.
Obtain the confirmation results for the period and the reconciliation against current practice.

Analysis:
Compare the register with the authorisation record and identify anyone working from a location their role does not permit.
Confirm the excluded duties and information are genuinely absent from the work done away from premises, not merely excluded on paper.
For a location type where the person supplies the equipment, test what protection is relied on and how it is confirmed.
Trace each shortfall to a correction or a withdrawal, and check the withdrawal date against the date access actually ended.
Test whether the reconciliation compared the register with observed practice rather than with itself.

Output:
Listing of people working away with no authorisation, or an authorisation naming a different location.
Schedule of shortfalls with the correction or withdrawal recorded against each.
Statement of what is relied on at each location type the organisation does not equip.
Exceptions where access continued after an authorisation was withdrawn.

title.en: Record which roles may work away from organisational premises, and where from

description.en: Decide role by role whether the work can be done away from your premises, whether that extends to a customer or partner site, shared and public spaces, and other countries, and which information or duties must not leave the premises at all. Attach the authorisation record listing role, approving manager, the permitted locations, and each exclusion with the reason it was excluded.

text.en: Decide role by role whether its work can be done away from organisational premises
Record for each permitted role whether that extends to customer or partner sites, shared and public spaces, and other countries
List the information or duties that must not leave the premises, with the reason for each exclusion
Record the approving manager for each role's remote-working authorisation
Attach the remote-working authorisation record

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation record: role, approving manager, permitted locations, and the information or duties excluded from working away

title.en: Write the rules a person must follow when working away from premises

description.en: State what is expected of the person: what they may work on, how they keep screens, papers, conversations and calls from being seen or overheard, how they store and destroy documents and portable items away from the office, what others sharing the space may and may not be given sight of, and what they do the moment equipment or information goes missing. Attach the rules document.

text.en: State what a person may work on when away from premises
Set out how screens, papers, conversations and calls are kept from being seen or overheard
Write how documents and portable items are stored and destroyed away from the office
State what others sharing the space may and may not be given sight of
Set out what the person does the moment equipment or information goes missing
Attach the remote-working rules document

evidenceHint.en: Remote-working rules covering equipment, surroundings, papers and portable items, shared spaces, and loss

title.en: Record what the organisation supplies for working away, and what the person supplies

description.en: For each permitted location type, write down what the organisation issues or pays for, what the person is expected to provide, and the protection relied on for each — for the equipment used, for the way work reaches your information, and for anything taken off site in physical form. Attach the statement, so that where a person's own equipment or a third party's premises are relied on, that reliance is a recorded decision rather than an assumption.

text.en: List each permitted location type from the remote-working authorisation record
Record for each location type what the organisation issues or pays for and what the person provides
Name the protection relied on for the equipment, for the route work takes to your information, and for anything taken off site in physical form
Record as an explicit decision each case where a person's own equipment or a third party's premises is relied on
Attach the supply and protection statement per location type

evidenceHint.en: Statement per location type of what the organisation supplies, what the person supplies, and the protection relied on for each

title.en: Record each person's remote-working authorisation as it is granted

description.en: Log every individual arrangement: the person, their role, the locations approved for them, the approval date and approving manager, and what they were issued to make it possible. Record withdrawals the same way when a role changes or an arrangement ends. Attach the remote-working register as it stood at the end of the period.

text.en: Log each individual remote-working arrangement as it is granted, with the person, role and approved locations
Record the approval date, the approving manager and what was issued to make the arrangement possible
Record each withdrawal and its date when a role changes or an arrangement ends
Attach the remote-working register as it stood at the end of the period

evidenceHint.en: Remote-working register: person, role, approved locations, approval date, what was issued, and any withdrawal with its date

title.en: Confirm for the period that what the remote-working rules require is actually in place

description.en: Check the people on the register against the rules — by a declaration from them, by their manager's confirmation, or from records you already hold, whichever you rely on — and record what was confirmed for each and how. Attach the confirmation results for the period naming every shortfall, what was missing, and whether it was corrected or the arrangement withdrawn.

text.en: Choose how compliance is confirmed for each person: their own declaration, their manager's confirmation or records already held
Check each person on the remote-working register against the rules by the chosen means
Record what was confirmed for each person and how
Name every shortfall, what was missing and whether it was corrected or the arrangement withdrawn
Attach the remote-working confirmation results for the period

evidenceHint.en: Confirmation results for the period naming each shortfall and whether it was corrected or the arrangement withdrawn

title.en: Reconcile who is working away from premises against the authorisation record

description.en: Compare the register against who is genuinely working away today, looking for arrangements that outlived a role change or a departure, people working from a location their role does not permit, and people working away with no recorded authorisation at all. Attach the reconciliation naming each discrepancy and the withdrawal or fresh authorisation that resolved it.

text.en: Establish from current practice who is working away from premises today and from where
Flag register entries that outlived a role change or a departure
Flag people working from a location their role does not permit, or with no recorded authorisation
Resolve each discrepancy by withdrawal or fresh authorisation and record which
Attach the reconciliation of the register against current practice

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of the register against current practice, with each discrepancy and the action that resolved it

templates.title: Information security event reporting
templates.description: Enable personnel to report security events
templates.objective: To ensure a person who notices something wrong knows what to say, has a route that is attended when they use it, and is willing to use it a second time.
templates.successCriteria:
Reportable situations are written in the words staff use and carry worked examples.
Every route names its receiving role and attended hours, with an alternative for when systems are unavailable and a recorded position on unnamed reports.
Reporters receive the acknowledgement and the protection the written commitment promises.
Reports are logged whatever they turn out to be, and each published route has been raised end to end with its elapsed time recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the reportable-situations list with its worked examples.
Obtain the route list with receiving roles, attended hours, the unavailable-systems alternative, and the position on unnamed reports.
Obtain the written reporter commitment and the acknowledgement wording used in practice.
Obtain the record of where each route is published and the date it went up.
Obtain the report log for the period, or the nil return, and the per-route test record.

Analysis:
Read the reportable-situations list for the vocabulary of the staff who must use it, not that of the security function.
Visit the places the publication record names and confirm the route shown there is the route currently attended.
Compare the acknowledgement actually sent to a sample of reporters with the wording the commitment promises.
Test the log for entries that came to nothing; a log holding only genuine incidents shows filtering before the log.
Check the per-route test raised a report down every published route, the out-of-hours alternative included, and recorded send and receipt times.

Output:
Route table showing publication points, attended hours, and the measured time to reach a receiver.
Listing of published routes that are unattended, superseded, or absent from the route list.
Comparison of the promised reporter acknowledgement with the one actually sent.
Statement of whether the log holds non-incident reports and what that implies about filtering before it.

title.en: Write, in the words staff use, what they should report

description.en: Describe the situations worth raising with concrete examples from your own setting — a device left behind, a message that does not look right, information sent to the wrong person, an unexpected request for credentials, a door found open, a control that visibly is not working — and state plainly that a suspicion is enough and that being wrong carries no penalty. Attach the list.

text.en: List the situations worth raising, using concrete examples drawn from your own setting
Cover devices left behind, suspect messages, misdirected information, unexpected credential requests, open doors and visibly failing controls
Rewrite each example in the words staff actually use rather than security terms
State plainly that a suspicion is enough to report and that being wrong carries no penalty
Attach the reportable-situations list with its worked examples

evidenceHint.en: Reportable-situations list with worked examples in the language staff actually use

title.en: Decide the routes staff can report by and who receives each one

description.en: Settle the ways a person can raise something and, for each, name the role that receives it, the hours it is attended, and what happens outside those hours. Include at least one route that still works when the usual systems are unavailable. Record too the position taken on a report made without the reporter naming themselves — whether a route exists for that and which one, or that none does and why — so the choice is a visible decision rather than an assumption. Attach the route list with the receiving role and attended hours against each entry.

text.en: List each route by which a person can raise a security event
Name the receiving role, the attended hours and the out-of-hours arrangement for each route
Include at least one route that still works when the usual systems are unavailable
Record the position on reports made without the reporter naming themselves, and which route serves them or why none does

hint.en: Having no anonymous route is acceptable only as a recorded decision, not by default

text.en: Attach the route list with the receiving role and attended hours per entry

evidenceHint.en: Route list with the receiving role and attended hours per route, the alternative used when systems are unavailable, and the recorded position on unnamed reports

title.en: Write down what a reporter is told afterwards and what protection they have

description.en: Commit to what happens from the reporter's side: the acknowledgement they get and how quickly, what they are told about the outcome, and the organisation's stated position on a good-faith report that turns out to be nothing or that concerns a colleague or a manager. Attach the commitment together with the wording actually used when acknowledging a report.

text.en: Set the acknowledgement a reporter receives and how quickly it is sent
State what a reporter is told about the outcome of their report
Write the organisation's position on a good-faith report that turns out to be nothing
Write the organisation's position on a good-faith report that concerns a colleague or a manager
Attach the reporter commitment together with the acknowledgement wording used in practice

evidenceHint.en: Written reporter commitment plus the acknowledgement wording used in practice

title.en: Publish the routes in the places people will be when they need them

description.en: Put the routes where the situation will find the person rather than where the security material lives — at the point of joining, where day-to-day work is discussed, and on or near the equipment and premises concerned. Attach the record of every place a route is published, with the date it went up and the person who maintains it, so a stale or removed notice is a visible row rather than a silent gap.

text.en: Publish the reporting routes in the material people receive at the point of joining
Post the routes where day-to-day work is discussed, not only where security material lives
Place route notices on or near the equipment and premises they concern
Record every place a route is published, the date it went up and who maintains it
Attach the publication record so a stale or removed notice shows as a row

evidenceHint.en: Record of every place a reporting route is published, with the date it went up and who maintains it

title.en: Log every report received, including the ones that turn out to be nothing

description.en: Capture each report as it arrives: the route it came by, the time received, what was described, who took it, and where it went next. Keep the ones closed as no issue in the same log — they are the evidence that the route is trusted and used. Attach the report log for the period, or a nil return if nothing was raised.

text.en: Capture each security report as it arrives, with the route used and the time received
Record what was described, who took the report and where it went next
Keep reports closed as no issue in the same log

hint.en: No-issue reports are the evidence that the route is trusted and used, so never prune them

text.en: Attach the report log for the period, or a nil return if nothing was raised

evidenceHint.en: Report log for the period (or a nil return): route, time received, what was described, who took it, and where it went next

title.en: Raise a report down every published route and record how long it took to reach its receiver

description.en: Send an unannounced test report by each route on the list, including the one that works when the usual systems are unavailable and any route the list records as usable without the reporter naming themselves, and record when it was sent and when the named receiving role actually had it in hand. Attach the per-route test record together with the fix applied to any route that lost the report or took longer than the commitment made to reporters allows.

text.en: Send an unannounced test report down each route on the published list
Include the route that works when usual systems are unavailable and any route for unnamed reports
Record when each test was sent and when the named receiving role actually had it in hand
Compare each route's time to receipt with the commitment made to reporters
Fix any route that lost the report or was too slow, and record the fix
Attach the per-route test record with send and receipt times

evidenceHint.en: Per-route test record with send and receipt times, and the fix applied to any route that failed or was slow

templates.title: Physical security perimeters
templates.description: Define and protect physical security perimeters
templates.objective: To ensure the boundary enclosing each area that needs protecting is known in full and kept in the condition the organisation decided it must be in.
templates.successCriteria:
Every site holds a marked plan or written description showing where each perimeter runs and what it encloses.
The register carries one row per stretch and per opening, with its condition and an adequacy judgement.
Shortfalls the register names are closed, each against a responsible person and a date.
A change to a perimeter produces an interim arrangement and an amended register row.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain each site's boundary record, marked plan or written description, naming the areas every perimeter encloses.
Obtain the perimeter register with one row per stretch and per opening, its condition and its adequacy.
Obtain the remediation record for the shortfalls the register names.
Obtain the period's perimeter change entries and the inspection report from walking each perimeter.

Analysis:
Trace the boundary on the plan for one site and confirm the register accounts for every stretch and opening along it, roofs, service ducts and shared walls included.
Test each adequacy judgement against what the enclosed areas hold, not against the barrier considered alone.
Follow each named shortfall to a completed action with a responsible person and a date, and identify those carried forward.
Compare the change entries with the register rows amended, and confirm the interim arrangement spanned the period the perimeter stood open.
Read the inspection report for differences found and confirm the register was corrected rather than the difference merely noted.

Output:
Marked plan per site annotated with the register row covering each stretch and opening.
Listing of openings present on site but absent from the register.
Schedule of outstanding shortfalls with their age and responsible person.
Record of perimeter changes lacking an interim arrangement or a register amendment.

title.en: Record where each security perimeter runs and what it encloses

description.en: For every site the organisation occupies, set down the line of each security perimeter and name the areas, rooms and facilities that fall inside it, so that every protected area is enclosed by a stated boundary. The record may be a marked plan or a written description of the boundary — either is acceptable provided the line and the areas inside it can be identified from it. Attach the boundary record for each site.

text.en: List every site the organisation occupies
Set down the line of each security perimeter at each site, on a marked plan or in a written description
Name the areas, rooms and facilities each perimeter encloses
Check that every protected area falls inside a stated boundary
Attach the perimeter boundary record for each site

evidenceHint.en: Boundary record per site — marked plan or written description — naming the areas each perimeter encloses

title.en: Record what forms each stretch of perimeter and every opening through it

description.en: Work along each boundary line in turn and set down, stretch by stretch, what physically separates inside from outside and its present condition, then list every opening through it — doorways, windows, hatches, loading points, ducts and service routes. Mark each stretch and each opening as adequate for what it encloses or as a shortfall. Attach the perimeter register.

text.en: Walk each perimeter boundary line in turn, stretch by stretch
Record what physically separates inside from outside on each stretch, and its present condition
List every opening through the boundary: doorways, windows, hatches, loading points, ducts and service routes

hint.en: Ducts and service routes count as openings, not only doors and windows

text.en: Mark each stretch and opening as adequate for what it encloses or as a shortfall
Attach the perimeter register, one row per stretch and per opening

evidenceHint.en: Perimeter register with one row per stretch and opening, its condition, and whether it is adequate

title.en: Close the perimeter shortfalls the register names

description.en: Take the stretches and openings the register marks as a shortfall and settle each one — by strengthening it, closing it, replacing it, or accepting it with a stated compensating arrangement and the reason. For each, record what was decided, what was done, who did it and when. Attach the remediation record, referencing the register rows it clears.

text.en: List the stretches and openings the perimeter register marks as a shortfall
Decide for each whether to strengthen, close or replace it, or accept it with a compensating arrangement and a reason
Record the action taken on each shortfall, who did it and when
Reference the perimeter register row each remediation clears
Attach the perimeter remediation record

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record naming each shortfall, the action taken, the person responsible and the date

title.en: Record each change to a perimeter and bring the register up to date

description.en: Whenever a boundary is altered — a new opening made, a stretch removed or breached for works, a partition moved, an area brought inside or taken outside a perimeter — record what changed, how the boundary was held while it was open, when it was reinstated, and amend the boundary record and perimeter register to match. Attach the change entries for the period with the amended register rows.

text.en: Record each alteration to a boundary: a new opening, a stretch removed or breached for works, a moved partition, an area brought in or out
Record how the boundary was held while it was open and when it was reinstated
Amend the boundary record and the perimeter register to match the change
Attach the perimeter change entries for the period with the amended register rows

evidenceHint.en: Perimeter change entries for the period, each showing the interim arrangement and the register rows amended

title.en: Walk each perimeter and report where it differs from the register

description.en: Go round the boundary of each site and check, stretch by stretch, that what the register describes is what is actually there — present, intact, closing and fastening as recorded, with no undocumented opening. Record every difference found, what it exposes, and how it was resolved. Attach the inspection report per site.

text.en: Walk the boundary of each site stretch by stretch, with the perimeter register in hand
Check each stretch and opening is present, intact, and closing and fastening as recorded
Look for any opening through the boundary that the register does not document
Record each difference found, what it exposes and how it was resolved
Attach the perimeter inspection report for each site

evidenceHint.en: Inspection report per site listing each difference from the register and its resolution

templates.title: Physical entry
templates.description: Control physical access to secure areas
templates.objective: To ensure only those holding a recorded entitlement pass into a controlled area, and that the entitlement ends when the need which justified it ends.
templates.successCriteria:
Each controlled area records who may enter, whether unaccompanied, and the basis for the entitlement.
Every entry point names what checks entitlement, how a refusal is handled, and who may override.
Admissions of people without their own entitlement record the authoriser, the accompaniment and the times in and out.
Withdrawals correspond to the leavers, role changes and ended engagements the period produced.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the entry entitlement record for each controlled area.
Obtain the per-entry-point record of what checks entitlement, the refusal handling and the override authority.
Obtain the admission terms for people without their own entitlement and the period's completed admission records.
Obtain the withdrawal records and the comparison of actual entry capability against recorded entitlement.

Analysis:
Extract who can actually open each controlled area from the access system and the key issue, and compare it name by name with the entitlement record.
Test the basis recorded for unaccompanied entitlement against the role the person now holds.
Check admission records for an authoriser entitled to authorise, and for a recorded exit against every recorded entry.
Match the period's leavers, role changes and ended engagements to withdrawals and measure the interval between the two dates.
Exercise the override at one entry point and confirm its use is recorded and reaches somebody who reviews it.

Output:
Name-by-name comparison of actual entry capability with recorded entitlement, per area.
Listing of admissions with no exit recorded, or an authoriser without the authority used.
Schedule of withdrawal intervals, naming entitlement still live after the need ended.
Record of override use and the review each instance received.

title.en: Record who is entitled to enter each controlled area and on what basis

description.en: For each area that is not open to everyone, set down which roles and which named individuals may enter, whether they may do so unaccompanied, and what gives them the entitlement — the job they hold, the contract they are under, the task they are engaged on. Attach the entitlement record covering every controlled area.

text.en: List every area that is not open to everyone
Record which roles and named individuals may enter each controlled area
Mark whether each entitled role or individual may enter unaccompanied
Record the basis of each entitlement: the job held, the contract under which they work, or the task they are engaged on
Attach the entry entitlement record covering every controlled area

evidenceHint.en: Entry entitlement record per area, naming the role or individual, whether unaccompanied, and the basis

title.en: Record how entitlement is checked at each entry point before someone is admitted

description.en: For every point at which a person can enter a controlled area, set down who or what establishes that the person arriving is entitled to be admitted, what happens when they are not, and who may admit somebody outside the normal check. Describe the arrangement as it actually operates, whatever form it takes. Attach the record covering each entry point, including any point where no check is made.

text.en: List every point at which a person can enter a controlled area
Record who or what establishes at each point that the arriving person is entitled to be admitted

hint.en: Describe the check as it actually operates, not as it was designed to work

text.en: Record what happens at each entry point when the person is not entitled
Name who may admit somebody outside the normal entitlement check
Attach the per-entry-point record, including every point where no check is made

evidenceHint.en: Per-entry-point record of who or what checks entitlement, the refusal handling and the override authority

title.en: Set out the terms on which people without their own entitlement are admitted

description.en: Write down the conditions under which visitors, contractors, delivery and collection staff and anyone else without an entitlement of their own is let into a controlled area: what identification is established, who authorises the admission, whether they are accompanied and by whom, and what is written down when they arrive and when they leave. Attach the admission terms together with the blank form the record will be kept on.

text.en: List who may need admitting without their own entitlement: visitors, contractors, delivery and collection staff and others
Set the identification to be established and who authorises each admission
State whether such people are accompanied inside the area and by whom
Define what is written down when they arrive and when they leave
Attach the admission terms with the blank admission record form

evidenceHint.en: Admission terms for non-entitled people, plus the blank record form they will be entered on

title.en: Record each admission of someone without their own entitlement

description.en: For every person admitted during the period on the terms above, capture the area entered, who authorised the admission, who accompanied them if anyone did, and the times of arrival and departure. Attach the completed admission records for the period.

text.en: Enter each admission on the record form at arrival, naming the area and who authorised it
Record who accompanied the person while inside, if anyone did
Record the departure time as the person leaves the controlled area
Check the period's admission records for entries with no departure time and follow them up
Attach the completed admission records for the period

evidenceHint.en: Completed admission records for the period showing area, authoriser, accompaniment and times in and out

title.en: Withdraw entry entitlement when the need for it ends, and record the withdrawal

description.en: When somebody leaves, changes role, or finishes the work that gave them entitlement, remove their ability to enter the areas concerned — recovering whatever they hold that admits them and striking them from the entitlement record — and note the date and who did it. Attach the withdrawal records for the period beside the list of leavers, role changes and completed engagements they answer to.

text.en: Take the period's leavers, role changes and completed engagements as the trigger list for withdrawal
Remove each person's ability to enter the controlled areas their entitlement covered
Recover whatever the person holds that admits them
Strike the person from the entitlement record, noting the date and who did it
Attach the withdrawal records beside the trigger list they answer to

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal records for the period, matched to the leavers, role changes and ended engagements they correspond to

title.en: Compare who can actually get in against the entitlement record

description.en: Take each controlled area and establish who is in a position to enter it in practice, then set that against the entitlement record. List everyone who can enter without an entitlement and everyone entitled who no longer needs it, and record what was done about each. Attach the comparison and its outcomes.

text.en: Establish for each controlled area who is in a position to enter it in practice

hint.en: Include anyone who can get in by a shared or master means, not only named holders

text.en: Compare that population against the entry entitlement record for the area
List everyone who can enter without an entitlement
List everyone entitled to enter who no longer needs to
Record what was done about each discrepancy and attach the comparison per area

evidenceHint.en: Comparison per area listing every discrepancy between actual and recorded entitlement, with its resolution

templates.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
templates.objective: To ensure each room is protected in proportion to what is kept and done inside it, and that its location and contents are not advertised to those outside.
templates.successCriteria:
Each room's record names what it holds and the protection that room is required to provide.
Public indications of where sensitive rooms are and what they contain have been removed or changed.
A room falls short of its required protection only while a dated remediation action is open.
A room found unsecured is recorded with the state it was in and the means by which it was made secure.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the room record naming each room, its holdings, and the protection it is required to provide.
Obtain the record of public indications found and the change made to each, with before and after.
Obtain the per-room remediation record and the period's securing findings.
Obtain the review comparing each room record with how the room is now used.

Analysis:
Walk a sample of rooms and compare what is present with what the record says the room holds.
Test the required protection against the holdings rather than against the room's original designation.
Look for indications the removal record missed: directories, wayfinding, delivery instructions, room booking listings and external signage.
Confirm each securing finding names both the state the room was found in and how it was made secure.
Compare the review's conclusions against the rooms whose use changed in the period, rooms taken on or given up included.

Output:
Room-by-room comparison of recorded holdings with the contents observed.
Listing of surviving public indications and where each was found.
Schedule of rooms below their required protection, with the age of the open action.
Record of rooms whose use changed without a corresponding amendment to the room record.

title.en: Record what each office, room and facility holds and the protection it therefore needs

description.en: Go through the rooms and facilities in use and set down, for each, the information, equipment and activities it contains and, from that, the protection the room itself must provide — how it is closed and fastened, what may be stored in it, whether it may be left unattended, and what separation it needs from neighbouring space. Attach the room record.

text.en: List the offices, rooms and facilities in use
Record the information, equipment and activities each room contains
Derive the protection each room must provide: how it closes and fastens, what may be stored there, whether it may be left unattended
Record the separation each room needs from neighbouring space
Attach the room record naming what each room holds and the protection it requires

evidenceHint.en: Room record naming each room, what it holds and the protection the room is required to provide

title.en: Remove the public indications of where sensitive rooms are and what they hold

description.en: Find where the location or purpose of a sensitive room is announced to people with no need to know it — signage and wayfinding, internal and external directories, published plans, delivery addressing, listings in the organisation's own materials — and change or remove each one. Attach a record of what was found and what was done to it, showing the state before and after.

text.en: Search signage and wayfinding for anything showing where sensitive rooms are or what they hold
Check internal and external directories, published plans and delivery addressing for the same
Check listings in the organisation's own materials for sensitive room locations or purposes
Change or remove each indication found, recording its state before and after
Attach the record of each public indication found and the change made

evidenceHint.en: Record of each public indication found and the change made to it, with before and after

title.en: Bring each room up to the protection its record requires

description.en: Take the rooms whose present state falls short of the room record and settle each shortfall — by providing the storage, fastening, separation or restriction the record calls for, by moving what is held into a room that already meets it, or by revising the requirement with a stated reason and who agreed it. Attach the remediation record per room.

text.en: Compare each room's present state with the protection its room record requires
Provide the storage, fastening, separation or restriction a room falls short on
Move what is held into a room that already meets the requirement where that is the better fix
Revise a room requirement only with a stated reason and the name of who agreed it
Attach the room remediation record naming each shortfall, the action and the date

evidenceHint.en: Remediation record per room naming the shortfall, the action taken and the date

title.en: Record every room found left open or otherwise not secured as required

description.en: Whenever a room in the record is found unattended without the securing its record calls for — standing open, fastening not engaged, protective arrangement not in use — note the room, who found it, when, what was not secured, and how the room was made secure again. Attach the findings for the period, including the occasions on which nothing was found.

text.en: Note each room found unattended without the securing its room record calls for
Record who found the room, when, and what was not secured
Record how the room was made secure again
Record the occasions rooms were checked and nothing was found
Attach the room securing findings for the period

evidenceHint.en: Securing findings for the period naming the room, the state it was found in and how it was made secure

title.en: Check each room record against how the room is now used

description.en: Rooms change hands and change purpose. Go through the room record and confirm, room by room, that what it says the room holds is still true and that the protection stated is still the protection needed; where it is not, say what changed and raise an action. Attach the review listing the rooms whose holdings or required protection have moved, with the action raised for each.

text.en: Confirm room by room that what the room record says each room holds is still true
Confirm the protection stated for each room is still the protection it needs
Record what changed for each room whose holdings or required protection have moved
Raise an action for each room whose record no longer holds
Attach the room record review listing the changed rooms and the action raised for each

evidenceHint.en: Review listing the rooms whose holdings or required protection changed, with the action raised for each

templates.title: Physical security monitoring
templates.objective: To ensure unauthorised presence is observed while it is happening and reaches somebody able to act, and that what the monitoring captures is itself protected.
templates.successCriteria:
The monitoring record names how and when each watched area is observed, and which areas are deliberately left unwatched.
Each kind of observation has a named recipient, a route to them, and an expected action.
Captured material is kept for a stated period and viewed only by those currently on the permitted list.
Every observation of possible unauthorised access is logged with its responder, its finding and its outcome.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the monitoring record of watched areas, the means of observation, the hours covered, and the areas left unwatched.
Obtain the response record naming the recipient, route and expected action for each kind of observation.
Obtain the retention and access statement for monitoring material with the current list of permitted viewers.
Obtain the period's monitoring log and the verification record for each monitored area.

Analysis:
Compare the watched areas against the areas the organisation treats as controlled and confirm each gap was a decision rather than an omission.
Generate an observation in one area and follow it to the named recipient, timing its arrival against the action expected.
Compare the permitted viewer list with the accounts and keys that can in fact reach the captured material.
Test retention by requesting material from the start of the stated period and material older than it.
Read the verification record for faults found and confirm each was repaired rather than simply logged.

Output:
Coverage map of watched and unwatched areas set against the controlled areas.
Timed trace of one observation from capture to the responder who acted on it.
Comparison of permitted viewers with actual access to captured material.
Schedule of monitoring faults, their repair dates, and the periods an area went unwatched.

title.en: Record which areas are watched for unauthorised access and how each is watched

description.en: Set down the areas, entry points and approaches kept under observation for people being where they should not be, and for each one how that observation is achieved and when it applies — continuously, out of hours, on rounds. Name plainly any area in scope that is not watched at all. Attach the monitoring record.

text.en: List the areas, entry points and approaches kept under observation for unauthorised presence
Record how each is observed and when observation applies: continuously, out of hours or on rounds
Name plainly each in-scope area that is not watched at all
Attach the physical monitoring record

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring record naming each watched area, how it is observed, when, and the areas left unwatched

title.en: Record who is told when something is observed, and what they are to do

description.en: For each kind of observation the monitoring can produce — somebody in an area out of hours, an entry forced or held open, an unaccompanied stranger, an area that should be occupied standing empty — set down who is told, by what route, and what they are expected to do, including the point at which they pass it to somebody else. Attach the response record covering every kind of observation.

text.en: List each kind of observation the monitoring can produce, such as out-of-hours presence or an entry forced or held open
Include an unaccompanied stranger and an area that should be occupied standing empty
Name who is told of each kind of observation and by what route
Record the action expected and the point at which it is passed to somebody else
Attach the response record covering every kind of observation

evidenceHint.en: Response record per kind of observation, naming the recipient, the route and the action expected

title.en: Record how what the monitoring captures is kept and who may see it

description.en: State where the material the monitoring produces is held, how long it is kept before disposal, who is permitted to view or release it and on what grounds, and how a request to view it is authorised and recorded. Attach the statement together with the current list of people permitted to view.

text.en: Record where the material the monitoring captures is held
Set how long monitoring material is kept before disposal
Name who may view or release monitoring material and on what grounds
Define how a request to view monitoring material is authorised and recorded
Attach the retention and access statement with the current list of people permitted to view

evidenceHint.en: Retention and access statement for monitoring material, with the list of people currently permitted to view it

title.en: Record every observation of possible unauthorised access and how it was dealt with

description.en: Capture each occasion during the period on which the monitoring produced something needing a response, including the ones that turned out to be innocent: what was observed, where, when, who responded, what they found, and how it ended. Attach the log for the period.

text.en: Capture each occasion the monitoring produced something needing a response, including the innocent ones
Record what was observed, where and when
Record who responded, what they found and how the occasion ended
Attach the monitoring log for the period

evidenceHint.en: Monitoring log for the period, each entry with the observation, the responder, the finding and the outcome

title.en: Confirm each area is still being watched the way its record says

description.en: Take the monitoring record area by area and establish that the observation it describes is actually happening now — that rounds are being made where rounds are the arrangement, that what should be in view is in view and not obstructed, that what should be captured is being captured, and that it reaches the person named in the response record. Note every arrangement found not working and the repair made. Attach the verification record.

text.en: Confirm rounds are being made in each area where rounds are the arrangement
Check that what should be in view is in view and unobstructed
Check that what should be captured is being captured
Confirm an observation in each area reaches the person named in the response record
Record each arrangement found not working and the repair made
Attach the monitoring verification record per area

evidenceHint.en: Verification record per monitored area, with how it was checked, the faults found and their repair

templates.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
templates.objective: To ensure the hazards each site is genuinely exposed to are answered by a protection somebody owns, or stand as exposures the organisation has knowingly accepted.
templates.successCriteria:
Each site's exposure record names its threats, the areas and assets exposed, and the effect expected.
Every recorded threat maps to a protection with an owner, or is named as unprotected.
Threats left uncovered end in a protection introduced or an exposure accepted by a named decider.
Every protection register row is accounted for in the period by a test, a service result, a condition check, or the provider's evidence.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain each site's exposure record with its threats, the areas and assets exposed, and the expected effect.
Obtain the protection register linking every threat to the protection in place and its owner.
Obtain the decisions recorded against the threats the register leaves uncovered.
Obtain the period's evidence that each protection still stands, and the reassessment against changes at and around each site.

Analysis:
Test the exposure record against the site's surroundings, services and history rather than against a generic threat list.
Account for every protection register row in the period's evidence and identify the rows supported by nothing.
Where the evidence is a provider's, confirm it covers the organisation's own equipment and areas rather than the building generally.
Where the protection is an inherent condition, confirm somebody checked the condition is unchanged instead of assuming it.
Read each accepted exposure for the decider's authority to accept it and for a date on which the acceptance is revisited.

Output:
Threat-to-protection matrix per site, with the owner and the evidence relied on this period.
Listing of protection register rows with no evidence for the period.
Schedule of accepted exposures, their decider, and their revisit date.
Record of changes at and around each site since the last assessment, with their effect on exposure.

title.en: Record the physical and environmental threats each site is exposed to

description.en: For every site, set down the natural and man-made threats it could suffer — fire, water, storm, ground movement, extremes of temperature, explosion or damage arising from activity nearby, disruption of the surrounding area — reasoning from the site's location, construction, neighbours and history. For each threat, record what would be affected and how badly. Attach the exposure record per site.
