Remove elevated rights from each administrator's everyday account used for email and browsing
Export from the directory the pairing of each administrator's standard account with their privileged identity
Record each system that cannot support separate privileged accounts and the compensating measure used there
Attach the directory export together with the note on systems without separation

evidenceHint.en: Directory export pairing each administrator's standard account with a separate privileged identity

title.en: Record each grant and revocation of privileged access with its authorisation

description.en: Log every elevation and removal as it happens, capturing who requested it, who approved it, the system, and the date it was withdrawn. Break-glass use is logged the same way with the reason for invoking it. Attach the log covering the period.

text.en: Log each privilege elevation as it happens, with the requester, the approver, the system and the date
Record the withdrawal date against each grant when the privilege is removed
Log every break-glass invocation the same way, adding the reason it was invoked
Attach the privileged access grant and revocation log covering the period

evidenceHint.en: Privileged access grant and revocation log for the period, including break-glass invocations

title.en: Recertify every privileged account against the register and withdraw those no longer justified

description.en: Put the current holder list for each privileged role in front of the system owner, have them confirm or reject each holder, and remove the rejected ones. Record what was removed and when, so the recertification shows an outcome rather than a signature. Attach the recertification with removals evidenced.

text.en: Prepare the current holder list for each privileged role in each system
Have each system owner confirm or reject every holder on their list
Remove the privileged access of every holder the system owner rejected
Record what was removed and the date of each removal

hint.en: A signed list with no removals evidenced shows a signature, not an outcome

text.en: Attach the recertification with the confirm or remove decision per account and the completed removals

evidenceHint.en: Recertification record showing confirm or remove per privileged account and the completed removals

templates.title: Information access restriction
templates.description: Restrict access to information per policy
templates.objective: To ensure that people reach only the information their role is permitted to read or change, including by bulk export, and that every change to those rules traces to an authorisation.
templates.successCriteria:
An access matrix states read, write or no access for each information class against each role.
System permissions implement the matrix row they correspond to, evidenced per system.
Bulk export and reporting of restricted information is confined to a named list of roles.
Every access-rule change in the period carries a requester and an approver, and account testing reports each deviation found with its correction.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the access matrix of information classes against roles with the access allowed in each cell.
Collect the per-system permission exports placed beside the matrix rows they implement.
Obtain the configuration record of bulk export and reporting rights and the roles that retain them.
Pull the access-rule change log for the period with its requesters and approvers.
Obtain the access test results per sampled account: expected access, actual access and correction.

Analysis:
Check that the matrix covers every information class in scope and leaves no cell undecided.
Compare a sampled system's permission export with its matrix row and note grants that go beyond it.
Test whether the bulk export path enforces the same restriction as the record-level permissions do.
Verify that change log entries name an approver who is not also the requester.
Assess deviations found in account testing for a correction that was applied rather than accepted.

Output:
Matrix-to-permission differences per sampled system.
A list of roles holding bulk export rights outside the named list.
Deviation findings per sampled account with the correction status of each.

title.en: Map each class of information to the roles permitted to read and to change it

description.en: Build a matrix whose rows are information classes or repositories and whose columns are business roles, marking read, write and no-access in each cell. Agree it with the owner of each information class rather than deriving it from what access currently exists. Attach the matrix.

text.en: Draw up a matrix with information classes or repositories as rows and business roles as columns
Mark each cell of the access matrix as read, write or no access
Agree each row of the matrix with the owner of that information class

hint.en: Start from what the owner says should exist, not from the access that exists today

text.en: Attach the agreed access matrix of information classes against roles

evidenceHint.en: Access matrix of information classes against roles, showing read, write or no access per cell

title.en: Configure system permissions so each role sees only what its matrix row allows

description.en: Translate the matrix into the actual permission model of each system holding the information — groups, roles, sharing settings — and remove access that exceeds the row. Attach a permission export per system alongside the matrix row it implements, so a reviewer can compare them.

text.en: Identify each system that holds information covered by the access matrix
Translate each matrix row into the groups, roles and sharing settings of the systems holding that information
Remove access in each system that exceeds what the matrix row allows
Export the permissions from each system once aligned
Attach each system's permission export beside the matrix row it implements

evidenceHint.en: Per-system permission export placed beside the matrix row it implements

title.en: Restrict bulk export and reporting of restricted information to named roles

description.en: Identify the routes that yield information in bulk — report builders, database query tools, data exports, integration credentials — and limit them to the roles the matrix permits, so read access to a record does not become read access to the population. Attach the configuration showing who retains bulk export.

text.en: Identify the bulk routes to restricted information: report builders, database query tools, data exports and integration credentials
Compare who holds each bulk route with the roles the access matrix permits
Restrict each bulk route to the roles the matrix permits and withdraw it from the rest

hint.en: Read access to a single record is no reason to keep bulk export of the whole population

text.en: Attach the configuration record listing the roles that retain bulk export and reporting rights

evidenceHint.en: Configuration record of bulk export and reporting rights, listing the roles that retain them

title.en: Record every access-rule change against the request that authorised it

description.en: As permissions are granted, altered or withdrawn, log the system, the principal, what changed, who asked and who approved. This is what makes an unexpected permission traceable later. Attach the change log for the period.

text.en: Log each grant, alteration or withdrawal of a permission as it is made
Capture against each access-rule change the system, the principal and what changed
Name against each access-rule change who asked for it and who approved it
Attach the access-rule change log for the period with requester and approver per entry

evidenceHint.en: Access-rule change log for the period, each entry carrying its requester and approver

title.en: Test a sample of accounts against the access matrix and report the deviations

description.en: Pick accounts across several roles, enumerate what each can actually reach in the live systems, and compare it to the matrix row for that role. Record every deviation with its cause — stale grant, over-broad group, matrix wrong — and the correction made. Attach the test results.

text.en: Select a sample of accounts spread across several business roles
Enumerate what each sampled account can actually reach in the live systems
Compare each account's actual access with the matrix row for its role
Record each deviation with its cause: stale grant, over-broad group or matrix wrong
Correct each deviation and record the correction made
Attach the access test results giving expected and actual access per sampled account

evidenceHint.en: Access test results per sampled account: expected access, actual access, deviation and correction

templates.title: Access to source code
templates.objective: To ensure that source code, and every copy of it kept elsewhere, is reachable only by the people and services that currently need it for work in hand.
templates.successCriteria:
The source code register lists each holding and each copy kept outside it, with its owner and its location.
A permission model names who may read, change and administer each holding, non-human identities included.
Holdings enforce the recorded permissions, and access that went beyond them has been withdrawn and listed.
Grants and withdrawals in the period are logged, and reconciliation shows every holder and copy as still needed or removed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the source code register covering each holding and each copy kept outside it.
Obtain the permission model naming read, change and administer holders, human and non-human.
Collect the per-holding permission listings taken after alignment, with the withdrawn access recorded.
Pull the source code access change log for the period, service accounts and tokens included.
Obtain the reconciliation of access holders and copies against current need.

Analysis:
Search build systems, backups and developer workstations for code copies the register omits.
Compare a sampled holding's live permissions with the model and quantify the surplus.
Check whether non-human identities hold change or administer rights where a read right would serve.
Trace logged grants back to a request and logged withdrawals to a leaver or a role change.
Assess whether copies judged unnecessary at reconciliation were deleted rather than left in place.

Output:
A list of code copies found outside the register.
Permission surplus findings per sampled holding, split by human and non-human identity.
Reconciliation outcomes naming the copies and accounts still awaiting removal.

title.en: Register the source code holdings and every copy kept outside them

description.en: Work outward from the code the organisation builds and runs: name each store that holds it and the owner of that store. Then record the copies living outside those stores — working copies on developer machines, archived or escrowed snapshots, and code handed to a third party — because a copy carries none of the store's restrictions with it. Attach the register with one row per holding and per copy.

text.en: Name each store holding the code the organisation builds and runs, with the owner of that store
Trace the working copies of that code on developer machines and add each to the register

hint.en: A copy outside the store carries none of the store's access restrictions with it

text.en: Add the archived or escrowed snapshots of the code, with where each is kept
Add the code handed to third parties, naming each party holding it
Attach the source code register with one row per holding and per copy, each with owner and location

evidenceHint.en: Source code register: each holding and each copy, with its owner and location

title.en: Record who may read, change and administer each source code holding

description.en: For every row of the register decide three separate things: who may read the code, who may change it, and who may alter the holding's own permissions and settings. Cover non-human identities explicitly — build, deployment and integration accounts hold change rights and are the ones usually left off the model. Attach the permission model.

text.en: Name for each row of the source code register who may read the code
Name for each holding who may change the code
Name for each holding who may alter its own permissions and settings
Add the build, deployment and integration accounts that hold change rights to the model

hint.en: Non-human identities are the holders most often left off a source code permission model

text.en: Attach the permission model naming read, change and administer holders per holding

evidenceHint.en: Permission model naming read, change and administer holders per holding, including non-human identities

title.en: Apply the recorded permissions at each holding and withdraw the access beyond them

description.en: Set each holding's permissions to match the model by whatever means that holding provides, and remove access exceeding the model rather than leaving it noted as an exception. Where a holding cannot express the model, record the restriction relied on instead and who owns it. Attach the resulting permission listing per holding together with the record of what was withdrawn.

text.en: Set each holding's permissions to match the permission model, using the means that holding provides
Remove every source code access exceeding the model rather than noting it as an exception
Record, for any holding that cannot express the model, the restriction relied on instead and who owns it
Produce the permission listing for each holding after alignment
Attach the per-holding listings together with the record of access withdrawn

evidenceHint.en: Per-holding permission listing after alignment, with the list of access withdrawn

title.en: Record each grant and withdrawal of source code access in the period

description.en: Log every addition and removal of access as people and services arrive, change role or leave, naming the holding, the identity, the level granted or removed, and what prompted it. Include credentials issued to or retired from automated identities, which change hands without anyone joining or leaving. Attach the log for the period.

text.en: Log each addition and removal of source code access as people and services arrive, change role or leave
Record against each entry the holding, the identity, the level granted or removed and what prompted it
Log the credentials issued to or retired from automated identities, which change without anyone joining or leaving
Attach the source code access change log for the period, including non-human identities

evidenceHint.en: Source code access change log for the period, including non-human identities

title.en: Reconcile the accounts and copies holding source code against who needs them now

description.en: Put the register and the current permission listings beside the people and services actually doing the work. Name every account that is no longer needed, every copy nobody will claim, and every third party still holding code beyond its purpose, and record the withdrawal or destruction of each. Attach the reconciliation with an outcome against every line.

text.en: Lay the source code register and current permission listings beside the people and services doing the work now
Name every account no longer needed and record its withdrawal
Name every copy of the code that nobody claims and record its destruction
Name each third party holding code beyond its purpose and record the withdrawal or destruction of its copy
Attach the reconciliation with an outcome against every holder and copy

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of source code access holders and copies against current need, with outcome per line

templates.title: Secure authentication
templates.objective: To ensure that each system demands proof of identity proportionate to what it protects, for service identities as much as people, so any weakening of that demand is a recorded decision.
templates.successCriteria:
Every system is registered with where identity is verified, the proof demanded, and the method non-human identities use.
Each system class states how many independent proofs a sign-in must present, with its justification recorded beneath it.
Systems short of their class requirement are listed with an owner and a date rather than counted as compliant.
Changes to what a system demands at sign-in carry the decider and the reason, and classes that saw no change are stated as such.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the authentication register naming verification point, proof demanded and non-human method per system.
Obtain the per-class requirement statement with the justification held beneath each class.
Collect the per-system evidence of the proof now demanded at sign-in.
Obtain the list of systems still short of their class with owner and date.
Pull the period's change record and attempt a sign-in against a sample of systems.

Analysis:
Check that every system in the scope inventory also appears in the authentication register.
Compare the proof each sampled system actually demanded at the attempted sign-in with what its class sets.
Test whether non-human identities authenticate by the registered method or by a shared static secret.
Examine the change record for reductions in demanded proof and whether a decider accepted each.
Confirm the classes recorded as unchanged saw no configuration change during the period.

Output:
Observed proof set against required proof per sampled system.
A list of systems short of their class with owner and remediation date.
Findings on non-human authentication methods and on any reduction accepted in the period.

title.en: Record how each system establishes that a user or service is who they claim to be

description.en: For every in-scope system record where the identity is verified — centrally or by the system itself — what proof it demands before a session begins, and how non-human identities authenticate to it. Attach the register; its value is that it makes visible the systems that accept a single shared secret and nothing more.

text.en: Enter each in-scope system in the authentication register, noting whether identity is verified centrally or by the system itself
Describe the proof each system demands before a session begins
Record how non-human identities authenticate to each system
Mark the systems that accept a single shared secret and nothing more
Attach the authentication register by system, place of verification, proof demanded and non-human method

evidenceHint.en: Authentication register: system, where identity is verified, proof demanded, and method used by non-human identities

title.en: Set how many independent proofs a sign-in must present for each class of system

description.en: State per class how many independent proofs a sign-in must present and of what kinds, how long a session may run before identity is established again, and what must happen after repeated failed attempts. Where the organisation has separately recorded what makes a secret or credential strong enough, reference that record rather than restating the requirement here. Record a justification for every class held below the general requirement. Attach the requirement statement.

text.en: State per system class how many independent proofs a sign-in must present and of what kinds
Set per system class how long a session may run before identity is established again
State what must happen after repeated failed sign-in attempts in each class
Reference the organisation's existing record of credential strength rather than restating it

hint.en: Only where such a record exists; the requirement statement does not repeat its content

text.en: Record a justification for every class held below the general requirement
Attach the authentication requirement statement per system class

evidenceHint.en: Authentication requirement statement per system class, with a justification for each class held below it

title.en: Bring each registered system up to the proof its class requires

description.en: Work through the register row by row, changing what each system demands at sign-in until it matches its class, and record every row still short of the requirement with an owner and a date. Attach, per system, evidence of what is now demanded, alongside the outstanding list — the list is as much the deliverable as the settings are.

text.en: Compare what each registered system demands at sign-in with the requirement for its class
Change each system's sign-in settings until it demands what its class requires
Capture per system evidence of the proof now demanded at sign-in
Record each system still short of its class requirement with an owner and a date

hint.en: The outstanding list is as much the deliverable as the changed settings

text.en: Attach the per-system evidence together with the outstanding list

evidenceHint.en: Per-system evidence of the proof now demanded at sign-in, plus the list of systems still short with owner and date

title.en: Record every change made this period to what a system demands at sign-in

description.en: Whenever a system enters the authentication register, changes the proof it demands, or is granted or released from a justification for sitting below its class requirement, record the system, its class, what was demanded before and what is demanded now, who decided and why. Where a class saw no change in the period, record that rather than leaving it out. Attach the change record for the period together with the register rows it updates.

text.en: Identify the systems that entered the authentication register, changed the proof demanded, or gained or lost a justification
Record for each such system its class and the proof demanded before and after
Name who decided each change to what a system demands, and the reason given
State each class that saw no change in the period rather than leaving it out
Attach the period's change record together with the register rows it updates

evidenceHint.en: Change record for the period: system, class, the proof demanded before and after, the decider and the reason, with the classes that saw no change stated as such

title.en: Attempt sign-in against a sample of systems and record what was actually demanded

description.en: Pick systems across the classes and try to sign in: confirm the proofs the requirement names are genuinely demanded, that repeated failure is answered as stated, and that a session does not outlive the period allowed. Record observed against expected behaviour for each system, and the fix for every deviation. Attach the test record.

text.en: Select a sample of systems spread across the system classes
Attempt sign-in to each and confirm the proofs the requirement names are genuinely demanded
Repeat failed sign-in attempts and record whether each system responds as the requirement states
Keep a session open past the allowed period and check whether the system ends it
Record observed against expected behaviour and the fix for each deviation
Attach the sign-in test record per sampled system

evidenceHint.en: Sign-in test record per sampled system: expected proof, observed behaviour, deviation and fix

templates.title: Capacity management
templates.objective: To ensure that the finite resources services depend on are measured against known ceilings and provisioned before demand reaches the level at which a service degrades.
templates.successCriteria:
The capacity register names each finite resource, the service it constrains, its measure, its present level and its ceiling.
Each resource has an acting level and an at-risk level, and each level names the action its crossing triggers.
Every register row has an observation method, an interval and a named recipient told when a level is crossed.
The period's report closes every threshold crossing with an action, and the forecast carries an exhaustion date and a provisioning decision per resource.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the capacity register with the measure, present level and ceiling recorded per resource.
Obtain the threshold list giving the acting and at-risk levels and the action each one triggers.
Obtain the observation table mapping every register row to method, interval and named recipient.
Pull the capacity report for the period showing levels reached and every crossing.
Obtain the capacity forecast with projected demand, exhaustion dates and provisioning decisions.

Analysis:
Test whether the register's ceilings match the limits the platform or the contract actually imposes.
Compare present levels in the register with the monitoring source they are said to come from.
Check that every crossing visible in the monitoring data appears in the period's report.
Verify each reported crossing reached its named recipient and closed with the action its threshold specifies.
Assess whether forecast exhaustion dates leave lead time enough for the provisioning decided.

Output:
Register accuracy findings on recorded ceilings and present levels.
Threshold crossings for the period that went unreported or unclosed.
Forecast findings naming resources whose lead time is shorter than provisioning requires.

title.en: List the finite resources whose exhaustion would degrade a service

description.en: Work back from each service in scope to the things it can run out of: processing, memory and storage, connection or record limits, network throughput, licence seats, and the people who are the constraint where no substitute exists. Give each a measure, its present level and its ceiling. Attach the capacity register.

text.en: Take each service in scope and identify the processing, memory, storage and network throughput it can run out of
Add the connection or record limits and the licence seats each service depends on
Add the people who are the constraint where no substitute for them exists
Record for each resource the measure used, its present level and its ceiling
Attach the capacity register naming the service each resource constrains

evidenceHint.en: Capacity register: resource, service it constrains, measure, present level and ceiling

title.en: Set the level at which each resource must be acted on, and the action it triggers

description.en: For every register row decide the level that obliges somebody to act and the level at which the service is at risk, and name the action each triggers — add capacity, move or shed load, remove data, obtain more seats. Size the acting level to how long that resource genuinely takes to add, not to a round number. Attach the threshold list.

text.en: Find out how long each resource on the capacity register genuinely takes to add
Set the acting level for each resource, sized to that lead time rather than to a round number
Set the level at which the service each resource supports is at risk
Name the action each level triggers: add capacity, move or shed load, remove data, or obtain more seats
Attach the threshold list with the acting level, at-risk level and triggered action per resource

evidenceHint.en: Threshold list per resource: acting level, at-risk level, and the action each triggers

title.en: Record how each capacity threshold is observed and who is told when it is crossed

description.en: For every register row state how the level is established — a continuously collected figure, a periodic report, a supplier's statement, a reading somebody takes — at what interval it is established, and the named recipient who is told when a threshold is crossed. Attach the table; a row with no observer against it is the finding it exists to produce.

text.en: Describe how each capacity register row's level is established: collected figure, periodic report, supplier statement or manual reading
State the interval at which each resource's level is established
Name the recipient told when each capacity threshold is crossed
Mark every register row with no observer against it

hint.en: A row with no observer is the finding this table exists to produce

text.en: Attach the observation table mapping each row to its method, interval and recipient

evidenceHint.en: Observation table mapping every register row to its observation method, interval and named recipient

title.en: Report the level each resource reached this period and what was done at every crossing

description.en: Bring together the period's figures for the register's resources, list every threshold crossing, and record against each what was done: capacity added, load moved, or the crossing accepted with a stated reason and a named person accepting it. Attach the report so an unactioned crossing is visible rather than absent.

text.en: Collect the period's figures for each resource on the capacity register
List every threshold crossing that occurred in the period
Note against each crossing the action taken, such as capacity added or load moved
Record any crossing accepted instead, with the stated reason and the named person accepting it
Attach the capacity report with the level reached per resource and the action closing each crossing

hint.en: An unactioned crossing must appear in the report, not be absent from it

evidenceHint.en: Capacity report for the period: level reached per resource, every crossing, and the action closing each

title.en: Project known demand against present capacity and record the provisioning decisions

description.en: Take the growth already committed — customer or headcount commitments, planned launches, data accumulating under retention rules — and work out the date each resource reaches its ceiling at that rate. Record the decision for each and when it has to start, given the lead time behind its acting level. Attach the forecast with its decisions.

text.en: Gather the growth already committed: customer or headcount commitments, planned launches and data accumulating under retention
Work out the date each resource reaches its ceiling at that rate of growth
Record the provisioning decision for each resource
Set the date each decision must start, allowing for the lead time behind its acting level
Attach the capacity forecast with the exhaustion date, decision and start date per resource

evidenceHint.en: Capacity forecast: projected demand, expected exhaustion date, and the decision and start date per resource

templates.title: Protection against malware
templates.objective: To ensure every route by which code and files reach the organisation's systems is met by a working defence, and that malicious code found on a system is dealt with under a known decision.
templates.successCriteria:
Every arrival route on the register reaches systems whose defence is recorded against that route, and undefended rows are named rather than left blank.
Removal from use and return to use of an affected system follow criteria fixed in advance, each with its deciding role named.
Each malicious code event of the period carries the system, what was found, the action taken and how it was closed.
Defences checked during verification stand in the state the register claims, and failing rows carry a remediation and a date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of routes by which code and files arrive, with the systems each route reaches.
Obtain the defence register showing the malware defence recorded against each system and route, including rows named as undefended.
Obtain the handling procedure for discovered malicious code, with its deciding roles and its removal-from-use and return-to-use criteria.
Collect the malicious code event log for the period, covering suspected as well as confirmed events.
Obtain the most recent verification of the defence register with its failing rows and the remediation against each.

Analysis:
Trace each arrival route to the systems it reaches and confirm the defence register carries a row for that pairing.
Establish whether rows marked undefended were accepted deliberately or are routes for which no defence was ever chosen.
Take the confirmed events from the log and check the steps taken and the people who decided them against the handling procedure.
Read the verification's stated coverage to see how much of the defence register was checked rather than assumed.
Follow each failing row to its remediation and confirm the date has not passed with the row still failing.

Output:
A coverage statement pairing every arrival route with the defence standing in front of it.
A list of undefended and unverified rows with the acceptance or the gap behind each.
A summary of the period's malicious code events measured against the handling procedure's criteria.

title.en: List the routes by which code and files reach the organisation's systems

description.en: Name every way something executable or file-borne arrives: messages and attachments, downloads and browsing, removable media and physical transfer, shared and collaboration spaces, software and components drawn from outside, and connections opened by suppliers. Record which systems each route reaches. Attach the register.

text.en: Name the message, attachment, download and browsing routes by which files and code reach the organisation
Add removable media and physical transfer, and shared and collaboration spaces, as arrival routes
Add software and components drawn from outside, and connections opened by suppliers
Map the systems each arrival route reaches
Attach the register of arrival routes with the systems each reaches

evidenceHint.en: Register of arrival routes with the systems each route reaches

title.en: Record the malware defence in place for each system and route in the register

description.en: Against each register row record what stands between an arriving item and its execution — detection on the system or at the route, restriction of what is permitted to run, inspection before the item is opened, or isolation of the receiving system — with who maintains that defence and how it is kept current. Rows with nothing against them are the output that matters. Attach the defence register.

text.en: Record against each route and system what stands between an arriving item and its execution
Note whether each defence is detection, restriction of what may run, inspection before opening, or isolation
Name who maintains each malware defence and how it is kept current
Mark every row with no defence against it as undefended

hint.en: The undefended rows are the output that matters; never leave them blank

text.en: Attach the defence register with the defence or the undefended status per row

evidenceHint.en: Defence register: the defence recorded against each system and route, or that row named as undefended

title.en: Record what happens when malicious code is found and who decides each step

description.en: Write the handling path: who is told, on what basis a system is taken out of use, who establishes that it is fit to return, what is done about anything the item may have reached, and the point at which the case is treated as an incident. Name roles rather than individuals so the path survives staff changes. Attach the procedure.

text.en: Write down which roles are told when malicious code is found

hint.en: Name roles rather than individuals so the path survives staff changes

text.en: Set the basis on which an affected system is taken out of use and the role that decides it
Name the role that establishes a system is fit to return to use, and the criteria applied
State what is done about anything the malicious item may have reached
Define the point at which a malicious code case is treated as an incident
Attach the handling procedure with the deciding roles and the removal and return criteria

evidenceHint.en: Handling procedure naming the deciding roles and the removal-from-use and return-to-use criteria

title.en: Record every suspected and confirmed malicious code event this period

description.en: Log each event whatever raised it — a defence that stopped or quarantined something, a person reporting a suspicious item, a supplier notification — with the system affected, what was found, what was done, and how the case closed. Items stopped before reaching a system count, and are the evidence the defence works. Attach the log.

text.en: Collect the period's events from defences that stopped or quarantined an item, people's reports and supplier notifications
Record for each event the system affected and what was found
Note what was done about each event and how the case closed
Include the items stopped before they reached any system

hint.en: These are the evidence that the defences work, so do not leave them out

text.en: Attach the malicious code event log for the period

evidenceHint.en: Malicious code event log for the period: system, what was found, action taken and closure

title.en: Check each recorded defence is in the state the register claims, and list those that are not

description.en: Go back over the defence register and establish for every row that what it records is genuinely present, still covering the systems named, and still being kept current by the person named. Record every row that fails that check together with the remediation against it and its date. Attach the verification.

text.en: Check for each row of the defence register that the recorded defence is genuinely present
Confirm each defence still covers the systems named against it
Confirm the person named is still keeping each defence current
Record each failing row with the remediation against it and its date
Attach the verification of the defence register listing the failing rows

evidenceHint.en: Verification of the defence register listing failing rows with remediation and date against each

templates.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation learns of vulnerabilities affecting the technologies it runs and brings each one to a disposition within the time its severity allows.
templates.successCriteria:
Every technology in use has a named announcement source and a named recipient of what that source publishes.
Each vulnerability of the period carries a rating band, a disposition, and the role that accepted any residual risk.
Assets missing from the period's assessment are accounted for individually with a reason and an action.
Closed vulnerabilities completed inside the elapsed time their band allows, and every overrun is explained.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the technology-to-source table with the recipient named against each source.
Obtain the rating scheme giving each band's required response, its elapsed-time allowance and the role permitted to accept risk.
Collect the period's assessment result, including the systems that could not be assessed and the reason given.
Export the vulnerability tracker for the period: affected system, disposition, date reached and acceptor per line.
Obtain the reconciliation of assessed assets against the asset inventory.

Analysis:
Compare the technology list against the asset inventory to find technologies in use that no source watches.
Take a sample of vulnerabilities published by a listed source during the period and look for each in the tracker.
Check dispositions against the scheme: the response matching the band, and accepted risk carrying the role the scheme permits.
Measure the elapsed time from each vulnerability becoming known to its disposition against the band's allowance.
Review unassessed and unreconciled assets to establish whether the gap is a coverage failure or a retired asset.

Output:
A coverage map of technologies to watching sources, with unwatched technologies listed.
A per-band table of measured elapsed times against allowance, with each overrun named.
A list of assets outside the period's assessment and the disposition of each.

title.en: Name the source that announces vulnerabilities for each technology in use

description.en: Take the technologies the organisation runs — operating systems, infrastructure and network products, databases, application platforms, and the components applications depend on — and record for each the source that would announce a weakness in it and the named person who receives that source. Attach the table; technologies with no source against them are the gap this task exists to expose.

text.en: List the technologies in use: operating systems, infrastructure and network products, databases, application platforms and components
Record the source that would announce a weakness in each technology
Name the person who receives each vulnerability source
Mark the technologies with no source against them

hint.en: These unwatched technologies are the gap the table exists to expose

text.en: Attach the technology-to-source table with the named recipient per source

evidenceHint.en: Technology-to-source table with the named recipient against each source, unwatched technologies visible

title.en: Record how a vulnerability is rated and what response each band requires

description.en: Write down what the rating takes into account — the severity as published, how exposed the affected system is, whether the weakness is known to be in use, and what the system holds — and the bands it produces. Against each band record the response required, whether to correct, to reduce by other means, or to accept, the elapsed time allowed, and who may accept. Attach the scheme.

text.en: Write down the factors the rating weighs: published severity, exposure of the system, known use of the weakness and what the system holds
Define the bands the vulnerability rating produces
Assign each band its required response: correct, reduce by other means, or accept
Set the elapsed time allowed for the response in each band
Name the role permitted to accept a vulnerability in each band
Attach the rating scheme with bands, responses, allowed times and accepting roles

evidenceHint.en: Rating scheme giving the bands, the response and elapsed time allowed for each, and the accepting role

title.en: Assess the estate against the vulnerabilities made known this period

description.en: Match what the sources announced during the period against the products and versions actually running, and produce the list of systems affected. Record the parts of the estate that could not be assessed and why, so that absence from the result is never read as cleanliness. Attach the assessment together with that exclusion list.

text.en: Collect the vulnerabilities the sources announced during the period
Match the announced vulnerabilities against the products and versions actually running
List the systems affected by each announced vulnerability
Record the parts of the estate that could not be assessed and the reason for each

hint.en: Absence from the result must never be read as a clean system

text.en: Attach the period's assessment result together with the exclusion list

evidenceHint.en: Assessment result for the period: affected systems, plus what could not be assessed and the reason

title.en: Record the disposition of every vulnerability identified this period

description.en: Give each identified vulnerability exactly one outcome: corrected, reduced by another named measure, or accepted with a stated justification and the person who accepted it. Record the date it reached that outcome, since an open item with no date is indistinguishable from a forgotten one. Attach the tracker with one line per vulnerability and affected system.

text.en: Enter each vulnerability identified this period in the tracker, one line per affected system
Give each tracker line one outcome: corrected, reduced by a named measure, or accepted
Add the justification and the accepting person to each line marked accepted
Record the date each tracker line reached its outcome

hint.en: An open item with no date is indistinguishable from a forgotten one

text.en: Export and attach the tracker with one line per vulnerability and affected system

evidenceHint.en: Tracker export: one line per vulnerability with affected system, disposition, date reached and acceptor

title.en: Account for every asset that did not appear in this period's assessment

description.en: Put the assets that appeared in the assessment beside the organisation's asset inventory and name each one missing from it, with the reason — retired, out of scope, unreachable, or simply never covered — and the action taken. Attach the reconciliation; the difference between the two lists is the part of the estate this control did not reach.

text.en: List the assets that appeared in this period's vulnerability assessment
Compare that list with the organisation's asset inventory
Name each inventory asset missing from the assessment with its reason: retired, out of scope, unreachable or never covered
Record the action taken for each missing asset
Attach the reconciliation of assessed assets against the asset inventory

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation of assessed assets against the asset inventory with a reason and action per missing asset

title.en: Measure the time taken from a vulnerability becoming known to its response completing

description.en: For the vulnerabilities closed during the period, measure the elapsed time between the source announcing it and the recorded response completing, and set that against the time its band allows. List every one that exceeded its allowance with the reason and what is being changed. Attach the measurement.

text.en: Select the vulnerabilities closed during the period
Measure for each the elapsed time from the source's announcement to the recorded response completing
Compare each elapsed time with the allowance for its band
List each overrun with its reason and what is being changed
Attach the elapsed-time measurement per closed vulnerability

evidenceHint.en: Elapsed-time measurement per closed vulnerability against its band's allowance, with each overrun explained

templates.title: Configuration management
templates.objective: To ensure each platform type runs from a defined security baseline, that new instances reach it before they hold live information, and that departures from it are known and owned.
templates.successCriteria:
Every platform type carries a governing baseline, and types with none are visible on the list rather than absent from it.
Each baseline gives a required value for every security-relevant setting and the source that value came from.
A new instance reaches baseline before it holds live information, shown by the most recent build of that platform type.
Deviations are corrected or held in the exception register with an owner and a revisit date or a stated reason for standing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the platform-type list with the instance count and governing baseline for each type.
Obtain each baseline definition: setting, required value and the source the value came from.
Obtain the per-platform statement of how a new instance is brought to baseline, with the confirmation from the most recent build.
Collect the baseline change history for the period, with the setting changed, author, date and reason.
Obtain the latest comparison of live configuration against baseline, its stated coverage, and the exception register.

Analysis:
Compare instance counts against the asset inventory to establish whether the platform-type list accounts for the live estate.
Sample settings from each baseline and confirm the required value still matches the source cited for it.
Take instances built during the period and check they reached baseline before live information was placed on them.
Read the coverage figure on the deviation comparison and work out what share of instances was actually compared.
Age the exception register to find entries past their revisit date and entries standing indefinitely with no stated reason.

Output:
A baseline coverage table of platform types, instance counts and the baseline governing each.
A list of required values that have drifted from the source they were taken from.
An aged exception register naming owners and overdue revisit dates.

title.en: List the platform types whose configuration is managed and the baseline governing each

description.en: Enumerate the platform and service types in use — operating systems, infrastructure and network devices, cloud services, databases, application platforms — with how many instances of each are running and which baseline of required settings governs it. Attach the list; a platform type with no baseline against it is the finding the list produces.

text.en: Enumerate the platform types in use: operating systems, infrastructure and network devices, cloud services, databases and application platforms
Count the running instances of each platform type
Name the baseline of required settings that governs each platform type
Mark each platform type with no baseline against it
Attach the platform-type list with instance count and governing baseline

evidenceHint.en: Platform-type list with instance count and governing baseline, types with no baseline visible

title.en: Record the required value of each security-relevant setting per platform type

description.en: For each platform type on the list, write down the settings that bear on security and the value each must hold, and name the guidance or internal decision the value was taken from. Where the chosen value departs from its source, record why. Attach the baseline for each platform type.

text.en: List the security-relevant settings for each platform type on the list
Set the value each security-relevant setting must hold
Name the guidance or internal decision each required value was taken from
Explain each chosen value that departs from its source
Attach the baseline for each platform type with setting, required value and source

evidenceHint.en: Baseline per platform type: setting, required value, and the source the value came from

title.en: Record how a new instance receives its baseline before it holds live information

description.en: State, per platform type, how a newly built instance comes to hold the required values and who confirms that it does before it carries live information or serves users. Attach the statement together with a worked example from the most recent instance built, whatever its date, showing that the confirmation actually happened; where no instance has been built since the process was written down, record that instead.

text.en: State for each platform type how a newly built instance comes to hold the required values
Name who confirms an instance meets its baseline before it holds live information or serves users
Collect the confirmation record for the most recent instance built of each platform type

hint.en: Use the most recent build whatever its date, not one picked because it looks good

text.en: Record each platform type with no instance built since the process was written down
Attach the statement together with the worked example or the record that none was built

evidenceHint.en: Per-platform statement of how a new instance is brought to baseline, with the confirmation from the most recent build or a record that none has been built since

title.en: Record every change made to a baseline definition, with its author and reason

description.en: Whenever a required value is added to, altered in, or dropped from a baseline, record who made the change, when, and why, so the baseline's present content can be traced back to decisions rather than to habit. Attach the baseline change history for the period.

text.en: Record each addition, alteration or removal of a required value in a baseline
Capture who made each baseline change and on what date
Write down the reason behind each baseline change
Attach the baseline change history for the period

evidenceHint.en: Baseline change history for the period: setting changed, author, date and reason

title.en: Compare live configuration against the governing baseline and record every deviation

description.en: Establish what values the instances a baseline governs actually hold, and where those differ from the required ones. State the coverage the comparison achieved — every instance, or a named sample and how it was chosen. Record against each deviation whether it was corrected or entered as an approved exception with an owner and either the date it is to be revisited or the reason it stands indefinitely. Attach the deviation record and the exception register.

text.en: Establish the values the instances governed by each baseline actually hold
State the coverage achieved: every instance, or a named sample and how it was chosen
List each live value that differs from the required one
Correct each deviation, or enter it as an approved exception with an owner
Record for each exception either its revisit date or the reason it stands indefinitely
Attach the deviation record and the exception register

evidenceHint.en: Deviation record stating the coverage achieved, plus the exception register carrying an owner and either a revisit date or a stated reason for standing indefinitely

title.en: Re-examine each baseline against the source its values came from and record what changed

description.en: Return to the source named against each required value — external guidance or the organisation's own recorded decision — and identify values that have moved, settings newly recommended and settings no longer relevant, updating the baseline accordingly. Attach the review record naming, for each baseline, the source consulted and the version or date of the decision it stands on, together with each required value that changed as a result.

text.en: Return to the source named against each required value, whether external guidance or the organisation's own decision
Identify values that have moved, settings newly recommended and settings no longer relevant
Update each baseline for the changes identified
Record for each baseline the source consulted and the version or date of the decision it stands on
Attach the baseline review record with each required value that changed

evidenceHint.en: Baseline review record naming the source consulted for each baseline and each required value changed as a result

templates.title: Information deletion
templates.description: Delete information when no longer needed
templates.objective: To ensure information is removed from every holding that carries a copy of it once the event that makes it due for deletion has occurred.
templates.successCriteria:
Each information category has a deletion trigger traceable to the schedule row, statute, contract or decision that fixes it.
The holdings list names every system, backup, archive, medium, environment and third party carrying a copy, each with an owner.
Holdings unable to delete on demand carry the date their copy expires and the restriction applied meanwhile.
A sample of information recorded as deleted yields no surviving copy, and unsearchable holdings are each resolved.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of information categories with the event that makes each due for deletion and the authority fixing that event.
Obtain the holdings list naming every copy of each category with its accountable owner.
Obtain the table of holding, removal method and accountable role, with expiry dates and interim restrictions where deletion on demand is impossible.
Collect the period's deletion coverage record, marked cleared, outstanding or unable against every holding.
Collect the third-party deletion confirmations received and the outstanding requests with the follow-up on each.

Analysis:
Trace a sample of triggers back to the schedule row, statute or contract cited and confirm the event is fixed there rather than assumed.
Compare the holdings list against system, backup and supplier registers to find copies the list omits.
For categories that fell due, check the coverage record marks every listed holding and not only the primary system.
Examine holdings marked unable and confirm the recorded expiry and interim restriction are actually in force.
Search the sampled holdings directly for items recorded as deleted and account for anything that comes back.

Output:
A per-category deletion coverage statement set against the full holdings list.
A list of holdings that cannot delete on demand, with expiry date and restriction for each.
Findings from the surviving-copy search and the resolution of each copy found.

title.en: Record the event that makes each information category due for deletion

description.en: For every category of information the organisation holds, record the event that makes it due for removal — a retention period expiring, a contract or an account ending, a project closing, a request from the person the information concerns, or the information no longer being needed for the purpose it was collected for — and name where that event is fixed. Where the retention schedule already fixes it, cite the schedule row and take the period as given: this control sets no periods of its own. Where a category has no row on the schedule, record its trigger and the basis for it here, so no category is left without one. Attach the list, one row per category.

text.en: List every category of information the organisation holds
Identify the event that makes each category due for deletion, such as a retention period expiring, a contract ending or a request
Cite the retention schedule row for each category it covers and take that period as given

hint.en: This control sets no retention periods of its own

text.en: Record the trigger and its basis, whether statute, contract or decision, for each category with no schedule row
Attach the list with one row per category and what fixes its deletion event

evidenceHint.en: List of information categories with the event that makes each due for deletion and the schedule row, statute, contract or decision that fixes that event

title.en: List every holding that carries a copy of each information category

description.en: Work outwards from the store of the authoritative copy to every other place a copy exists: replicas and reporting systems, backups and archives, offline and removable media, printed files, development and test environments, mailboxes and shared drives, and other organisations processing it on the organisation's behalf. Name the person accountable for each holding. Where an information asset inventory exists it names the primary systems only, so take those as the starting point and extend the list to the copies it does not carry. A deletion that misses a holding leaves the information in existence, so this list is what every later deletion is measured against. Attach it cross-referenced to the categories.

text.en: Take the primary systems from the information asset inventory, where one exists, as the starting point
Trace from each authoritative store to its replicas, reporting systems, backups and archives

hint.en: A deletion that misses one holding leaves the information in existence

text.en: Add offline and removable media, printed files, and development and test environments holding copies
Add mailboxes, shared drives and other organisations processing the information on the organisation's behalf
Name the person accountable for each holding
Attach the holdings list cross-referenced to the information categories

evidenceHint.en: Holdings list per information category naming every system, backup, archive, medium, environment and third party holding a copy, each with its accountable owner

title.en: Record the removal method that puts information beyond recovery at each holding

description.en: For every holding on the list, state how information is put beyond recovery there and the role that carries it out — overwriting in place, destruction of the medium, cryptographic erasure where the copy cannot be reached directly, or a written instruction to the organisation holding it. Where a holding cannot delete on demand, such as an append-only archive, a backup set that only expires as a whole, or a copy under legal hold, record that fact, the date the copy expires by itself, and the restriction that applies to it until then. Attach the method-per-holding table.

text.en: State for each holding how information is put beyond recovery: overwriting, medium destruction, cryptographic erasure or written instruction
Name the role that carries out removal at each holding
Identify the holdings that cannot delete on demand, such as append-only archives, whole-set backups and copies under legal hold
Record for each of those the date the copy expires by itself and the restriction applied until then
Attach the method-per-holding table with the expiry dates and interim restrictions

evidenceHint.en: Table of holding, removal method and accountable role, and — for holdings that cannot delete on demand — the date the copy expires and the restriction applied meanwhile

title.en: Clear the information that fell due and mark each recorded holding for it

description.en: Take the categories whose deletion event occurred during the period, remove the information using the method recorded for each of their holdings, then set that work against the holdings list, marking every holding cleared, still outstanding, or unable to be cleared with the reason and the restriction standing in its place meanwhile. What this produces is coverage against the holdings list rather than a second record of the disposals themselves: where a removal is already recorded elsewhere, such as a media withdrawal entry or a contractor's destruction certificate, reference that entry instead of restating it. Attach the coverage record for the period.

text.en: Identify the categories whose deletion event occurred during the period
Remove the information from each of their holdings using the method recorded for that holding
Mark every holding listed for those categories as cleared, outstanding or unable to be cleared

hint.en: This is coverage against the holdings list, not a second log of the disposals

text.en: Record the reason and the interim restriction for each holding outstanding or unable to be cleared
Reference existing removal records, such as media withdrawal entries or destruction certificates, instead of restating them
Attach the deletion coverage record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Deletion coverage record for the period: each category cleared set against every holding listed for it, marked cleared, outstanding or unable, with the reason for each exception

title.en: Obtain confirmation from each other organisation holding information that fell due

description.en: For every third party on the holdings list carrying a category that fell due this period, ask in writing for confirmation that the information has been removed from their systems, their backups and any copies they passed on further, and record the date the request went out. Attach the confirmations received alongside the parties that have not answered and the follow-up taken on each: a request sent is a different state from a deletion confirmed, and the record has to show which of the two each party is in.

text.en: Identify the third parties on the holdings list carrying a category that fell due this period
Request in writing that each confirm removal from their systems, their backups and any copies they passed on
Record the date each deletion confirmation request went out
Follow up each party that has not answered and record the follow-up taken
Attach the confirmations received alongside the outstanding requests

hint.en: A request sent is not a deletion confirmed; show which state each party is in

evidenceHint.en: Third-party deletion confirmations received for the period, plus the outstanding requests with the date sent and the follow-up taken on each

title.en: Search for surviving copies of a sample of information already recorded as deleted

description.en: Take a sample from the period's coverage record and look for that information in every holding its category lists, reaching past the systems the deletion touched directly into the backups, archives and third-party copies. Record what was searched, how it was searched, what was found, and how each surviving copy was dealt with. A search that finds nothing is the result; a holding that could not be searched at all is a finding in its own right and is recorded as one rather than passed over. Attach the verification record.

text.en: Take a sample of items from the period's deletion coverage record
Search for each sampled item in every holding its category lists, including backups, archives and third-party copies
Note each holding searched, how it was searched and what was found
Deal with each surviving copy found and record the resolution
Raise each holding that could not be searched as a finding in its own right
Attach the deletion verification record

evidenceHint.en: Verification record: items sampled, holdings searched, surviving copies found, holdings that could not be searched, and the resolution of each

templates.title: Data masking
templates.description: Mask data per access control policy
templates.objective: To ensure people who are not entitled to a data item's real value receive an obscured one instead, and that real values reach anyone only on a recorded decision.
templates.successCriteria:
Each restricted item names the obligation behind it and the user populations entitled to its real value.
Every screen, report, extract and interface carrying a listed item shows the recorded treatment to users outside those populations.
Where a treatment is reversible, the register names who may reverse it and each reversal appears as a recorded disclosure.
Attempts on sampled items from a non-entitled position return the obscured form, and any real value obtained has a fix raised.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of restricted items with the obligation behind each and the populations entitled to the real value.
Obtain the treatment record: what is presented instead of the real value, whether it is reversible, and who can reverse it.
Collect the sample output from each screen, report, extract and interface as a non-entitled user receives it.
Obtain the period's record of real-value disclosures with requester, reason, approver and duration, together with the refusals.
Obtain the results of the attempts made to reach listed items from a non-entitled position.

Analysis:
Compare the register against data inventories and stated obligations to find items that should be restricted but are not listed.
Check each sample output against the recorded treatment and note any place where the real value still appears.
Confirm that the people able to reverse a treatment are the people the entitlement and approval records name.
Reconcile the disclosure record against reversal and access activity to find real values released without a record.
Repeat a sample of the non-entitled attempts independently and compare what returns with what the register claims.

Output:
An item-by-item statement of where the recorded treatment is applied and where it is not.
A list of disclosures and reversals found that the disclosure record does not carry.
Results of the independent attempts, with a fix raised for each item that yielded its real value.

title.en: List the data items whose real values must be hidden from some of the people who use them

description.en: Working from the organisation's access decisions and its obligations over personal and other regulated data, name the specific items — identifiers, contact details, financial values, health data — that must not show their real value to everyone who legitimately uses the record, and the user populations entitled to see them in full. Attach the register giving, per item, the obligation behind it and the entitled populations.

text.en: Collect the organisation's access decisions and its obligations over personal and other regulated data
Name the items, such as identifiers, contact details, financial values and health data, that must not show their real value to every user
Record the obligation behind each restricted item
Name the user populations entitled to see each item in full
Attach the register of restricted items with obligation and entitled populations

evidenceHint.en: Register of restricted items with the obligation behind each and the user populations entitled to the real value

title.en: Record how each listed item is obscured and whether the real value can be recovered

description.en: For each item in the register state what a non-entitled user sees instead — nothing, part of the value, a substitute, an aggregate — whether the real value can be recovered from what is shown, and who holds the means to recover it. Attach the register extended with the treatment, its reversibility and the holder of the recovery means.

text.en: Record for each restricted item what a non-entitled user sees instead: nothing, part of the value, a substitute or an aggregate
Determine whether the real value can be recovered from what is shown
Name who holds the means to recover the real value for each reversible treatment
Attach the register extended with treatment, reversibility and holder of the recovery means

evidenceHint.en: Register showing, per item, what is presented instead of the real value, whether it is reversible and who can reverse it

title.en: Apply the recorded treatment everywhere a listed item is shown or handed out in day-to-day use

description.en: Work through the screens, reports, printed output, extracts and interfaces to other parties where each item appears in normal operation, and make each of them present the item as the register requires. Attach, for each of those points, a sample of its output showing the item as a non-entitled user actually receives it.

text.en: List the screens, reports, printed output, extracts and interfaces to other parties where each item appears in normal use
Configure each of those points to present the item as the masking register requires
Capture a sample of each point's output as a non-entitled user receives it

hint.en: Capture it through non-entitled access, not an administrator's or developer's view

text.en: Attach the sample output for each screen, report, extract and interface

evidenceHint.en: Sample output from each screen, report, extract or interface showing the item as a non-entitled user receives it

title.en: Record each occasion a person is given the real value of a listed item

description.en: Whenever someone outside the entitled population is shown or sent an unobscured value — for an investigation, a support case, a legal request — record the item, who asked, the reason given, who agreed and how long the access lasted. Attach the record covering the period, including requests that were refused.

text.en: Log each occasion someone outside the entitled population is shown or sent an unobscured value
Capture for each disclosure the item, who asked, the reason given, who agreed and how long the access lasted
Include the requests for a real value that were refused alongside those granted
Attach the record of real-value disclosures and refusals for the period

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period of every disclosure of a real value: item, requester, reason, approver, duration, and refusals

title.en: Establish what a non-entitled user can actually obtain of a sample of listed items

description.en: Take items from the register and, using access that belongs to a population not entitled to the real value, try to obtain that value by the means genuinely available to such a user — searching or filtering on it, exporting or building a report, calling an interface, or asking a system that receives a copy. Record for each attempt what came back and whether the real value, or enough of it to reconstruct the value, was obtainable. Confirm in the same pass that the means of recovering a real value is still held only by the people the register names. Raise a fix with an owner for every attempt that succeeded. Attach the results.

text.en: Pick a sample of items from the masking register to test
Obtain access belonging to a population not entitled to each sampled item's real value
Attempt to obtain the real value by searching or filtering, exporting, building a report, calling an interface, or asking a receiving system
Record what came back and whether the real value, or enough to reconstruct it, was obtainable
Confirm the means of recovering a real value is still held only by the people the register names
Raise a fix with an owner for every successful attempt and attach the results

evidenceHint.en: Results per item attempted: the access used, what came back, whether the real value was obtainable, and the fix raised where it was

templates.title: Data leakage prevention
templates.objective: To ensure information that must not leave uncontrolled meets a measure on every route out, and that departures which are permitted happen the sanctioned way.
templates.successCriteria:
Each information category states the departure permitted for it and names who agreed that position.
Every route in scope carries a measure with an owner, and unrestricted routes carry a named acceptance rather than silence.
The people who handle identified information have received the issued handling instruction, shown by its distribution list.
Ways out that appeared during the period were given a measure and a decider, or the period is recorded as producing none.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the table of information categories with the departure permitted for each and the person who agreed it.
Obtain the route-to-measure register with each measure's owner and the acceptance recorded against unrestricted routes.
Obtain the issued handling instruction, its date and the distribution list showing who received it.
Collect the period's additions to the register, or the statement that no new way out appeared.
Collect the suspected leakage records for the period and the results of the tests run against each measure in force.

Analysis:
Compare the register against egress, endpoint and collaboration tooling to find ways out that it does not carry.
Check each route's measure is at least as strict as the tightest departure position among the categories that route can carry.
Compare the distribution list against the population that handles identified information and identify who never received the instruction.
Read the suspected leakage records for routes or categories the register did not anticipate.
Compare the behaviour observed in each measure's test with the behaviour the register claims for it.

Output:
A route-by-route statement of the measure in force and the categories that route can carry.
A list of unrestricted and unregistered routes with the acceptance or the gap behind each.
Test findings per measure, with the corrections made where behaviour differed from the register.

title.en: Record the information that must not leave uncontrolled and what may happen when it does leave

description.en: Name the categories of information whose unauthorised disclosure would harm the organisation or breach an obligation, and state for each what may happen when it leaves: it must not leave at all, it may leave only with a named person's agreement, it may leave but what passes must be recorded or examined, or it may leave unrestricted with the exposure accepted. Name who agreed the position for each category. Take the organisation's transfer routes as already listed elsewhere and do not enumerate them again here. Attach the table, one row per category.

text.en: Name the categories of information whose unauthorised disclosure would harm the organisation or breach an obligation

hint.en: Take the transfer routes as already listed elsewhere; do not enumerate them again here

text.en: State for each category the departure allowed: not at all, on a named person's agreement, recorded or examined, or unrestricted
Record who agreed the departure position for each category
Attach the table with one row per information category

evidenceHint.en: Table of information categories, the departure allowed for each — not at all, on agreement, recorded or examined, or unrestricted — and who agreed it

title.en: Record the measure standing in front of each route that is in scope

description.en: For every in-scope route state which applies: the route is closed altogether, it is open only with a named person's agreement, it is open but what passes is recorded or examined, or it is open unrestricted with the exposure accepted. Name the owner of each measure and, for anything left unrestricted, who accepted it. Attach the route-to-measure register.

text.en: Record for each in-scope route whether it is closed, open on agreement, open but recorded or examined, or open unrestricted
Name the owner of the measure on each route
Name who accepted the exposure for each route left unrestricted
Attach the route-to-measure register with each route's measure, owner and any named acceptance

evidenceHint.en: Route-to-measure register: route, the measure in force, its owner, and the named acceptance of any route left unrestricted

title.en: Issue the handling instruction telling people the sanctioned way to send each kind of identified information

description.en: Turn the register into an instruction the people who handle this information can act on: for each closed or controlled route, the sanctioned alternative and who to ask when there is none. Attach the issued instruction with its date and the list of people or groups it was sent to.

text.en: Identify from the route-to-measure register each route that is closed or controlled
Write the sanctioned alternative for each such route, and who to ask where there is none
Issue the handling instruction to the people and groups who handle the identified information
Attach the issued instruction with its date and the distribution list

evidenceHint.en: The issued handling instruction, its date, and the distribution list showing who received it

title.en: Record each new way information could leave that appeared this period and the measure decided for it

description.en: As a new service, device type, connection or working arrangement comes into use that gives information a further way out of the organisation, record what it is, who noticed it, which categories it could carry, and the measure decided for it — closed, allowed only under a condition, watched, or accepted — together with who decided. Where nothing new appeared in the period, record that. Attach the additions made to the route-to-measure register during the period.

text.en: Identify each new service, device type, connection or working arrangement that gave information a further way out this period
Record who noticed each new way out and which information categories it could carry
Name the measure decided for each, whether closed, allowed under a condition, watched or accepted, and who decided
Add each new way out to the route-to-measure register, or state that none appeared in the period
Attach the period's additions to the route-to-measure register

evidenceHint.en: Additions to the route-to-measure register for the period: the new way out, who noticed it, the categories it could carry, the measure decided and the decider, or a statement that none appeared

title.en: Record each suspected leakage raised this period and what was done about it

description.en: Take every case that came to notice however it arrived — a person reporting a mistake, something found in an examination of a controlled route, a recipient or supplier telling the organisation, a routine check — and record what was suspected, what was established, the action taken and any change made to the route measures. Attach the record for the period.
