text.en: Collect every suspected leakage however it arrived: a reported mistake, a route examination, a recipient or supplier, or a routine check
Record what was suspected and what was established for each case
Note the action taken and any change made to the route measures
Attach the suspected leakage record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period: each suspected leakage, how it came to notice, what was established, the action taken and any change to the measures

title.en: Test each measure in force against uncontrolled departure and record whether it behaved as recorded

description.en: Take the measures on the route-to-measure register one at a time and establish what each actually does with harmless data of the identified kind: for a measure recorded as closing a way out, attempt to use it; for one that requires an agreement, attempt without the agreement; for one that records or examines what passes, send something and then look for it in what was recorded; for anything left accepted, confirm the acceptance is still held by the person named. Record the result against each measure and the correction made wherever the behaviour did not match the register. Attach the results.

text.en: Attempt to use each way out recorded as closed, using harmless data of the identified kind

hint.en: Use harmless test data of the identified kind, never real restricted information

text.en: Attempt each agreement-controlled route without the agreement
Send harmless data through each recorded or examined route and look for it in what was recorded
Confirm the acceptance of each unrestricted route is still held by the person named
Record the result per measure and the correction made where behaviour did not match the register
Attach the test results per measure in force

evidenceHint.en: Results per measure in force: what was attempted against it, what it did, and the correction made where the behaviour did not match the register

templates.title: Information backup
templates.objective: To ensure copies of the information the organisation depends on exist at the frequency and retention it requires, are protected in their own right, and have been shown to restore.
templates.successCriteria:
Every registered system and dataset is covered by a job running to the required frequency and retention, including a separately held copy.
Backup copies are encrypted and reachable only by the restricted set of accounts recorded for them.
Each failure in the period's job outcomes carries a resolution and a copy eventually produced.
A restore performed in the period returned verified data, with the backup set used and the elapsed time recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the backup register of systems and datasets with their required frequency and retention.
Obtain the backup job configurations, including the job writing the separately held copy.
Obtain the encryption settings and the access list for the backup copies and the storage holding them.
Collect the period's backup job status report with the resolution recorded against each failure.
Obtain the restore test record: backup set restored, verification performed and elapsed time.
Obtain the reconciliation of configured jobs against the systems inventory.

Analysis:
Compare each job's schedule and retention against what the register requires for that system or dataset.
Confirm the separately held copy is genuinely separate, not a second copy on the same platform or in the same failure domain.
Review who can read, alter or delete backup copies and compare that set with the accounts administering the source systems.
Follow each failed job to its resolution and establish whether a good copy was produced before the next one fell due.
Read the reconciliation for systems present in the inventory that no configured job covers.

Output:
A register-to-job comparison showing frequency and retention met or missed for each system.
A statement of the restore test's scope, verification result and elapsed time.
A list of inventory systems with no backup job and the decision taken on each.

title.en: Register the systems and datasets in backup scope with their required frequency and retention

description.en: List what must be backed up, how often each item needs a copy taken, and how long copies are kept, derived from the business need for that data. Attach the backup scope register showing system, dataset, frequency and retention.

text.en: List the systems and datasets that must be backed up
Set how often each dataset needs a copy taken, derived from the business need for that data
Set how long copies of each dataset are kept
Attach the backup scope register showing system, dataset, frequency and retention

title.en: Configure the backup jobs to the registered schedule, including a copy held separately

description.en: Set up jobs covering every entry in the register, with at least one copy kept in a separate location or account so a failure at the primary site does not take the backups with it. Attach the job configuration export mapped line by line to the register.

text.en: Configure a backup job for every entry in the scope register at its registered frequency and retention
Configure at least one copy held in a separate location or account from the primary

hint.en: A copy in the same site or account can be lost in the same failure as the primary

text.en: Export the backup job configuration
Map each exported job line by line to its register entry and mark entries with no job
Attach the mapped job configuration export

title.en: Apply encryption and access restriction to the backup copies

description.en: Encrypt backup data at rest and in transit and limit who can read, alter or delete the backup repository, recording where the keys are held. Attach the encryption and access-control configuration for the backup repository, with the list of accounts holding delete rights.

text.en: Enable encryption of backup data at rest and in transit
Record where the backup encryption keys are held
Restrict who can read, alter or delete the backup repository
List the accounts holding delete rights on the backup repository
Attach the repository's encryption and access-control configuration with the delete-rights list

title.en: Review the backup job outcomes for this period and resolve every failure

description.en: Check the completion status of each scheduled job, investigate failed and partial runs, and record the fix or the re-run. Attach the job status report for the period showing each job's result and the resolution of any failure.

text.en: Check the completion status of each scheduled backup job for the period
Investigate each failed or partial backup run
Record the fix or the re-run for each backup failure
Attach the backup job status report with the resolution recorded per failure

evidenceHint.en: Backup job status report for the period, with the resolution recorded per failure

title.en: Restore data from backup and record what came back and how long it took

description.en: Perform an actual restore into an isolated environment, verify the restored data is complete and usable, and note the elapsed time. Attach the restore test record naming the backup set used, the data verified and the duration — a job that reports success is not proof the data is recoverable.

text.en: Select a backup set and restore it into an isolated environment

hint.en: A job that reports success is not proof the data can be recovered

text.en: Verify the restored data is complete and usable
Record the elapsed time the restore took
Attach the restore test record naming the backup set, the verification performed and the duration

evidenceHint.en: Restore test record: backup set restored, verification performed, elapsed time

title.en: Reconcile the configured backup jobs against the systems inventory to expose unprotected systems

description.en: Compare the systems actually covered by a running job against the full systems inventory, and list every system with no backup. Attach the reconciliation with each gap and the decision taken — add a job, or record why the system needs none.

text.en: List the systems covered by a running backup job
Compare those systems with the full systems inventory
List every system in the inventory with no backup
Decide for each gap whether to add a job or record why the system needs none
Attach the reconciliation with each unprotected system and the decision taken

templates.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
templates.objective: To ensure services carry enough redundancy to meet the availability their owners require, and that switching to it has been exercised rather than assumed.
templates.successCriteria:
Each in-scope processing facility has a stated availability requirement attributable to its business owner.
Identified single points of failure are each addressed by a provisioned redundant component or recorded as accepted.
A failover exercise has moved each covered service onto its redundant component, with switchover time and issues recorded.
Availability measured over the period meets the recorded requirement, and every shortfall is explained.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the availability requirement recorded for each in-scope information processing facility.
Obtain the architecture records identifying the single points of failure in each in-scope service.
Obtain evidence that the redundant component provisioned for each addressed single point of failure is live.
Collect the failover test records: service, component failed over, switchover time and issues found.
Obtain the measured availability figures for each service over the period.

Analysis:
Check that each availability requirement traces to a business owner rather than to an infrastructure default.
Review the architecture for shared dependencies the analysis missed, such as a common power feed, network path or management plane.
Confirm each redundant component is independent of the one it stands behind, including where both come from a single provider.
Compare switchover times observed in the failover tests against the availability requirement they exist to support.
Compare measured availability with the requirement and trace each shortfall to the failure that caused it.

Output:
A facility-by-facility table of availability requirement, single points of failure and the redundancy provided.
A summary of the failover exercises with switchover times and the issues still open.
A variance statement of measured availability against requirement, naming the cause of each shortfall.

title.en: Record the availability requirement for each information processing facility in scope

description.en: For every service or facility the business depends on, state the availability it must sustain and the maximum tolerable outage, agreed with the service owner. Attach the service list with those targets — redundancy decisions are only assessable against a stated requirement.

text.en: List each service or facility the business depends on
Agree with each service owner the availability the service must sustain
Agree with each service owner the maximum tolerable outage
Attach the service list with its availability and outage targets

hint.en: Redundancy decisions can only be assessed against a stated requirement

title.en: Identify the single points of failure in each in-scope service's architecture

description.en: Walk each service's components — compute, storage, network path, power, supplier dependency — and mark every element whose loss would stop the service. Attach the analysis per service listing the single points of failure found.

text.en: Walk through each in-scope service's compute, storage and network path
Check the power and supplier dependencies of each service
Mark every element whose loss would stop the service
Attach the analysis listing the single points of failure found per service

title.en: Provision the redundant component for each single point of failure being addressed

description.en: Put the duplicate component, alternate path or standby facility in place for the failure points the availability requirement demands, and record the ones deliberately left unaddressed with the reason. Attach the architecture record showing the redundant path per service.

text.en: Select the single points of failure the availability requirement demands be addressed
Put the duplicate component, alternate path or standby facility in place for each
Record each failure point deliberately left unaddressed, with the reason
Attach the architecture record showing the redundant path per service

title.en: Fail over to the redundant component and record the switchover result

description.en: Take the primary component out of service under controlled conditions, confirm the service continues on the redundant one, and record the time taken to switch and anything that did not carry over. Attach the failover test record per service tested.

text.en: Plan the controlled conditions under which the primary component is taken out of service
Take the primary out of service and confirm the service continues on the redundant component
Measure the time taken to switch over to the redundant component
Record anything that did not carry over to the redundant component
Attach the failover test record per service tested

evidenceHint.en: Failover test record: service, component failed over, switchover time, issues found

title.en: Compare measured availability against the recorded requirement for each service

description.en: Pull the actual uptime and outage duration for the period and set it beside each service's stated target, identifying every service that fell short and why. Attach the availability report with the shortfalls and the remedial action agreed.

text.en: Pull the actual uptime and outage duration for each service over the period
Compare each with the service's stated availability target and maximum tolerable outage
Identify each service that fell short and why
Agree the remedial action for each availability shortfall
Attach the availability report with the shortfalls and the remedial actions

templates.title: Logging
templates.objective: To ensure systems produce a record of the events that matter, that those records survive where they are kept, and that a source falling silent is noticed.
templates.successCriteria:
Every system in the logging register produces the event classes recorded against it and delivers them to the stated destination.
Each source has a holding place, form and retention period recorded, and systems recording nothing carry a stated reason.
The people able to alter or remove stored records are a named minimum, each with the reason they keep that ability.
Delivery gaps found in the period were raised and closed, and an ordinary administrator's attempt to alter a stored record did not pass unnoticed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the logging register: system, event classes recorded, destination, and the systems recording nothing with the reason given.
Obtain the holding place, form and retention period recorded for every source.
Obtain, per holding place, the named list of people able to alter or remove stored records and the reason each retains it.
Collect the delivery check for the period showing each source's most recent record and the gaps raised.
Obtain the record of the alteration and removal attempts made with an ordinary administrator's access.

Analysis:
Compare the register against the asset inventory to find systems producing nothing that were never asked to produce anything.
Generate a sample of events on live systems and confirm the corresponding record arrived at the stated destination.
Retrieve the oldest record still held for a sample of sources and compare its age with the retention period recorded.
Review the alter-and-remove lists for accounts that also administer the systems whose records they can reach.
Read the attempt results and confirm the restriction was changed wherever an attempt succeeded.

Output:
A source-by-source statement of event classes recorded, destination reached and retention achieved.
A list of delivery gaps during the period with the closure of each.
Findings from the alteration and removal attempts and the restrictions tightened as a result.

title.en: Record the events each system must produce a record of, and where those records go

description.en: Go through the systems in use and decide, per system, which classes of event are recorded — sign-in and sign-in failure, use of elevated rights, access to held information, configuration change, error and failure. Where a system produces no record, enter it with the reason rather than omitting it. Attach the logging register, one row per system with its event classes and the destination the records are kept in.

text.en: Decide per system which event classes it records: sign-in and sign-in failure, use of elevated rights, access to held information, configuration change, error
Record the destination where each system's records are kept
Enter each system that produces no record, with the reason, rather than omitting it
Attach the logging register with one row per system

evidenceHint.en: Logging register: system, event classes recorded, destination, and the systems recording nothing with the reason

title.en: Record where each source's records are kept and for how long

description.en: For every source in the register, record the place the records are held, the form they are held in, and how long they are kept before disposal — stated per event class where the periods differ. Attach the register extended with the holding place, form and retention for every source.

text.en: Name for each logging source the place its records are held
Note the form each source's records are held in
State how long records are kept before disposal, per event class where the periods differ
Attach the logging register extended with holding place, form and retention

evidenceHint.en: Logging register extended with the holding place, form and retention period for every source

title.en: Reduce the set of people able to alter or remove stored records to a named minimum

description.en: For each holding place, establish who can change or delete a record once it is stored and cut that to the smallest named set, kept separate from the people who administer the systems the records come from. Attach, per holding place, the list of who retains that ability with the reason each is on it.

text.en: Establish for each holding place who can change or delete a record once stored
Cut that set to the smallest named list of people
Remove from the list anyone who administers the systems the records come from
Record the reason each remaining person retains the ability
Attach the named list per holding place with the reason against each person

evidenceHint.en: Per holding place, the named list of people able to alter or remove stored records, with the reason each retains it

title.en: Confirm every source in the register is still producing records and raise the gaps

description.en: For each source, find the most recent record it produced and compare that against how often the source is expected to produce one. Raise every source silent beyond its expected interval with the person accountable for it, by whatever route the organisation uses to pursue such things, and record what the investigation found. Attach the check covering the period.

text.en: Find the most recent record each source in the logging register produced
Compare it with how often the source is expected to produce a record
Raise each source silent beyond its expected interval with the person accountable for it
Record what the investigation of each silent source found
Attach the period's delivery check with each source's latest record and the gaps raised

evidenceHint.en: Delivery check for the period: source, most recent record, the gaps raised and the outcome of each

title.en: Attempt to alter and to remove a stored record using an ordinary administrator's access

description.en: With the owner's agreement, use an account that administers a logged system to try first to change and then to delete one of that system's stored records, and record exactly what the holding place did in each case. Attach the test record naming the access used, the attempts made, the result of each, and any restriction changed afterwards.

text.en: Agree the tamper test with the owner of the logged system
Use an account that administers the logged system to try to change one of its stored records

hint.en: Use the logged system's administrator, not someone already on the named list for the store

text.en: Attempt with the same access to delete one of the stored records
Record exactly what the holding place did in response to each attempt
Change any restriction the test shows to be inadequate and record the change
Attach the test record naming the access used, the attempts and their results

evidenceHint.en: Test record: the access used, the attempts made, the result of each, and the restriction changed as a result

templates.title: Monitoring activities
templates.objective: To ensure the behaviours the organisation has decided to watch for are actually looked for, reach someone who acts on them, and are seen when they occur.
templates.successCriteria:
Each watched target names the behaviours it is watched for and the record or signal each is recognised from.
Every listed behaviour has a method, frequency and owner for looking, and those with no method remain visible on the list.
Observations in the period reached the person the routing table names and carry a disposition and the action taken.
The behaviour produced deliberately was noticed, routed and acted on, with the time each step took recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the watch list of targets, the behaviours each is watched for, and the record or signal each behaviour is recognised from.
Obtain the extended watch list showing how, how often and by whom each behaviour is looked for, including behaviours with no method.
Obtain the routing table: behaviour, who is told, how word reaches them, the first action expected and the escalation.
Collect the period's observation record with dispositions, actions taken and any resulting change to the watch list.
Obtain the exercise record for the behaviour produced deliberately.

Analysis:
Compare the watch list against the systems and networks in the asset inventory to find targets nobody watches.
Confirm the record or signal named for a behaviour exists on that target and is kept long enough to be looked at.
Establish how many listed behaviours still have no method and whether those are the ones most relied upon.
Trace sampled observations from the first record through routing to disposition and measure the time each step took.
Compare the exercise timeline against the first action and escalation the routing table expects.

Output:
A watch list coverage statement separating behaviours with a working method from those without.
A timeline for the sampled observations from occurrence to disposition.
The exercise result: whether the produced behaviour was noticed, by whom, and the correction made.

title.en: Record which systems and networks are watched and the behaviour each is watched for

description.en: For every watched target, name the behaviour that would matter — repeated failed sign-ins, access at an unusual hour, an unexpected outbound connection, rights being raised, a service stopping — and the record or signal that behaviour would show up in. A target entered simply as 'monitored' says nothing; the behaviour is the entry. Attach the watch list.

text.en: List every system and network target that is watched
Name for each target the behaviour that would matter, such as repeated failed sign-ins, unusual-hour access or rights being raised
Identify the record or signal each behaviour would be recognised from
Attach the watch list of targets, behaviours and signals

hint.en: A target entered as monitored with no behaviour against it says nothing

evidenceHint.en: Watch list: target, the behaviours watched for, and the record or signal each would be recognised from

title.en: Record how each listed behaviour is looked for and how often

description.en: For every row of the watch list, say whether the behaviour is looked for continuously, at a stated interval by a named person reading the records, or in a report produced on a schedule — and who does the looking. Where a behaviour is not looked for at all today, record it as a gap rather than leaving the row blank. Attach the watch list extended with method, interval and person, plus the gap list.

text.en: Record for each watch-list row whether it is looked for continuously, at a stated interval, or in a scheduled report
Name the person or team who does the looking for each row
Enter each behaviour not looked for at all today as a gap rather than a blank row
Attach the extended watch list together with the gap list

evidenceHint.en: Watch list extended with how, how often and by whom each behaviour is looked for, plus the behaviours with no method yet

title.en: Name who is told when a listed behaviour is seen and what they do first

description.en: For each behaviour, name the team or rota that is told, the way word reaches them, the first action expected of them — investigate, escalate, or set aside with a stated reason — and who it passes to if they do not act. Attach the routing table covering every row of the watch list.

text.en: Name the team or rota told when each watched behaviour is seen
Record how word of each behaviour reaches them
State the first action expected: investigate, escalate, or set aside with a stated reason
Name who each behaviour passes to if the first recipient does not act
Attach the routing table covering every row of the watch list

evidenceHint.en: Routing table: behaviour, who is told, how word reaches them, the first action expected, and the escalation

title.en: Record every observation of a watched behaviour in the period and its disposition

description.en: Take the observations that arose, however they arose, and record for each what was seen, when, who dealt with it, whether it turned out to be genuine, mistaken or already known, what was done in response, and any change made to the watch list as a result. Attach the observation record for the period.

text.en: Collect the observations of watched behaviours that arose in the period, however they arose
Record for each observation what was seen, when, and who dealt with it
Mark each observation as genuine, mistaken or already known
Note the action taken and any change made to the watch list as a result
Attach the period's observation record with the disposition of each observation

evidenceHint.en: Observation record for the period: what was seen, when, who dealt with it, the disposition, the action taken and any change to the watch list

title.en: Produce a watched behaviour deliberately and record whether it was noticed

description.en: Choose a behaviour from the watch list, arrange with the target's owner to produce it at a known time, then record whether it was noticed, how long afterwards, by whom, and whether the person named to be told actually heard. Where it went unnoticed, record what was changed. Attach the exercise record.

text.en: Choose a behaviour from the watch list to produce deliberately
Arrange with the target's owner to produce it at a known time
Record whether it was noticed, how long afterwards and by whom
Confirm whether the person named to be told actually heard
Correct the gap wherever the behaviour went unnoticed and record what was changed
Attach the exercise record with the time produced, the time noticed and the correction made

evidenceHint.en: Exercise record: behaviour produced, time produced, whether and when it was noticed, by whom, who was told, and the correction made

templates.title: Clock synchronization
templates.objective: To ensure timestamps recorded across the estate refer to the same time, so that events on different systems can be placed in order against one another.
templates.successCriteria:
Every system that records timestamps appears in the clock inventory with the source it currently uses.
A written standard names the primary and fallback time source, the protocol and the maximum offset tolerated.
Systems in the inventory point at the approved source, and each one that could not be repointed is listed with its reason.
Offsets measured in the period fall within tolerance, and every system outside it has a recorded correction.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the clock inventory: system, configured time source and the offset measured at the time of the check.
Obtain the written time standard with its primary and fallback source, protocol and maximum tolerated offset.
Obtain the per-system configuration output taken after repointing, and the list of systems that could not be repointed.
Collect the period's offset readings with systems outside tolerance flagged and the correction recorded against each.
Obtain the correlated event trace showing one event in the logs of two systems.

Analysis:
Compare the clock inventory against the systems that produce timestamped records to find sources it does not cover.
Read the configured time source directly on a sample of systems instead of relying on the recorded value.
Measure current offsets independently and compare them with the tolerance the standard sets.
Consider what the timestamps of the systems that could not be repointed are worth when events must be placed in order.
Read the correlated trace and check the timestamp difference between the two systems against the tolerance.

Output:
An inventory-wide statement of configured source and measured offset for each system.
A list of systems outside tolerance or pointing somewhere other than the approved source.
The correlation result with the timestamp difference and the follow-up raised on it.

title.en: List every system that records timestamps and the time source it currently uses

description.en: Go through the systems inventory — servers, network devices, workstations, appliances and hosted services — and record for each the time source it is presently configured against and the offset measured at the time of the check. Attach the clock inventory with a row per system.

text.en: Take each system from the systems inventory, including servers, network devices, workstations, appliances and hosted services
Record the time source each system is presently configured against
Measure each system's clock offset at the time of the check
Attach the clock inventory with a row per system

evidenceHint.en: Clock inventory: system, current configured time source, measured offset at the time of the check.

title.en: Record the approved time source and the tolerated drift in a written standard

description.en: Name the primary and fallback time source, the protocol used to reach them, and the maximum offset a system may show before it is treated as a fault. State which system classes the standard covers and how a system without direct reachability to the source is served. Attach the standard.

text.en: Name the primary and fallback time source
Record the protocol used to reach the time sources
Set the maximum offset a system may show before it is treated as a fault
State which system classes the time standard covers
Describe how a system with no direct reach to the time source is served
Attach the written time standard naming the sources, the protocol and the maximum tolerated offset

evidenceHint.en: Written time standard naming the primary and fallback source, the protocol and the maximum tolerated offset.

title.en: Point each system in the clock inventory at the approved time source

description.en: Reconfigure every system whose recorded source is not the approved one, working through the inventory, and record the systems that cannot be changed together with the reason and the arrangement covering them. Attach the per-system configuration output showing the source in effect after the change.

text.en: Identify from the clock inventory each system whose time source is not the approved one
Reconfigure each such system to use the approved time source
Record each system that cannot be repointed, with the reason and the arrangement covering it
Capture each system's configuration output showing the source in effect after the change
Attach the configuration output with the list of systems not repointed

evidenceHint.en: Per-system configuration output after the change, plus the list of systems that could not be repointed and why.

title.en: Measure the clock offset of each system against the approved source

description.en: Run the offset check across the inventory, record the reading for every system, and raise the systems exceeding the tolerated drift for correction, noting what was done. Attach the offset readings for the period.

text.en: Run the offset check across every system in the clock inventory
Record the offset reading for each system
Flag each system exceeding the tolerated drift and raise it for correction
Note the correction made for each flagged system
Attach the period's offset readings with out-of-tolerance systems and their corrections marked

evidenceHint.en: Offset readings for the period, one per system, with systems outside tolerance flagged and the correction recorded.

title.en: Trace one event across the logs of two systems and compare the recorded timestamps

description.en: Choose an event both systems record — a sign-in crossing an authentication service and an application, for instance — extract the timestamp each wrote, and compare the difference against the tolerated drift in the standard. Attach the correlated trace showing both log entries, the difference, and any follow-up raised.

text.en: Choose an event two systems both record, such as a sign-in crossing an authentication service and an application
Extract the timestamp each system wrote for that event
Compare the difference between the timestamps with the tolerated drift in the standard
Raise a follow-up where the difference exceeds the tolerated drift
Attach the correlated trace with both log entries, the difference and any follow-up

evidenceHint.en: Correlated event trace with both systems' log entries, the timestamp difference and the follow-up raised.

templates.title: Use of privileged utility programs
templates.objective: To ensure programs able to override a system or application control exist only where someone is permitted to run them, and that every run can be attributed to a person and a reason.
templates.successCriteria:
The inventory names, for each such program, the systems it is installed on and the control it can override.
Programs with a permitted user carry the role permitted, the systems that role covers and the circumstance justifying a run.
Programs with no permitted user are removed, placed beyond ordinary reach, or left under an accepted compensating restriction.
Every recorded run matches an entry in the permission record, and each unmatched run has been resolved individually.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the inventory of programs able to override a control, with the systems each is installed on and the control it overrides.
Obtain the permission record: program, permitted role, the systems covered and the circumstance justifying a run.
Obtain the before-and-after state per system for programs with no permitted user, including any accepted compensating restriction.
Collect the period's run records with the person, system, date and stated reason for each run.
Obtain the comparison of recorded runs against the permission record and the resolution of the unmatched runs.

Analysis:
Scan a sample of systems for override-capable programs and compare what is present with what the inventory lists.
Check that the role permitted for each program is held only by people whose duties require it on those systems.
Confirm removal or restriction actually took effect on the systems claimed rather than being recorded as intended.
Invoke a listed program under observation and establish whether a run record appeared for it.
Read the unmatched runs for a pattern: a role that outgrew its permission, or a system with no owner.

Output:
An inventory-to-system reconciliation naming override-capable programs found but not listed.
A comparison of recorded runs against permitted ones, with the resolution of each unmatched run.
A list of programs left in place with no permitted user and the restriction relied on for each.

title.en: List the programs able to override a system or application control, and where they are installed

description.en: Go through the builds in service for tools that can bypass an access check, write directly to storage or memory, read or reset credentials, or change what is recorded. Record each one with the systems it is present on and the specific control it is able to override. Attach the inventory.

text.en: Gather the build definitions or images for each class of system in service
Identify in each build the tools able to bypass an access check, write directly to storage or memory, read or reset credentials, or alter what is recorded
Record every system on which each identified tool is present
Name against each tool the specific control it is able to override

hint.en: Name the control overridden, such as file permissions, not what the tool generally does

text.en: Attach the inventory of privileged utility programs, their systems and the controls they override

evidenceHint.en: Inventory: program, the systems it is present on, and the control it is able to override

title.en: Record who may run each listed program, on which systems, and in what circumstance

description.en: For every entry in the inventory, name the role permitted to run it, the systems that permission covers, and the circumstance that justifies a run — a recovery, an examination, a migration. Where no role needs it, mark the entry for removal rather than leaving it unassigned. Attach the permission record.

text.en: Name for each inventoried utility program the role permitted to run it
Set out which systems that role's permission to run the program covers
Record the circumstance that justifies a run of each program, such as a recovery, an examination or a migration
Mark for removal every program no role needs, rather than leaving the entry unassigned
Attach the permission record listing program, permitted role, systems covered and justifying circumstance

evidenceHint.en: Permission record: program, permitted role, the systems covered, and the circumstance that justifies a run

title.en: Remove or place beyond ordinary reach every listed program with no permitted user

description.en: On each system holding an entry marked for removal, take the program off; where it cannot be taken off because the platform supplies it, restrict who is able to invoke it. Where neither is possible, record the restriction standing in its place and who accepted the residual exposure. Attach the state of each affected system before and after.

text.en: Record the state of each system holding a utility program marked for removal before changing it
Take the marked program off every system where the platform allows it to be removed
Restrict who can invoke the program where the platform supplies it and it cannot be taken off
Record the compensating restriction where neither is possible, and who accepted the residual exposure
Attach the before and after state of each affected system

evidenceHint.en: Per system, the state before and after: the program removed, its invocation restricted, or the accepted compensating restriction

title.en: Record each run of a listed program with the person, the system and the reason

description.en: Capture every occasion one of the inventoried programs is used, taking it from whatever records the run — the system's own records, an operator's entry in a register, the request that authorised it — so the run is attributable to a person and a purpose rather than only to an account. Attach the record for the period.

text.en: Identify for each inventoried program what records its runs: the system's own records, an operator register or the authorising request
Collect every run of a listed privileged utility in the period from those sources
Attribute each run to the person who performed it, not only to the account it ran under

hint.en: A shared or service account name alone does not attribute a run; trace it to a named person

text.en: Record the system, the date and the stated reason against each run
Attach the record of privileged utility runs for the period

evidenceHint.en: Record for the period: program, person, system, date, and the stated reason for the run

title.en: Account for every recorded run that the permission record does not cover

description.en: Compare each run recorded in the period against the role, system and circumstance the permission record allows, and list the runs with no match. Record what investigating each one found and how it ended — the permission widened, the access withdrawn, or an incident raised. Attach the comparison.

text.en: Compare each utility run recorded in the period with the role, system and circumstance the permission record allows
List the runs that match no entry in the permission record
Investigate each unmatched run and record what the investigation found
Record how each unmatched run was resolved: the permission widened, the access withdrawn or an incident raised
Attach the comparison of recorded runs against the permission record

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of recorded runs against the permission record, listing the unmatched runs and how each was resolved

templates.title: Installation of software on operational systems
templates.objective: To ensure software reaches an operational system only through a permitted person and a recorded approval, and that whatever is found running there can be explained.
templates.successCriteria:
Each class of operational system has something that settles whether software belongs on it, with an owner named against it.
The installation rule states the permitted roles, the approval a package must carry, what is recorded and how an installation is undone.
The ability to install rests with the roles the rule permits, and systems where it could not be reduced carry a compensating measure.
Each installation of the period records the version installed, the version replaced, the installer and the approval reference.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain, per system class, what settles whether software belongs there and the accountable owner of it.
Obtain the written installation rule with its permitted roles, required approval, installation record and method of undoing an installation.
Obtain the list of who retains the ability to install software on each system class, and the systems where it could not be reduced.
Collect the period's installation record: system, software, version installed and version replaced, installer and approval reference.
Obtain the findings from the sampled operational systems, including software nothing recorded explains.

Analysis:
Check the permitted list, managed image or repository contents are current enough to settle the question for software in use today.
Compare the accounts able to install software against the roles the rule permits, taking in service and automation accounts.
Trace a sample of installations back to the approval the rule requires and to the person who carried them out.
Inventory the software present on sampled operational systems independently and compare it with the installation record.
Establish for each unexplained item how it arrived and whether the route it came by is still open.

Output:
A system-class statement of what governs software presence and who owns that determination.
A comparison of install-capable accounts against the rule's permitted roles, with the exceptions named.
A list of unexplained software found on the sampled systems and the decision taken on each.

title.en: Record what says whether a piece of software belongs on each class of operational system

description.en: For every class of system in service — a server role, a standard workstation build, an appliance — record what determines whether a piece of software belongs there: an enumerated list of permitted software with versions where the version matters, a managed image or repository whose contents can be produced on request, or the record of approvals and installations for that class. Name the person accountable for keeping it current. Attach whichever of these the organisation holds, one per class.

text.en: List the classes of operational system in service, such as server roles, standard workstation builds and appliances
Identify for each class what decides whether software belongs there: a permitted list, a managed image or repository, or the approval record

hint.en: A managed image or repository counts only if its contents can be produced on request

text.en: Include versions on any permitted software list wherever the version matters
Name the person accountable for keeping each class's software reference current
Attach the software reference held for each system class, one per class, with its owner

evidenceHint.en: Per system class, what says whether software belongs there — a permitted list, a managed image or repository contents, or the recorded approvals — with the accountable owner of each

title.en: Write down who may install software on an operational system and what must happen first

description.en: State which roles may install, what approval a package must carry before it may be installed at all, what must be recorded at the time of installing, and how the version being replaced is kept available so an installation can be undone. Where the organisation maintains a permitted list, say how an approved package reaches it; where it does not, the recorded approval stands as the authority on its own. Attach the written rule showing who approved it and when.

text.en: Name the roles permitted to install software on operational systems
State the approval a software package must carry before it may be installed at all
Specify what must be recorded at the time of each installation
Describe how the replaced version is kept available so an installation can be undone
Set out how an approved package reaches the permitted list, or state that the recorded approval is the authority where no list is kept
Attach the written installation rule showing who approved it and when

evidenceHint.en: The written installation rule naming the permitted roles, the approval a package must carry, what is recorded at installation, and how an installation is undone

title.en: Reduce the ability to install software on operational systems to the people the rule permits

description.en: Work class by class, taking the ability to install away from anyone the rule does not name. Where it cannot be taken away — a platform where operating it is inseparable from installing on it — record the system, the reason, and what stands in place of the restriction. Attach, per class, the list of who retains the ability.

text.en: List, class by class, everyone who currently holds the ability to install software on operational systems
Withdraw the ability to install from anyone the installation rule does not name
Record each system where that ability cannot be taken away, with the reason and what stands in place of the restriction

hint.en: The usual case is a platform where operating it cannot be separated from installing on it

text.en: Attach, per system class, the list of who retains the ability to install software

evidenceHint.en: Per system class, who retains the ability to install software, plus the systems where it could not be reduced and what compensates

title.en: Record every installation and version change made on an operational system this period

description.en: For each one, record the system, the software, the version put on and the version it replaced, who did it, and the approval it was carried out under. Where installing is done by hand, make the entry at the time rather than reconstructing it afterwards. Attach the installation record for the period.

text.en: Record the system, the software and the version put on for each installation or version change
Note the version each installation replaced on that system
Record who performed each installation and the approval reference it was carried out under
Enter each installation done by hand at the time it is done, rather than reconstructing it afterwards
Attach the software installation record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Installation record for the period: system, software, version installed and the version replaced, installer, and the approval reference

title.en: Account for software found on a sample of operational systems that nothing recorded explains

description.en: Take a sample spanning the system classes, list what is actually present on each, and set that against the reference state recorded for the class and the installation record. For every item neither explains, record what it is, how it arrived if that can be established, and the decision taken — removed, or approved and brought within the reference state. Attach the findings.

text.en: Select a sample of operational systems that spans every system class
List the software actually present on each sampled system
Compare each item found with the reference state recorded for its class and with the installation record
Record for every item neither explains what it is and, where it can be established, how it arrived
Decide for each unexplained item whether it is removed or approved and brought within the reference state
Attach the findings from the sampled systems with the decision on each item

evidenceHint.en: Findings from the sampled systems: the unexplained software found, what was established about it, and the decision on each

templates.title: Networks security
templates.objective: To ensure every network the organisation runs has a named owner, and that information crossing out of one carries the protection decided for that crossing.
templates.successCriteria:
Every network in operation appears on the network register with a named accountable person.
Each point where a network meets something outside the organisation's control is recorded, authorised, and carries a stated in-transit protection.
Traffic accepted without protection names the person who accepted it.
The period's findings account for what was attached to each registered network, with an outcome for items no record explained.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the network register naming, for each network, what it carries, who uses it and who is accountable for it.
Obtain the external-connection register with the purpose and authoriser of each connection.
Collect the recorded in-transit protection per connection, including traffic accepted as unprotected.
Gather the attachment findings produced for each registered network in the period.
Obtain the most recent reconfirmation of the register and the decisions it records.

Analysis:
Compare the register against the networks actually in operation and note any network with no accountable person.
Trace each external connection to its authorisation and confirm the recorded purpose still applies.
Check the protection recorded for a connection against the boundary carrying it, and that unprotected traffic names a current acceptor.
Follow attached items that no record explained through to the outcome recorded against them.
Confirm the reconfirmation covered every connection and that its decisions were acted on.

Output:
A register-to-reality comparison naming networks and connections missing from the records.
A schedule of external connections showing protection claimed against protection observed.
A list of unexplained attachments and of connections never reconfirmed, with owners.

title.en: List the networks the organisation operates and name who is accountable for each

description.en: Record every network in use — office, data centre, cloud virtual network, wireless, remote access, and any network serving visitors or equipment rather than staff — with what it carries, who uses it, and the named person accountable for it. Attach the network register with a row per network.

text.en: Identify every network in use: office, data centre, cloud virtual network, wireless, remote access, and visitor or equipment networks

hint.en: Networks serving visitors or equipment rather than staff are the ones most often left off

text.en: Record what each network carries and who uses it
Name the person accountable for each network
Attach the network register with one row per network

evidenceHint.en: Network register: network, what it carries, who uses it, and the named person accountable for it

title.en: Record every point at which a registered network meets something outside the organisation's control

description.en: For each registered network, list the links to anything the organisation does not itself run — internet access, provider circuits, partner connections, remote access into it, wireless reaching beyond the premises — with the purpose of each and the person who authorised it. A link nobody can account for is the finding this task exists to surface. Attach the external-connection register.

text.en: List for each registered network every link to something the organisation does not itself run

hint.en: Cover internet access, provider circuits, partner links, remote access in and wireless reaching off the premises

text.en: Record the purpose of each external connection
Name the person who authorised each external connection
Flag as a finding every external connection nobody can account for
Attach the external-connection register

evidenceHint.en: External-connection register: network, the connection, its purpose, and who authorised it

title.en: Record the protection required for the organisation's information as it crosses each of those connections

description.en: For every connection on the register, state what must be protected while it is in transit and to what standard, and name the traffic that crosses unprotected together with the reason it is accepted and who accepted it. Attach the register extended with the protection required per connection.

text.en: State for each connection on the external-connection register what information must be protected in transit
Record the standard of protection required for that information on each connection
Identify the traffic that crosses each connection unprotected
Record why each unprotected flow is accepted and who accepted it
Attach the external-connection register extended with the in-transit protection required

evidenceHint.en: External-connection register extended with the in-transit protection required, including traffic accepted as unprotected and who accepted it

title.en: Account for what is attached to each registered network this period

description.en: Establish what is currently present on each registered network, by whatever means that network yields, and set it against what is expected there. Record every device, service or connection found that no record explains, what it turned out to be, and whether it was removed, moved or recorded as legitimate. Attach the findings for the period.

text.en: Establish what is currently attached to each registered network by the means that network allows
Compare what was found on each network with what is expected to be there
Record each device, service or connection that no record explains, and what it turned out to be
Record whether each unexplained item was removed, moved or recorded as legitimate
Attach the findings per network for the period

evidenceHint.en: Findings per network for the period: what was found attached, the items no record explained, and the outcome for each

title.en: Reconfirm that each recorded external connection is still needed and still protected as recorded

description.en: Walk the external-connection register with the person accountable for each network: confirm the purpose still holds, that the protection actually in place is the protection recorded, and withdraw the connections no longer needed. Record the decision taken on every entry, including those removed. Attach the reconfirmation.

text.en: Walk the external-connection register with the person accountable for each network
Confirm with them that the purpose recorded for each connection still holds
Check that the protection actually in place on each connection matches the protection recorded
Withdraw the external connections that are no longer needed
Record the decision taken on every entry, including those removed, and attach the reconfirmation

evidenceHint.en: Reconfirmation of the register: per connection, whether still needed, whether the protection matches the record, and the decision taken

templates.title: Security of network services
templates.description: Address security in network service agreements
templates.objective: To ensure the security the organisation depends on from its network service providers is contracted, evidenced by the provider, and actually delivered.
templates.successCriteria:
Every network service in use is registered with its provider and the agreement that governs it.
Agreed mechanisms, service levels and management arrangements cite the clause carrying them, and services whose agreement has no such clause sit on the gap list.
Assurance held for each externally provided service states its type and the date of the latest evidence.
Shortfalls against agreed levels and provider incidents carry the provider's response.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the network service register with provider, business use and governing agreement reference.
Collect the per-service record of agreed mechanisms, levels and management arrangements with its clause citations, and the gap list.
Gather the assurance entries for externally provided services and the latest evidence each cites.
Obtain the period's service performance record with shortfalls, incidents raised and provider responses.
Obtain the comparison of agreed mechanisms against those actually in place.

Analysis:
Check each register entry against a signed agreement and identify services running without one.
Read the cited clauses to confirm they carry the mechanisms and levels recorded against them.
Judge whether the assurance held is of the type claimed and recent enough to be relied on.
Compare delivered service levels with those agreed and confirm shortfalls were raised with the provider.
Confirm mechanisms found in place match those contracted and that each difference has a named remediation owner.

Output:
A service-by-service statement of contracted terms against terms evidenced.
A list of services in use with no agreement, no security clause, or no current assurance.
A remediation schedule for services whose delivered security differs from what was agreed.

title.en: List the network services in use and the provider of each

description.en: Record every network service the organisation consumes, internally provided and externally purchased — internet access, wide-area links, DNS, VPN, cloud connectivity, wireless — with its business use, the provider, and the contract or internal service description that governs it. Attach the network service register.

text.en: Identify every network service in use, internal and purchased: internet access, wide-area links, DNS, VPN, cloud connectivity, wireless
Record the business use and the provider of each network service
Reference the contract or internal service description that governs each service
Attach the network service register

evidenceHint.en: Network service register: service, provider, business use and the governing agreement reference.

title.en: Record the security mechanisms and service levels agreed for each network service

description.en: For every service in the register, extract from its contract, service level agreement or internal service description the security mechanisms committed (authentication, encryption, filtering, resilience), the availability commitment and the management arrangements. Mark services whose agreement carries no such terms as gaps. Attach the per-service record citing the clause.

text.en: Obtain the contract, service level agreement or internal service description for each registered network service
Extract the security mechanisms each agreement commits to, such as authentication, encryption, filtering and resilience
Record the availability commitment and the management arrangements agreed for each service
Cite the clause each recorded commitment comes from
Mark as gaps the services whose agreement carries no security terms
Attach the per-service record of agreed mechanisms and service levels with the gap list

evidenceHint.en: Per-service record of agreed security mechanisms, service levels and management arrangements, citing the clause, with the gap list.

title.en: Record the assurance the organisation may obtain for each externally provided network service

description.en: For each external service, note what its agreement entitles the organisation to — audit, an assurance or certification report, service reporting — and where the most recent evidence received is filed. Mark services entitling the organisation to nothing so the exposure is visible. Attach the assurance column of the register with clause references.

text.en: Identify for each external network service what its agreement entitles the organisation to: audit, an assurance or certification report, or service reporting
Record the clause each assurance entitlement relies on
Note where the most recent assurance evidence received from each provider is filed, and its date
Mark the services that entitle the organisation to no assurance at all, so the exposure is visible
Attach the assurance column of the network service register with clause references

evidenceHint.en: Assurance entries per external service: the clause relied on, the assurance type, and the location and date of the latest evidence received.

title.en: Record delivered service levels and provider incidents for each network service in the period

description.en: Collect provider reporting or internal measurement for every service, note where delivery fell short of the agreed levels, and record any incident raised with the provider and the response given. Attach the service performance record for the period.

text.en: Collect provider reporting or internal measurement for each network service for the period
Compare delivered service levels with the agreed levels and note each shortfall
Record each incident raised with a provider and the response the provider gave
Attach the network service performance record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Service performance record for the period per network service, with shortfalls against agreed levels, incidents raised and provider responses.

title.en: Check each network service in use against its agreement for the mechanisms actually in place

description.en: Taking one service at a time, confirm the mechanisms its agreement names are configured and working — encryption enabled, filtering active, resilient path exercised — and identify services in use with no agreement at all. Attach the comparison listing findings, the service owner and the remediation owner for each.

text.en: Take each network service in turn and list the security mechanisms its agreement names
Confirm each mechanism is configured and working: encryption enabled, filtering active, resilient path exercised
Identify network services in use that have no agreement at all
Record each finding with the service owner and a named remediation owner
Attach the comparison of agreed mechanisms against those in place

evidenceHint.en: Comparison of agreed mechanisms against those in place per service, listing findings, services with no agreement, and the remediation owner.

templates.title: Segregation of networks
templates.objective: To ensure that what can pass between the organisation's network domains is confined to what was deliberately permitted, and that the confinement holds when it is tested.
templates.successCriteria:
Each network domain is listed with the systems and users it holds and the reason it is kept apart.
Every connection allowed between two domains sits on the permitted-flow list with the person who authorised it.
Each domain pair has an enforcement measure with a named maintainer, and flows found without justification have been dispositioned.
Reachability testing finds nothing crossing a boundary that the permitted-flow list does not carry.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the domain list with the systems, users and separation reason for each domain.
Obtain the permitted-flow list showing each allowed cross-domain connection and its authoriser.
Collect the boundary record naming the enforcement measure and maintainer per domain pair.
Gather the period's change record for permitted-flow rows added, amended or removed.
Obtain the reachability results, one row per source and destination attempted.

Analysis:
Check that every domain in operation is listed and that its stated reason for separation still applies.
Trace each permitted-flow row to a named authoriser and a business need still current.
Confirm the enforcement measure recorded for a domain pair exists at that boundary and has a current maintainer.
Reconcile the change record against the list to find rows added or removed with no change entry.
Compare reachability results with the permitted-flow list and follow each disagreement to its remediation.

Output:
A domain map showing separation reasons and the measure enforcing each boundary.
A list of permitted flows lacking an authoriser, a reason or an enforcing measure.
A schedule of paths found reachable that the permitted-flow list does not carry, with owners.

title.en: Record the network domains in use and why each is held apart

description.en: Work with the people who run the network to list each domain in use — grouped by trust level, by business function, or by the sensitivity of what it carries — and for each record the systems and user groups that sit in it and the reason it is kept apart from the others. Mark any system not yet assigned to a domain. Attach the dated domain list.

text.en: List each network domain in use, working with the people who run the network
Record how each domain is grouped: by trust level, by business function or by sensitivity of what it carries
Record the systems and user groups that sit in each domain
State the reason each domain is kept apart from the others
Mark any system not yet assigned to a domain
Attach the dated domain list

evidenceHint.en: The domain list: each domain, its systems and users, and the reason it is separated

title.en: Record what may pass between each pair of domains and who authorised it

description.en: Build a permitted-flow list holding one row per connection allowed to cross a domain boundary: source domain, destination domain, what the connection carries, the business reason, and the person who authorised it. State on the list that anything not held on it is not permitted, and cross-reference every row to the domain list. Attach the permitted-flow list.

text.en: Create one row for each connection allowed to cross a domain boundary
Record on each row the source domain, destination domain, what the connection carries and the business reason
Name the person who authorised each permitted cross-domain flow
State on the list that any flow not held on it is not permitted
Cross-reference every row of the permitted-flow list to the domain list
Attach the permitted-flow list

evidenceHint.en: The permitted-flow list, one row per allowed cross-domain connection with its authoriser

title.en: Record how the permitted-flow list is enforced at each boundary

description.en: For each pair of domains, record the measure that actually holds the boundary — whatever the organisation uses, from separate physical infrastructure to filtering at a shared gateway — the team that maintains it, and how a connection absent from the permitted-flow list is prevented. Remove, or raise for decision, anything found in place that no row on the list justifies. Attach the boundary record cross-referenced to the list, showing the disposal of each unjustified item.

text.en: Identify for each pair of domains the measure that actually holds the boundary, from separate infrastructure to filtering at a shared gateway
Name the team that maintains each boundary measure
Record how each boundary prevents a connection absent from the permitted-flow list
Compare what is configured at each boundary with the rows on the permitted-flow list
Remove, or raise for decision, anything in place at a boundary that no row on the list justifies
Attach the boundary record cross-referenced to the list, showing the disposal of each unjustified item

evidenceHint.en: Boundary record naming the enforcement measure and maintainer per domain pair, with unjustified items dispositioned

title.en: Record every change to what is permitted between domains

description.en: For each row added to, amended on, or removed from the permitted-flow list during the period, capture who asked for it, what changed, the reason and the date it took effect, using the record the network team already keeps rather than a second one. Attach the change record for the period.

text.en: Draw from the network team's existing change record every permitted-flow row added, amended or removed in the period

hint.en: Use the record the network team already keeps; do not start a second one

text.en: Capture for each change who asked for it, what changed and the reason
Record the date each change to a permitted flow took effect
Attach the change record for permitted flows for the period

evidenceHint.en: Change record for the period, one entry per permitted-flow row added, amended or removed

title.en: Test what can actually be reached from each domain against the permitted-flow list

description.en: From a position inside each domain, attempt to reach destinations in the other domains, covering both connections the list permits and a sample it does not, and record the observed outcome for every attempt. Raise remediation with a named owner wherever observation and list disagree. Attach the results with the disagreements and their remediation.

text.en: Choose a test position inside each network domain
Attempt from each position to reach destinations in other domains that the permitted-flow list allows
Attempt a sample of cross-domain destinations the permitted-flow list does not allow
Record the observed outcome of every reachability attempt
Raise remediation with a named owner wherever observation and the list disagree
Attach the reachability results with the disagreements and their remediation

evidenceHint.en: Reachability results, one row per source and destination attempted, with disagreements and remediation

templates.title: Web filtering
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation's position on which external web content may be reached holds for every user and device, and that access granted around it is time-bound.
templates.successCriteria:
The position table states, for each kind of restricted content, the outcome for every user and device group.
Devices the arrangement does not cover are listed as uncovered rather than assumed protected.
Affected users can reach the published route for requesting restricted content, and each request has a recorded decider.
Every access allowed through carries a scope, a reason, and an end date or revisit point that closed entries show was honoured.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the position table showing the outcome per content kind for each user and device group.
Obtain the coverage record naming the arrangement used by each group and listing covered and uncovered devices.
Collect the published request route and the evidence that affected users reach it.
Obtain the period's register of access allowed through, with scope, requester, reason, decider and end date.
Obtain the attempt sheet recording a representative site tried for each restricted kind.

Analysis:
Check that every user and device group in use appears in the position table with a stated outcome.
Compare the device inventory against the coverage record to find devices neither covered nor listed as uncovered.
Confirm the request route is reachable by the users it is meant for and that decisions came from the named decider.
Examine allowed-through entries for an end date or revisit point, and test closed entries against it.
Read the attempt sheet against the position table and identify content reachable that the table says should not be.

Output:
A coverage statement naming the groups and devices outside the filtering arrangement.
An exceptions schedule showing scope, decider and expiry for each access allowed through.
A fix list for restricted content found reachable and for exceptions past their end date.

title.en: Record which external web content must not be reachable, and by whom

description.en: For each group of users and devices — staff, contractors, shared or public-facing machines, servers — state what kinds of external site are not to be reachable, what is allowed, and how something fitting none of the stated kinds is treated. Name the person who agreed the position for each group. Attach the position table.

text.en: Identify the user and device groups to cover: staff, contractors, shared or public-facing machines, and servers
State for each group which kinds of external site must not be reachable and what is allowed
Decide how a site fitting none of the stated kinds is treated for each group

hint.en: Sites that fit no stated kind are where a filtering position most often goes unstated

text.en: Name the person who agreed the web filtering position for each group
Attach the position table, one row per kind of content with the outcome per group

evidenceHint.en: The position table: one row per kind of content showing the outcome for each user and device group

title.en: Record how the position is achieved for each group, and what it covers

description.en: For each group in the position table, record the arrangement that carries the restriction, the point at which it takes effect, and who maintains it. List the devices and connections covered by it and, separately, those that are not covered together with what is done about them. Attach the coverage record.

text.en: Record for each group in the position table the arrangement that carries the web restriction
Note the point at which each arrangement takes effect and who maintains it
List the devices and connections each filtering arrangement covers
List separately the devices and connections not covered, and what is done about each

hint.en: List uncovered devices explicitly; leaving them out reads as full coverage

text.en: Attach the web filtering coverage record

evidenceHint.en: Coverage record naming the arrangement per group and listing covered and uncovered devices

title.en: Record and publish the route by which access to restricted content is asked for and decided

description.en: Write down where such a request is raised — which may be the organisation's existing change or service route — what the requester must supply, who decides, and where the decision is recorded. Make it reachable by the people the restriction affects and attach evidence of how they reach it, whether that is the point at which access is refused, an internal page, the service route itself, or an instruction issued to the group. Attach the published text.

text.en: Name where a request for access to restricted web content is raised, which may be the existing change or service route
State what the requester must supply with the request
Name who decides each request and where the decision is recorded
Publish the route where affected people will find it: at the refusal page, on an internal page, in the service route or by instruction
Attach the published text and evidence of how affected users reach it

evidenceHint.en: The recorded request route and evidence of how the affected users reach it

title.en: Record each access allowed through the restriction, with its scope and the point at which it is revisited

description.en: Keep one register entry per access allowed through: what was allowed, for whom, the reason given, who decided, and either the date the access ends or, where the need is standing, the point at which it is to be revisited. Close entries as they end and record the outcome when a standing entry is revisited, so the register shows what is open today and on what basis. Where the restriction admits no exceptions for a group, record that rather than keeping an empty register. Attach the register for the period.

text.en: Open a register entry for each access allowed through the web restriction, naming what was allowed and for whom
Record the reason given and who decided
Set an end date for each entry or, for a standing need, the point at which it is to be revisited
Close entries as access ends and record the outcome whenever a standing entry is revisited
Record for any group whose restriction admits no exceptions that this is so, instead of keeping an empty register
Attach the register of access allowed through for the period

evidenceHint.en: Register of access allowed through for the period: scope, requester, reason, decider, and an end date or stated revisit point, with closed and revisited entries shown

title.en: Attempt a representative site from each restricted kind and record what happened

description.en: From a device in each covered group, try to reach one representative site for every kind of content the position table says must not be reachable, and record the outcome of each attempt. Raise a fix, with an owner, wherever access succeeded that should not have. Attach the attempt sheet.

text.en: Choose one representative site for every kind of content the position table says must not be reachable
Attempt each representative site from a device in every covered group
Record the site, kind, user group and observed outcome of each attempt
Raise a fix with an owner wherever a site was reached that should have been blocked
Attach the attempt sheet with the fixes raised

evidenceHint.en: Attempt sheet: site, kind, user group and observed outcome, with fixes raised

templates.title: Use of cryptography
templates.objective: To ensure cryptography is used only with algorithms and key strengths the organisation has approved, and that every key it relies on is accounted for to its destruction.
templates.successCriteria:
Every system and application using cryptography appears in the inventory with its algorithm and purpose.
Each recorded use runs on an algorithm and key length the cryptographic standard approves for that use case.
Each key in the register has a custodian, a rotation interval and a stated destruction method.
Generation, rotation, revocation and destruction events in the period each appear in the key-management log.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the cryptography inventory listing system, algorithm and purpose for every use.
Obtain the cryptographic standard showing approved algorithms and minimum key lengths per use case.
Obtain the key register with generation, custody, rotation interval and destruction method for each key.
