Collect the key-management log for the period covering generation, rotation, revocation and destruction.
Obtain the latest reconciliation of the key register against the inventory.

Analysis:
Compare each inventory entry with the standard and list uses running below the approved algorithm or key length.
Check that registered keys have a named custodian and that their rotation intervals have been met.
Trace a sample of log entries to the register row each should have changed.
Identify keys in use the register does not carry, and register rows for keys no system uses.
Confirm destruction entries record the method the register states and that the key is no longer accepted.

Output:
A conformance table of cryptographic uses against approved algorithms and key lengths.
A list of keys past their rotation interval or holding no custodian.
A reconciliation of inventory against key register, with each discrepancy and its resolution.

title.en: Inventory every system and application using cryptography

description.en: Walk the system inventory with the teams that run each system and record where cryptography is used — data at rest, data in transit, signing, tokens — naming the system, the algorithm and the purpose of each use.

text.en: Walk the system inventory with the team that runs each system
Identify where each system uses cryptography: data at rest, data in transit, signing and tokens
Record the algorithm and purpose of each cryptographic use against its system
Compile the cryptography inventory listing system, algorithm and purpose for every use

evidenceHint.en: The cryptography inventory, listing system, algorithm and purpose for every use.

title.en: Record the approved algorithms and minimum key lengths for each use

description.en: For each use case in the inventory (transport, storage, signing, hashing, password storage), write down which algorithms are approved, the minimum key length or parameter set, and which are no longer permitted.

text.en: Group the inventoried uses by use case: transport, storage, signing, hashing and password storage
Record the approved algorithms for each cryptographic use case
Set the minimum key length or parameter set for each approved algorithm
List the algorithms that are no longer permitted for each use case

evidenceHint.en: The cryptographic standard, showing approved algorithm and minimum key length per use case.

title.en: Record how each key is generated, distributed, rotated and destroyed

description.en: Build a key register with one row per key or key set, covering where it is generated, who holds it, how it reaches the systems that need it, its rotation interval, and how it is destroyed at end of life.

text.en: Create a key register row for each key or key set the organisation relies on
Record where each key is generated and who holds it
Describe how each key reaches the systems that need it
Set the rotation interval for each key
Record how each key is destroyed at end of life

evidenceHint.en: The key register, one row per key with generation, custody, rotation interval and destruction method.

title.en: Log every key generation, rotation, revocation and destruction

description.en: Capture each key lifecycle event as it happens — which key, which event, who performed it and when — so that what the register claims can be proven against real activity.

text.en: Capture each key generation, rotation, revocation and destruction as it happens
Record for each lifecycle event which key, which event, who performed it and when
Reference each logged event to its key register row so the register can be proven against activity
Retain the key-management log for the period

evidenceHint.en: The key-management log for the period, one entry per lifecycle event.

title.en: Reconcile the key register against the cryptography inventory

description.en: Compare the register with the systems inventory, listing keys in live use that have no register row and register rows for keys no longer in use, and record how each discrepancy was resolved.

text.en: Compare the key register with the cryptography inventory and the systems listed in it
List the keys in live use that have no key register row
List the key register rows for keys no longer in use
Record how each discrepancy between register and inventory was resolved

evidenceHint.en: The reconciliation, with every discrepancy found and its resolution.

templates.title: Secure development life cycle
templates.objective: To ensure every kind of development the organisation performs runs through defined stages, each leaving a security output that a named person confirms.
templates.successCriteria:
Each kind of development work performed is named in scope or carries a recorded reason for its exclusion.
Every lifecycle stage states the security output it must produce and where that output is held.
Each stage names the person who confirms its completion, and a stage not performed carries a waiver from the authority the route names.
Release records for the period show the stages completed and the outputs produced for each product released.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope statement naming each kind of development work, who performs it and the reason for any exclusion.
Obtain the lifecycle definition listing each stage, its required security output and where that output is held.
Obtain the accountability list naming who confirms each stage, and the waiver route with the authority it names.
Collect the release records for products released in the period, with stages, outputs and waivers.
Obtain the sampled stage-by-stage review of completed development work.

Analysis:
Compare development actually performed in the period, contractor work included, against the scope statement.
Retrieve the security output named for each stage of a sampled release and confirm it exists where the definition says.
Check that stage confirmations came from the accountable person rather than the author of the work.
Examine each waiver for the authority the route names and a reason recorded at the time.
Follow missing outputs from the sampled review to a named owner and a remediation date.

Output:
A scope comparison naming development work performed outside the lifecycle.
A stage completion matrix per released product with the location of each security output.
A waiver schedule beside the stages recorded complete with no output behind them.

title.en: Record the development work the lifecycle governs and who performs each kind

description.en: State the kinds of work in scope — new systems, changes to systems already in use, configuration of software the organisation acquired, and work carried out by suppliers on its behalf — and who performs each. Mark anything deliberately outside the lifecycle together with the reason it is excluded. Attach the scope statement.

text.en: List the kinds of development in scope: new systems, changes to live systems, configuration of acquired software, and supplier work
Name who performs each kind of development work
Mark any work deliberately outside the lifecycle and the reason it is excluded
Attach the lifecycle scope statement

evidenceHint.en: Scope statement naming each kind of development work, who performs it, and the reason for any exclusion

title.en: Write the lifecycle stages and the security output each stage must produce

description.en: Set out the stages a piece of development passes through and, for each, the security output that must exist before the stage is complete and where that output is held. Name the outputs as deliverables rather than as tools, so a team working on paper and a team working in a toolchain can both satisfy them. Attach the lifecycle definition.

text.en: Set out the stages a piece of development passes through
Name for each stage the security output that must exist before the stage is complete
Record where each stage's security output is held
Phrase each output as a deliverable, not a tool, so paper-based and toolchain teams can both satisfy it
Attach the lifecycle definition

evidenceHint.en: The lifecycle definition: each stage, the security output required, and where that output is held

title.en: Record who confirms each stage is complete and how a stage may be waived

description.en: Name the person or role accountable for confirming each stage's output exists before the next stage begins, then write down the authority needed to waive a stage, what must be recorded when one is waived, and how long a waiver stands. Attach the accountability list and the written waiver route.

text.en: Name the person or role who confirms each stage's output exists before the next stage begins
Record the authority needed to waive a lifecycle stage
State what must be recorded when a stage is waived and how long a waiver stands
Attach the stage accountability list and the written waiver route

evidenceHint.en: Accountability list per stage plus the written waiver route and the authority it names

title.en: Record the lifecycle stages completed for each product released this period

description.en: For every release in the period, capture which stages were completed, where each stage's output is held, and any stage waived with the authority for it, inside the release record the team already produces. Attach the release records for the period.

text.en: List every product release made in the period
Capture in each release record the lifecycle stages completed and where each stage's output is held

hint.en: Use the release record the team already produces, not a separate form

text.en: Record any stage waived for a release and the authority it was waived under
Attach the release records for the period

evidenceHint.en: Release records for the period, each naming the stages completed, their outputs and any waiver

title.en: Sample completed development work and check it stage by stage against the lifecycle

description.en: Take a sample of work finished in the period, walk each item through the lifecycle definition, and record for every stage whether the required output exists. Raise each missing output with the person named for that stage on the accountability list. Attach the review with its gaps and owners.

text.en: Select a sample of development work finished in the period
Walk each sampled item through the lifecycle definition stage by stage
Record for every stage whether the required security output exists
Raise each missing output with the person named for that stage on the accountability list
Attach the lifecycle review with its gaps and owners

evidenceHint.en: The sampled review, one row per item and stage, with missing outputs and their owners

templates.title: Application security requirements
templates.description: Identify and address application security needs
templates.objective: To ensure each application the organisation builds, buys or specifies is held to security requirements that fit the information it handles and how far it can be reached.
templates.successCriteria:
Every application is listed with its owner, the information it handles, its reachability and a requirement-set decision.
The standing requirements every application must meet are approved and dated by a named approver.
Each application decided to need one has its own requirement set, linked to its entry on the application list.
Applications acquired or newly specified in the period record the requirements set, who agreed them and the evidence offered.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the application list with owner, information handled, reachability and requirement-set decision per entry.
Obtain the approved standing security requirement set with its approver and date.
Collect the per-application requirement sets for the applications decided to need one.
Obtain the records for applications acquired or newly specified in the period.
Obtain the revised standing requirement set and the list of applications to be brought up to it.

Analysis:
Compare the application list with the systems actually in use and find applications with no entry or no decision.
Check that an in-scope application's requirement set addresses what its list entry says it handles and how it is reached.
Confirm the standing requirements were approved by someone holding authority to approve them.
For acquisitions, check requirements were set before agreement and that the evidence offered was assessed, not merely received.
Test whether applications named for uplift against the revised standing set carry owners and dates.

Output:
An application inventory marking which entries hold a requirement set and which do not.
A traceability table from each standing requirement to the application sets carrying it.
An uplift schedule for applications sitting below the current standing requirements.

title.en: List the applications needing a security requirement set, with what each handles

description.en: Record the applications the organisation builds, buys or subscribes to, noting for each the owner, the information it handles, who can reach it, and whether it exchanges information across networks the organisation does not control. Mark which of them need a documented security requirement set. Attach the application list.

text.en: List the applications the organisation builds, buys or subscribes to, with the owner of each
Record the information each application handles and who can reach it
Note whether each application exchanges information across networks the organisation does not control
Mark which applications need a documented security requirement set
Attach the application list

evidenceHint.en: Application list with owner, information handled, reachability, and the requirement-set decision per entry

title.en: Write the standing security requirements every application must meet

description.en: State as requirements, not as products, what any application must do: how it establishes who a user is and what they may do, how it handles information held and in transit, what it records about significant actions, how it behaves on invalid input and on failure, and what integrity a transaction it carries must retain. Attach the approved standing requirement set with its approver and date.

text.en: State how any application must establish who a user is and what they may do

hint.en: Express each as a requirement on the application, not as a product to buy

text.en: State how an application must handle information it holds and information in transit
Specify what an application must record about significant actions
Define how an application must behave on invalid input and on failure
Set the integrity a transaction carried by an application must retain
Obtain approval of the standing requirement set and attach it with its approver and date

evidenceHint.en: The approved standing security requirement set, with approver and date

title.en: Derive and record the security requirements for each application in scope

description.en: For every application marked in scope, record which standing requirements apply, which do not and why, and what further requirements its information and reachability demand. Hold the result where the delivery or procurement work for that application is already tracked, linked to its list entry. Attach the requirement set for each in-scope application.

text.en: Record for each application marked in scope which standing security requirements apply
Record which standing requirements do not apply to the application and why
Add the further requirements the application's information and reachability demand
Hold the result where the application's delivery or procurement work is already tracked, linked to its list entry
Attach the security requirement set for each in-scope application

evidenceHint.en: Per-application requirement sets, each linked to its application list entry

title.en: Record the security requirements set for each application acquired or newly specified

description.en: As each application is specified or bought in the period, capture the security requirements it was required to meet, who agreed them with the business owner, and what was offered as evidence that the application meets them. Attach the record for each acquisition or specification in the period.

text.en: Capture, as each application is specified or bought, the security requirements it was required to meet
Record who agreed those requirements with the business owner
Record what was offered as evidence that the application meets those requirements
Attach the record for each application acquisition or specification in the period

evidenceHint.en: Per-acquisition record naming the requirements set, who agreed them, and the evidence offered

title.en: Re-examine the standing requirements against what has changed

description.en: Review the standing requirement set against new obligations, new kinds of exposure, and the defects and incidents seen since it was written, recording what was added, amended or dropped and why. templates.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
templates.objective: To ensure system designs are shaped by engineering principles the organisation agreed, so that departing from one is a decision somebody took rather than an oversight.
templates.successCriteria:
The principles are written down with the meaning each carries in this organisation, and are approved.
One real design is annotated to show which principle each part satisfies, proving the principles can be applied.
Every system designed or substantially redesigned in the period holds an examination record naming the principles checked.
Departures are accepted by the authority the arrangement names, and principles departed from repeatedly are revisited.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved principles document with the meaning recorded against each principle.
Obtain the annotated worked example showing which principle each part of that design satisfies.
Obtain the examination arrangement, including when a design is examined and how a departure is authorised.
Collect the completed examination records for systems designed or substantially redesigned in the period.
Obtain the comparison of the period's designs and redesigns against the examinations held.

Analysis:
Read the principles for wording specific enough that a design can be judged against them.
Check the worked example maps parts of a live design to principles rather than restating the principles.
List the systems designed or redesigned in the period and identify those never examined.
Examine accepted departures for the authority the arrangement names and a rationale recorded with the acceptance.
Test whether the conclusion drawn about repeatedly departed principles was carried back into the principles.

Output:
An examination register naming the designs covered and the designs missed.
A departure schedule showing the principle, the acceptor and the reason accepted.
A judgement on whether the principles as written can be applied to a design at all.

title.en: Write down the engineering principles systems are designed to

description.en: Agree the principles the organisation designs to and give each one line saying what it means for our systems rather than in the abstract. Record who approved the set and when. Attach the principles document.

text.en: Agree the secure engineering principles the organisation designs systems to
Write one line per principle saying what it means for the organisation's own systems
Record who approved the set of principles and when
Attach the principles document

evidenceHint.en: The approved principles document, one entry per principle with its meaning here

title.en: Record how the principles are met in one existing design, as the worked example

text.en: Choose one system the organisation runs to serve as the worked example

hint.en: Showing unmet principles is the point; omitting them makes the example misleading

text.en: Attach the annotated design as the example other designs are shaped against

evidenceHint.en: The annotated design of one real system showing which principle each part satisfies

templates.title: Secure coding
templates.objective: To ensure code accepted into the organisation's systems was written against rules suited to its language and confirmed against those rules before acceptance.
templates.successCriteria:
Every language and framework in use cites the coding rules that apply to it, or is flagged as having none.
The secure coding rules sit where the developers writing the code can reach them.
Each rule names the person or automated check that confirms it, and rules with neither are shown as unchecked.
Acceptance records for the period show which rule confirmations were completed for each change and who completed them.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the language and framework list with the coding rules cited or the gap flagged per row.
Obtain the published secure coding rules and the evidence of where developers reach them.
Obtain the rule-to-check map naming the confirming person or check for every rule.
Collect the acceptance records for changes accepted in the period with their rule confirmations.
Obtain the manual sample review of accepted code read against the rules.

Analysis:
Compare the language and framework list against the repositories in use and find stacks citing no rules.
Check the rules are reachable by developers in practice, not merely published somewhere.
Identify the rules the map leaves unchecked and whether the exposure that creates is stated anywhere.
Sample accepted changes and confirm each confirmation came from the named check or from someone other than the change's author.
Read the manual review findings against the rule cited and follow each breach to the fix raised.

Output:
A rules coverage table by language and framework.
A list of coding rules with no confirming person and no automated check.
A findings list of code accepted in breach of a rule, with the confirmation recorded and the fix raised.

title.en: List the languages, frameworks and code in use and the coding rules that apply to each

description.en: Record every language and framework the organisation writes in, including scripts and infrastructure definitions, and name the secure coding rules that apply to each. Flag any for which no rules have been chosen yet. Attach the list with the rules cited or the gap flagged per row.

text.en: List every language and framework the organisation writes in, including scripts and infrastructure definitions
Name the secure coding rules that apply to each language and framework

evidenceHint.en: The language and framework list, each row citing its coding rules or flagging the gap

text.en: Add rules for error and failure behaviour

Where a confirmation is a test that already sits on the organisation's security testing schedule, name it by reference rather than restating what it does or when it runs. Where a rule has no check at all, record it as unchecked rather than leaving it unstated. Attach the rule-to-check map.

Attach the acceptance records for the period.

templates.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
templates.description: Test security during development and acceptance
templates.objective: To ensure no change is put into use before the security testing its kind demands has been run and the result it produced has been judged good enough to accept.
templates.successCriteria:
Each kind of change is matched to the security tests it must pass and what those tests cover.
Every test states the result a change must reach to be accepted and names who may accept a shortfall.
Changes accepted in the period have the test results that supported the decision filed against them.
Every finding the testing raised carries a disposition, the person who decided it, and an owner.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the test schedule showing each test, what it covers and the kinds of change that must pass it.
Obtain the acceptance criteria per test and the authority named for accepting a shortfall.
Collect the test results filed against changes accepted in the period.
Obtain the findings record carrying a disposition, decider and owner per finding.
Obtain the sample review of changes put into use during the period.

Analysis:
Check that every kind of change made in the period maps to at least one required test.
Take a sample of accepted changes and confirm the filed results belong to that change and predate its acceptance.
Compare each filed result against the acceptance criterion for that test and isolate the shortfalls.
Confirm accepted shortfalls were accepted by the named authority rather than by the team delivering the change.
Follow open findings to an owner, and judge whether dispositions of no action are reasoned.

Output:
A coverage matrix of change kinds against the tests required of them.
An acceptance sample showing results held, results missing and results dated after release.
A shortfall schedule naming the acceptor behind each accepted failure, beside the open findings and their age.

title.en: Record the security tests each kind of change must pass and what each covers

text.en: List the security tests in use across development and acceptance

Record which kinds of change must pass each test before being accepted

templates.title: Outsourced development
templates.objective: To ensure development performed by suppliers carries security requirements the organisation can enforce, and that each deliverable is examined before it is trusted.
templates.successCriteria:
Every supplier performing development is registered with its scope of work and the systems that work touches.
Each development contract carries the security requirement set through identified clauses.
Supplier-written code passes the intake procedure's review and testing gates before it reaches the codebase.
Each deliverable holds an acceptance review and test record, with the findings raised against the supplier.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of suppliers performing development, with scope of work and systems touched.
Obtain the security requirement set for development contracts and the clauses that carry it.
Obtain the intake procedure for supplier-written code and the gates it places before merge.
Collect the acceptance review and test records for deliverables received in the period.
Obtain the per-supplier assessments against contracted security requirements.

Analysis:
Compare the supplier register against procurement and repository records to find development done by unregistered suppliers.
Read the cited clauses to confirm they impose the requirement set rather than referring to it loosely.
Trace a sample of merged supplier commits back through the intake gates and identify code merged without them.
Check deliverables were tested for security defects before acceptance and that findings went back to the supplier.
Review each supplier assessment for gaps and confirm every gap carries remediation and a date.

Output:
A register comparison naming development suppliers outside the register or without contracted requirements.
An intake exception list of supplier code merged without the required gates.
A supplier assessment summary with gaps, remediation owners and dates.

templates.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
templates.objective: To ensure development and test work can neither reach nor disturb live operation, and that anything moving between environments moves by a chosen route.
templates.successCriteria:
Each system's environments are listed with purpose, hosting and owner, marking those that hold live-derived information.
Every environment has a recorded measure holding it apart from live operation and a team maintaining it.
Access in an environment matches its role statement, and anything spanning environments sits on the register with a reason, grantor and end date.
Verification confirms a development or test environment cannot reach live information.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the environment list showing system, purpose, hosting, owner and whether it holds live-derived information.
Obtain the separation record naming the measure and maintaining team per environment.
Obtain the per-environment role statement, the access list showing it applied, and the cross-environment register.
Obtain the written route by which code and configuration reach live operation.
Obtain the verification record of attempts made to reach live information from development or test.

Analysis:
Check the environment list against hosting and billing records to find environments nobody declared.
Test whether environments holding live-derived information carry the protection live operation itself carries.
Compare the access list in each environment against its role statement and isolate rights beyond it.
Trace a sample of releases to confirm they moved in the permitted direction and met the stated preconditions.
Examine cross-environment entries for an end date already passed with the access still in place.

Output:
An environment inventory marking those holding live-derived information and the measure separating each.
An access comparison of rights held against rights the role statement allows.
A list of live-information paths reachable from development or test, with the remediation raised.

templates.title: Change management
templates.description: Manage changes to information processing facilities
templates.objective: To ensure a change to information processing facilities is assessed, approved and reversible before it is made, and that an emergency change is answerable afterwards.
templates.successCriteria:
The scope definition names which classes of change must take the change route and which need not.
A change record cannot be completed without an impact assessment and a back-out plan.
Each change in the period's register carries its assessment, approver, test result and outcome.
Changes made outside the normal route appear in the emergency log with approval recorded after the fact.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scope definition naming the change classes inside and outside the change procedure.
Obtain the change procedure covering request, assessment, approval, testing and back-out.
Obtain the change record template or tool configuration showing the mandatory assessment and back-out fields.
Collect the period's change register with assessment, approver, test result and outcome per change, and the emergency log.
Obtain the sample review of production changes against their approval times.

Analysis:
Compare changes visible in production systems with the register to find changes that never entered the route.
Attempt a change record without an impact assessment or back-out plan and observe whether the tool accepts it.
For a sample of register entries, confirm the approval time precedes the implementation time.
Check the approver was someone other than the implementer and held authority over that class of change.
Examine emergency entries for a retrospective approval and judge whether the emergency justification holds.

Output:
A register completeness comparison against the changes observed in production.
A field enforcement result showing whether the mandatory fields can be bypassed.
An approval timing schedule of changes implemented before approval, with the emergency entries beside it.

title.en: Define which changes to information processing facilities require the change route

title.en: Record the change procedure from request through approval to back-out

evidenceHint.en: Change procedure document covering request, assessment, approval, testing and back-out

evidenceHint.en: Change register for the period, one row per change with assessment, approver, test result and outcome

title.en: Record the retrospective approval for every change made outside the normal route

description.en: Where a change had to be made urgently, capture what was done, who authorised it at the time, and the approval recorded afterwards. Attach the emergency change log for the period.

text.en: Identify every change in the period that was made urgently outside the normal route
Capture what was done and who authorised it at the time
Obtain and record the retrospective approval for each emergency change
Attach the emergency change log for the period

evidenceHint.en: Emergency change log with the after-the-fact approval recorded against each entry

title.en: Sample production changes and confirm approval preceded implementation

description.en: Take a sample of changes from the register and check that the recorded approval carries a date before the implementation date, listing any that do not. Attach the sample review with the exceptions found.

text.en: Select a sample of production changes from the change register
Compare each sampled change's recorded approval date with its implementation date
List every change whose approval does not predate its implementation
Attach the sample review with the exceptions found

evidenceHint.en: Sample review listing changes checked and any implemented without prior approval

templates.title: Test information
templates.objective: To ensure information used for testing is authorised before it is copied, protected while it is held, and removed once the testing no longer needs it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every testing activity has a recorded information need, and each one using live-derived records states why invented information will not serve.
Each dataset held for testing is registered with its origin, its protection, its named authoriser and a removal date.
Copies taken in the period were authorised on the written terms before the copy was made.
Nothing sits in a testing environment unregistered or past its removal date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the needs list and mark which testing activities are recorded as requiring live-derived information.
Obtain the authorisation terms, noting the authorising role, the holding limits and the end-of-use action.
Obtain the test information register and take from it the full population of datasets held.
Obtain the copy record for the period and the removal record for entries that fell due in it.
List the datasets actually present in each environment named on the needs list.

Analysis:
Trace each copy made in the period to an authorisation by the named role, dated before the copy.
Check each register row carries the protection the terms require for that origin and a removal date inside the holding limit.
Reconcile the environment listing against the register both ways, separating unregistered datasets from registered ones no longer present.
Confirm entries past their removal date appear in the removal record with a location and a person, then re-check the environment.
Weigh each stated reason for live-derived information against what the testing activity actually needs.

Output:
A population of test datasets held, each marked registered, unregistered or overdue.
A copy trace giving the authoriser and authorisation date behind every copy made in the period.
An exception list naming unauthorised, overdue and unaccounted-for test information against its owner.

title.en: Record what information each testing activity needs and where it comes from

description.en: List the testing activities carried out and, for each, the information it needs, whether that information can be made up or must be derived from live records, and the reason live-derived information is necessary. Attach the needs list.

text.en: List the testing activities the organisation carries out
Record the information each testing activity needs and its source
Decide for each whether the information can be made up or must be derived from live records
Record the reason wherever live-derived information is necessary
Attach the test information needs list

evidenceHint.en: Needs list: testing activity, information required, source, and the reason live-derived information is needed

title.en: Record who authorises live-derived information for testing and on what terms

description.en: Write down who may authorise a copy of live-derived information for testing, what must be done to it before it is used, where it may be held, how long it may be kept, and what happens to it when that period ends. Attach the written terms naming the authorising role.

text.en: Name the role that may authorise a copy of live-derived information for testing
State what must be done to the information before it is used in testing
Set where live-derived test information may be held and how long it may be kept
State what happens to the information when its holding period ends
Attach the written authorisation terms naming the authorising role

evidenceHint.en: Written authorisation terms naming the authorising role, the holding limits and the end-of-use action

title.en: Record every test dataset already held, its origin and its removal date

description.en: Go through the environments in use and record each dataset held for testing: where it came from, whether it derives from live records, what protection it carries, who authorised it, and when it is due to be removed. Mark any dataset found with no authorisation behind it. Attach the test information register.

text.en: Inspect each environment in use and identify every dataset held for testing
Record each dataset's origin and whether it derives from live records
Record the protection each dataset carries and who authorised it
Record the date each test dataset is due to be removed
Mark any dataset found with no authorisation behind it
Attach the test information register

evidenceHint.en: Test information register, one row per dataset with origin, protection, authoriser and removal date

title.en: Record each live-derived copy taken for testing this period

description.en: For every copy made in the period, record the source, the destination environment, what was done to the information before it was used, who authorised it, and the date it falls due for removal, adding the row to the test information register. Attach the copy record for the period.

text.en: Record for every live-derived copy taken in the period its source and its destination environment
Note what was done to the information before it was used
Record who authorised the copy and the date it falls due for removal
Add each copy as a row on the test information register
Attach the test data copy record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Copy record for the period, one row per copy with source, destination, authoriser and removal date

title.en: Remove the test information whose authorised holding period has ended

description.en: Work the register for entries past their removal date, remove or return the information wherever it is held, and record what was removed, from where and by whom, closing the register entry as you go. Attach the removal record for the period.

text.en: Search the test information register for entries past their removal date
Remove or return that information wherever it is held
Record what was removed, from where and by whom
Close each register entry as its information is removed

hint.en: Close the entry only once every copy is gone, not just the first location found

text.en: Attach the test information removal record for the period

evidenceHint.en: Removal record for the period naming each dataset removed, its location and who removed it

title.en: Compare the test information actually held against the register

description.en: Inspect the environments on the list and compare what is held there with the register, reporting anything held that the register does not show, anything past its removal date, and anything held with no authorisation behind it. Raise each with a named owner. Attach the comparison with its findings.

text.en: Inspect each environment on the environment list for test information held there
Compare what is held in each environment with the test information register
Report anything held that the register does not show, anything past its removal date and anything with no authorisation
Raise each finding with a named owner
Attach the comparison with its findings

evidenceHint.en: Comparison record listing unregistered, overdue and unauthorised test information with owners

templates.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
templates.objective: To ensure testing carried out for audit purposes stays inside limits the system owner accepted, and leaves the systems it examines operational and unaltered.
templates.successCriteria:
No audit test begins before its window, permitted actions and stop authority are accepted by the owner of every system it reaches.
Access used by participants carries a stated basis and an end time, and none outlives the window.
What was done on each system during the window can be reconstructed afterwards from what was retained.
Systems in scope are confirmed back as they were, with accounts, settings, files and jobs left by the test removed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Take the audit tests run in the period and obtain the scope record written for each before it ran.
Obtain the owner agreement for each test: window, permitted and prohibited actions, stop authority and named contact.
Obtain the access record listing each participant and tool, the basis of the access and when it was to end.
Obtain the activity account retained for each system in scope over its window.
Obtain the withdrawal record and the post-test check record produced at the close of each test.

Analysis:
Compare the systems and actions the scope record anticipated with those the agreement permits, and both with the activity account.
Check each agreement carries the system owner's acceptance dated before the window opened.
Confirm each access was withdrawn at or before its stated end, including access raised in passing during the test.
Read the activity account for actions outside the permitted set or the agreed hours, and follow each to the stop authority named for that test.
Confirm the post-test check covers every system the scope record named and that residue found was restored or left open with an owner.

Output:
A per-test comparison of scope anticipated, actions permitted and activity carried out.
An access ledger giving the basis and withdrawal date of every access used for audit testing.
A schedule of systems checked after each test showing residue found, restored or outstanding.

title.en: Record the systems, information and actions each planned audit test will reach

description.en: Before the test begins, and with the person who will carry it out, record which systems it will reach, what information it will see, what it will do to them, and the load or interruption the system owner states those systems can bear. Attach the scope record for the planned test.

text.en: Agree the scope with the person who will carry out the audit test, before the test begins
Record which systems the audit test will reach and what information it will see
Record what the test will do to each system in scope
Obtain from the system owner the load or interruption those systems can bear
Attach the scope record for the planned audit test

evidenceHint.en: Per-test scope record naming systems, information reached, intended actions and the owner's stated constraints

title.en: Agree the window, the permitted actions and the limits with each system owner

description.en: Settle with the owner of each system in scope when the test may run, what may be done, what must not be done, who to contact if service is affected, and who may stop the test. Have both the person carrying out the test and the system owner accept it before anything begins. Attach the accepted agreement.

text.en: Settle with the owner of each system in scope when the audit test may run
Agree what the test may do and what it must not do
Name the contact if service is affected and the person who may stop the test
Obtain acceptance from both the tester and the system owner before anything begins
Attach the accepted audit test agreement

evidenceHint.en: Agreement naming window, permitted actions, prohibitions, stop authority and contact, accepted by both parties

title.en: Record the access the test needs, on what basis it is granted and when it ends

description.en: For each person or tool taking part, record what access will be used — access already held, access granted for this test, or supervised access alongside a member of staff — what that access permits, and the date and time it ends. Attach the access record.

text.en: List each person or tool taking part in the audit test
Record whether each uses access already held, access granted for this test, or supervised access alongside staff
Record what each access permits on the systems in scope
Set the date and time each access ends
Attach the audit test access record

evidenceHint.en: Access record per participant showing what access is used, what it permits, and when it ends

title.en: Capture what was done on each system during the window

description.en: Retain, against the test record, an account of the activity carried out on each system in scope during the agreed window, sufficient to reconstruct it afterwards — whatever the organisation can produce, from the systems' own activity records to a step log kept by the participant and countersigned by an observer. Attach it to the test record.

text.en: Identify what the organisation can produce to account for activity on each system, from its own activity records to a step log
Retain the activity account for each system in scope across the agreed window
Have an observer countersign any step log kept by the participant
Check the account is sufficient to reconstruct what was done afterwards
Attach the activity account to the audit test record

evidenceHint.en: The activity account covering the audit window, filed against the test record

title.en: Withdraw the access used for the test when the window closes

description.en: At the end of the window, withdraw or return each access on the access record, including anything raised in passing during the test, and record what was withdrawn and the date. Attach the withdrawal record.

text.en: Withdraw or return each access on the access record when the audit window closes
Identify any access raised in passing during the test and withdraw it too

hint.en: Access raised in passing is the kind most often missed, as it is not on the original record

text.en: Record what was withdrawn and the date
Attach the access withdrawal record

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal record showing each access withdrawn and the date it was withdrawn

title.en: Check each system touched for anything the test left behind

description.en: After the window closes, check the systems in scope for accounts, changed settings, files, jobs or residual load left by the test, and confirm each is back as it was. Record what was checked, what was found and what was restored, raising anything outstanding with the system owner. Attach the post-test check record.

text.en: Check each system in scope after the window closes for accounts, changed settings, files or jobs the test left behind
Check each system for residual load left by the test
Restore each item found to how it was before the test and record what was restored
Raise anything outstanding with the system owner
Attach the post-test check record listing systems checked, residue found and what was restored

evidenceHint.en: Post-test check record listing systems checked, residue found and what was restored
